npc:abercrombie.text: Abercrombie. Abercrombie appears to be a feeble, eccentric hermit dwelling in a dilapidated shack in western Duskwood near Raven Hill Cemetery. Claiming to be a harmless recluse plagued by the horrors of the woods, he readily enlists sympathetic travelers to gather peculiar reagents and supplies on his behalf. Tucked away in the rotting shadows near Raven Hill Cemetery, Abercrombie cuts a pathetic figure. He presents himself as an old man merely trying to survive the terrors of Duskwood, asking travelers to run modest errands into Darkshire for supplies, herbs, and thread. To those unfamiliar with the history of the region, he seems like just another unfortunate soul left behind as the province fell into decay.

npc:alanndarian-nightsong.text: Alanndarian Nightsong. Alanndarian Nightsong is a night elf resident of Auberdine in Darkshore dedicated to tending to the region's beleaguered fauna. She works alongside travelers to remedy the blights plaguing the local wildlife, particularly the region's deer, sickened by poison in Darkshore's waters. Situated in the coastal settlement of Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong watches over the fragile ecological balance of Darkshore. As mysterious taints seep into the soil and waters, the creatures of the ancient woods have begun to succumb to sickness and unnatural aggression. Alanndarian acts as a guardian and naturalist, seeking practical remedies to ease their suffering and restore their natural vigor. Much of Alanndarian's attention is focused on identifying the root causes of the afflictions spreading through the local fauna. Through careful gathering of botanical reagents and researching the principal water sources of the region, she crafts salves and curative draughts. She enlists wandering adventurers to apply these cures directly to ailing forest creatures, attempting to stave off the spreading corruption before it permanently overtakes Darkshore's wildlife.

npc:althea-ebonlocke.text: Althea Ebonlocke. Commander Althea Ebonlocke leads the Night Watch, the beleaguered town guard protecting Darkshire from the terrors of Duskwood. A relative of Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, she shoulders the defense of an isolated region abandoned by Stormwind's regular military. She organizes patrols, tasks adventurers with culling local horrors, and coordinates the town's survival against constant monstrous threats. While her relative, Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, handles civil governance within the town hall, Commander Althea directs Darkshire's thin line of physical defense. When Stormwind failed to deploy royal troops to guard Duskwood against creeping horrors, the citizenry formed the Night Watch. Under Althea's steady, unyielding command, these volunteers patrol the fog-shrouded roads, keeping skeletal undead, ferocious wolves, and spiders from overrunning the town perimeter. Althea is pragmatic and understands the limits of her militia. Outnumbered and continually bleeding recruits, she freely enlists passing mercenaries and travelers to thin the threats at Darkshire's doorstep. She directs campaigns against the ghouls and skeletons at the tranquil and sorrowful graveyards of the forest, while remaining vigilant against darker rumors stirring deep in the woods.

npc:asterion.text: Asterion. Asterion is an ancient Highborne spirit bound to the ruins of Bashal'Aran in Darkshore. Once the trusted second to governor Athrikus Narassin ten millennia ago, he was mysteriously imprisoned in a magical moonstone seal that held him through mortal life and into the afterlife. Today, his specter remains shackled to the ruined shrine, surrounded by demonic beasts and dreaming of liberation. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran were sister cities blessed by Queen Azshara herself. Azshara appointed Athrikus Narassin to govern the twin settlements, and Asterion served as his right hand. Respected for both his physical combat prowess and his command of arcane sorcery, Asterion lived among the people of Bashal'Aran while frequently traveling between the sister cities to manage the needs of their citizens. For reasons lost to time, Asterion fell out of favor with his master. Athrikus fashioned a powerful moonstone seal, forging an inescapable magical cage to confine Asterion within Bashal'Aran. The imprisonment stretched through centuries of agonizing confinement; worse still, when Asterion finally perished, he discovered death offered no release. His spirit remained bound to the ruined shrine, left behind when the world cracked open and demons overran the ancient settlement.

npc:athridas-bearmantle.text: Athridas Bearmantle. Athridas Bearmantle is a night elf druid residing in Dolanaar within the boughs of Teldrassil. Tasked with safeguarding the local settlement, he directs young adventurers to investigate the encroaching corruption affecting the local wildlife and the nearby Gnarlpine furbolgs. Stationed within Dolanaar, Athridas Bearmantle stands as an early line of defense for the night elves emerging from Shadowglen. As the boughs of the newly grown world tree Teldrassil exhibit unnatural signs of decay and unrest, Athridas works tirelessly to coordinate local scouting efforts and protect the peaceful township from surrounding threats. Much of Athridas's concern centers on the neighboring Gnarlpine tribe of furbolgs. Once peaceful neighbors, the Gnarlpine have succumbed to a spreading madness and corruption that poisons their shamans and chieftains, driving them into violent frenzy against the Kaldorei. Athridas mobilizes willing champions to contain the threat and unearth the deeper taint taking root in the wilderness.

npc:auntie-bernice-stonefield.text: "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield. At the Stonefield homestead in south-central Elwynn Forest, “Auntie” Bernice Stonefield keeps watch over the neighborhood. Widowed when her husband fell in the kingdom’s military campaigns, she is known throughout the valley for her pork belly pies. She stays outside the farmhouse beside Ma Stonefield and remains deeply suspicious of the rival Maclure family. Bernice carries the cost of war, as many common folk in the Kingdom of Stormwind do. Her husband fell in military campaigns, and she now lives with her kin at the family homestead. She helps Ma Stonefield manage the farm’s daily affairs, keeping the household fed and running. Her pork belly pies have made her famous among the people of the valley.

npc:balthule-shadowstrike.text: Balthule Shadowstrike. Balthule Shadowstrike is a night elf scout stationed in northern Darkshore near the Tower of Althalaxx. Serving as a forward agent for Delgren the Purifier, he keeps watch over the sinister cultists and dark practitioners occupying the ancient elven ruins. Adventurers traveling along the northern coast are often directed to him to assist in unravelling and disrupting the dark rituals underway at the tower. Perched in the wilderness just west of the Tower of Althalaxx, Balthule Shadowstrike maintains a lonely and perilous vigil. Darkshore's northern reaches are thick with restless spirits and shadowed ruins, but the activity around the tower poses a particularly acute threat. Balthule operates under the direction of Delgren the Purifier, observing the movements of dark casters who have crept into the ancient Highborne remnants.

npc:baros-alexston.text: Baros Alexston. In Stormwind City Hall, Baros Alexston keeps watch over the capital he helped rebuild. Once a close friend of Edwin VanCleef in the Stonemasons Guild, he stayed loyal to the crown when the guild fractured. Baros grew up on the Alexston Farmstead in Westfall's rolling grasslands. Thieves overran and burned the family homestead while he was young. Before they fled, his father hurriedly hid their cherished heirlooms across the grounds. Baros later journeyed to the capital and joined the Stonemasons Guild. For years, he labored beside Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef as they raised Stormwind anew from the ashes of the First War.

npc:billy-maclure.text: Billy Maclure. At Maclure Vineyards, Billy Maclure's pranks stir trouble between two neighboring farms. The young human boy dodges chores and plays at the feud between his family and the Stonefields, but fresh pastries can win his cooperation. Billy Maclure spends his days outside the barn at Maclure Vineyards, near farmer Gerard Tiller. He grows up among the grapevines in southern Elwynn Forest, often dodging chores and roaming the meadows. The Maclures and Stonefields have long been hostile toward each other. Billy treats their feud as a chance for pranks and petty theft.

npc:blind-mary.text: Blind Mary. Blind Mary is a tormented banshee haunting an abandoned, ruined farmhouse just southeast of Darkshire in Duskwood. Once a vain and beautiful mortal woman, her violent death and transformation drove her to self-inflicted mutilation in grief over what she had become. Before the shadows fell across Duskwood, Mary was known as a striking mortal woman who took immense pride in her beauty, rarely seen without her treasured looking glass. When the undead swept over the region, Mary was slain along with many of her neighbors. Unlike those who found rest in the earth, her spirit lingered on as an ethereal banshee, condemned to wander the mortal realm in a ghastly, translucent form. Awakening to undeath, Mary was overwhelmed by sorrow, horror, and fury at her monstrous reflection. Incapable of enduring the sight of her spectral visage, she clawed out her own eyes with her bare hands so she would never gaze upon herself again. In her agony, she discarded her beloved looking glass, leaving her to drift through her abandoned home as a blind, weeping wraith clutching to faint memories of the mortal life she lost.

npc:bolvar-fordragon.text: Bolvar Fordragon. Stormwind’s crown and armies rest with Bolvar Fordragon while King Varian is missing. As Regent and Supreme Commander of Stormwind’s armed forces, he stands beside young King Anduin in Stormwind Keep and tries to hold the kingdom together. Domestic troubles grow, while Lady Katrana Prestor’s counsel often delays his military decisions. King Varian vanished on the way to a peace summit on Theramore Isle, leaving Stormwind in political disarray. Ten-year-old Prince Anduin was crowned to preserve continuity, while Highlord Bolvar Fordragon took up the work of ruling as Regent. A venerated paladin devoted to the crown, Bolvar now faces a kingdom under strain. Stormwind’s soldiers are spread thin across Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood. Lady Katrana Prestor’s dismissive counsel adds to the burden, repeatedly blocking him from sending royal troops to towns on the frontier.

npc:calor.text: Calor. Calor is a dedicated resident of Darkshire who aids the Carevin family in defending Duskwood. Operating under the direction of Jonathan Carevin, he actively coordinates efforts to hunt down the vicious worgen stalking the gloomy forests. Adventurers looking to push back the ravenous beasts haunting the woods often find their assignments through him. Stationed within the beleaguered settlement of Darkshire, Calor works closely with Jonathan Carevin, one of the town's prominent defenders. Amid the endless gloom and creeping terrors of Duskwood, Calor devotes himself to supporting the Carevin household's mission: eradicating the supernatural horrors encroaching upon the town's perimeter before the remaining townsfolk are slaughtered. Calor's primary duty centers on confronting the feral worgen prowling the woods, particularly around blighted areas like the Rotting Orchard. These ferocious wolf-men are far more aggressive and dangerous than common beasts, slaughtering travelers and patrols alike. Calor enlists capable fighters to cull their ranks and investigate their origins, desperate to stem the bloodthirsty tide.

npc:captain-grayson.text: Captain Grayson. At Westfall Lighthouse, Captain Grayson keeps watch over the beacon that failed him. His ship smashed against the dark coastline, and now he tends the light so other sailors will not meet his fate. Captain Grayson once sailed the southern seas of the Eastern Kingdoms as a ship’s captain. One night, the lighthouse fire went dark as his vessel neared Westfall’s jagged shoals. The ship struck the rocks, and Grayson died with it. He awoke as an earthbound phantom, trapped upon the coast. In death, Captain Grayson went to Westfall Lighthouse, hoping to learn what waited beyond life. There he saw Old Murk-Eye, a notorious murloc, drive away the keeper and his family. The brave keepers returned to rekindle the flame, but Old Murk-Eye rallied the surrounding murlocs and led a second, brutal slaughter. Grayson could only watch as the family was butchered. With the keepers dead and Westfall crumbling under neglect, Captain Grayson bears the beacon’s solemn burden on his spectral shoulders. He asks passing travelers to gather fuel for the great flame. He also seeks vengeance for the slaughtered family: hunt down Old Murk-Eye and drive back the coastal murlocs.

npc:captain-stoutfist.text: Captain Stoutfist. Captain Stoutfist is the dwarven officer in charge of military defenses at Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. With the Dragonmaw clan pushing aggressively out of their marshland strongholds, Stoutfist coordinates defensive maneuvers and counter-offensives to ensure the vital Alliance port does not fall. Menethil Harbor serves as the principal deepwater port connecting Ironforge and Stormwind to the marshy lowlands of the Wetlands and the sea beyond. As the town's commanding officer, Captain Stoutfist bears the heavy burden of keeping its docks, civilian populace, and garrison secure against surrounding threats. The marshlands are notoriously hazardous, but the biggest peril to the settlement is an organized surge from renegade orcs. The Dragonmaw clan, entrenched within the Wetlands since the Second War, has begun pushing their operations directly toward the roadways and passes. By infiltrating Dun Algaz, they threaten to sever the overland lifeline connecting Loch Modan and Ironforge to Menethil Harbor. Facing a severe shortage of troops, Captain Stoutfist relies on visiting Alliance volunteers recommended by Mountaineer Valstag Ironjaw to stem the tide.

npc:chief-engineer-hinderweir-vii.text: Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII is a veteran dwarven engineer stationed atop the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan. Tasked with the upkeep and defense of this monumental feat of engineering, he oversees its delicate mechanisms while keeping watch for sabotage. Those who speak with him quickly discover that grave dangers threaten the integrity of the great dam. The Stonewrought Dam is one of the crowning achievements of dwarven stonecraft and engineering, holding back the massive waters of the Loch. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII bears the immense responsibility of maintaining its structure and operational machinery. Perched along the crest of the dam, he monitors the waterways, sluice gates, and structural stress points against the elements and local hazards.

npc:clerk-daltry.text: Clerk Daltry. Clerk Daltry is the civic record keeper stationed in Darkshire Town Hall in Duskwood. Surrounded by ledgers and registry books, he helps investigate the village's past and track down historical records, even if his archives are somewhat neglected and out of date. While Darkshire struggles against encroaching beasts, undead horrors, and supernatural gloom, everyday civic duties fall to Clerk Daltry. Working out of the Darkshire Town Hall alongside Lord Ello Ebonlocke and the local council, Daltry maintains the town's historical ledgers, property rolls, and census data. In a region fractured by disaster, his records are among the few surviving links to the days before Grand Hamlet fell into shadow. Because Darkshire has been cut off from regular Stormwind administration, Daltry's record-keeping is notoriously imperfect. Old documents go missing, ledgers fall behind, and vital town files are frequently misplaced or damaged. Adventurers investigating local cold cases or long-lost residents frequently consult him, only to find that uncovering the truth requires digging through overlooked notes or venturing out into the dangerous woods to recover lost papers.

npc:cliffwatcher-longhorn.text: Cliffwatcher Longhorn. Cliffwatcher Longhorn is the stoic tauren leader stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Tasked with safeguarding the isolated Horde outpost, he coordinates defenses against encroaching Galak centaur and monitors the suspicious machinations of the Grimtotem tribe. Perched upon the soaring rock spires of Thousand Needles, Freewind Post relies on sharp eyes and steady leadership to survive. Cliffwatcher Longhorn oversees the day-to-day security of this precarious settlement. With hostile forces gathering on the canyon floor below and along neighboring ridges, Longhorn acts as the settlement's primary coordinator for scouting reports and defensive military efforts.

npc:collin-mauren.text: Collin Mauren. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Collin Mauren studies practical magic and crafts useful spells from natural reagents. He also makes arcane scrolls for his friend Gaxim Rustfizzle, a gnome engineer and explorer. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Collin Mauren studies magic's practical uses. He crafts arcane formulas to solve specific problems, drawing on natural anomalies and raw components gathered across Azeroth. Their properties help him make functional scrolls and reagents for friends and travelers. Collin Mauren is helping his friend Gaxim Rustfizzle set off NG-5 explosives from a distance. Gaxim, a gnome tinkerer, needed a way to trigger them remotely, so Collin devised a messaging spell for a scroll. To impress the spell on it, Collin uses debris from Westfall's erratic Dust Devils. He awaits word on how Gaxim's scheme fares. Collin Mauren's studies reach from Stormwind across the Great Sea to Kalimdor's Stonetalon Mountains. He seeks the scales of the region's basilisks, whose resilient hides interest him as materials for synthesizing new spells. Travelers heading into Kalimdor often receive his requests for these rare hides. The scales fuel his study of how primal creature anatomy can steady complex enchantments.

npc:corithras-moonrage.text: Corithras Moonrage. Corithras Moonrage is a night elf scholar and quest giver stationed in the village of Dolanaar on Teldrassil. He guides newly arrived adventurers in understanding the nature of the great World Tree and tasks them with maintaining its sacred moonwells. Through his lessons, he reveals both the spiritual importance of Teldrassil and the growing burdens carried by the kaldorei. Residing in the shaded settlement of Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage serves as an instructor to travelers leaving the sheltered bounds of Shadowglen. As young kaldorei venture into the wider boughs of Teldrassil, Corithras ensures they understand the history of their new home. He teaches that survival in this changing era requires vigilance and reverence for the natural order. Much of Corithras's duty revolves around collecting moonwell water for the druids in Darnassus. He directs adventurers to collect pure waters from moonwells across Teldrassil in specially crafted phials for delivery to Fandral Staghelm. Through these trials, he monitors the health of the World Tree and seeks to maintain the delicate balance of the wilderness against creeping corruption.

npc:daphne-stilwell.text: Daphne Stilwell. On Westfall's cliffs, Daphne Stilwell keeps an orchard above the Longshore. She and her husband Jordan fled the north and now aid the Church of the Holy Light while guarding their home from nearby outlaws. West of Moonbrook and the Deadmines exit, Daphne Stilwell tends a homestead and apple orchard on the bluffs. From the Longshore below or gryphon routes south to Stranglethorn Vale above, the farm looks quiet. But life there is not safe. Bandits and scavengers roam nearby, while Daphne works among the trees and watches over her isolated land. Before coming to Westfall, Daphne and her husband Jordan lived in Lordaeron near Pyrewood Village, where they worked in what is now Shadowfang Keep. Darkness and disaster drove them south with thousands of other human refugees. Near Stormwind, Jordan's renowned skill as a craftsman and Daphne's steady presence brought them close to the Church of the Holy Light. They support the church and provide holy arms to paladins of the Silver Hand.

npc:delgren-the-purifier.text: Delgren the Purifier. Delgren the Purifier is a human paladin stationed at Maestra's Post on the northern edge of Ashenvale. Operating alongside comrades Balthule Shadowstrike and Feero Ironhand, he aids the night elves in cleansing demonic and shadow magic threatening the frontier, with a particular focus on the sinister Cult of the Dark Strand. Human paladins are a rare sight deep within the ancient forests of Kalimdor, but Delgren the Purifier arrived with a mission. Affiliated with the Argent Dawn, Delgren traveled west with a cadre of holy warriors determined to assist the Alliance's new night elf allies against the lingering evils of demons and undead remnants from the Third War. Stationed near the border of Darkshore and Ashenvale, he maintains a watchful vigil over travelers passing south from Auberdine. Despite his fierce devotion to the Holy Light and zealous nickname, Delgren possesses an unusual perspective on Kalimdor's tangled politics. Much to the annoyance and disdain of his conservative superiors, he took the time to learn Orcish. This rare linguistic skill hints at an unconventional mind—one that seeks to understand the enemies and neighbors sharing this untamed continent rather than relying solely on blind dogma.

npc:denalan.text: Denalan. Denalan is an accomplished night elf herbalist and botanist who tends a quiet lakeside plot along the eastern shore of Lake Al'Ameth. Working under a simple awning, he devotes his days to studying the island's plant life and seeking botanical remedies for the strange corruption affecting Teldrassil. He frequently enlists young adventurers to gather samples, study violent timberlings, and test enchanted soils. While many kaldorei focus on martial vigilance or high druidic rites, Denalan pursues the patient, meticulous craft of herbalism. Stationed along the tranquil eastern banks of Lake Al'Ameth, he has established a modest research camp consisting of a cloth awning, simple field tools, and tidy rows of cultivated planter boxes. Rather than retreating to the grand barrows of Darnassus, he prefers to remain close to the loam, directly examining the unusual flora that has sprouted since the planting of the new World Tree. Denalan's research is far more than an academic curiosity; it addresses the growing unrest among Teldrassil's native wildlife. The timberlings, normally docile woodland beings of wood and sprout, have turned increasingly aggressive. Denalan enchants specialized soil to nurse wild seeds in captivity and analyze how malignant forces seep into the root systems. By studying strange specimens like shimmering fronds, glowing fruit, and moss-twined growths, he seeks to isolate whatever dark taint is troubling the forest boughs.

npc:dirania-silvershine.text: Dirania Silvershine. Dirania Silvershine is a night elf resident of Shadowglen in Teldrassil. Deeply loyal and observant, she watches over the tranquil grove and looks out for her companion Iverron when his reckless ventures land him in peril. Dirania stands among the tranquil boughs of Shadowglen, the secluded vale where young night elves begin their service to Kalimdor and the Alliance. While many in the barrow mounds and sanctuaries look to broad spiritual duties, Dirania stays mindful of those nearest to her, attentive to the quiet dangers that stir even in the heart of Teldrassil. Dirania's immediate concern is her companion Iverron. Overeager and careless around the poisonous woodland creatures creeping across the glen, Iverron frequently gets into trouble. When he succumbs to a venomous bite from the local webwood spiders, Dirania takes it upon herself to seek out willing hands to gather ingredients and prepare a remedy before the venom takes a permanent toll.

npc:dorn-plainstalker.text: Dorn Plainstalker. Dorn Plainstalker is a solitary tauren elder residing in the Weathered Nook overlooking the canyons of Thousand Needles. He serves as an overseer of traditional rite of passage trials, challenging Horde adventurers to prove their character and fortitude. Through trials of faith, endurance, strength, and lore, he tests whether travelers are worthy servants of the Earth Mother and their people. Secluded in a shallow cave high atop the canyon ridges of the Weathered Nook, Dorn Plainstalker lives apart from the bustle of Freewind Post. Reaching his mountain redoubt requires winding along the sheer northern cliffs overlooking the towering mesas below. From this quiet vantage point, Dorn maintains ancient customs and judges those who seek guidance in the harsh southern barrens. Dorn Plainstalker guides pilgrims through a demanding series of tests meant to measure the core virtues of a tauren champion: faith, endurance, strength, and lore. Rather than mere exercises in brute force, these trials force aspirants to confront fear, leap blindly into the unknown, outlast cunning wilderness predators, and ponder the sacred history of Kalimdor before claiming their final passage.

npc:duthorian-rall.text: Duthorian Rall. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall guides new holy warriors through their trials. The respected human knight of the Silver Hand is one of the Alliance's most influential paladins, overseeing their training and spiritual tests. He teaches charity, valor, and devotion as they prepare to defend Azeroth from the Scourge and threats within the kingdom. In the Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall upholds the traditions of the Knights of the Silver Hand. The kingdom is unsettled by internal strife, and King Varian Wrynn is missing. Duthorian carries the duty of teaching discipline to new initiates. Respected paladins in the field send promising recruits to him: Brother Wilhelm in Goldshire and Brandur Ironhammer in Ironforge, so they can begin their sacred trials. Duthorian teaches that martial power without a moral foundation is hollow. In the Tome of Divinity trials, he tests an initiate's empathy through acts of mercy and selfless service across Stormwind. Only after these tests does he entrust candidates with deeper mysteries. Near Heroes' Vigil, he tests them with the Symbol of Life, then sends them to aid wounded allies and learn to channel the Light's power to restore fallen comrades from death.

npc:elling-trias.text: Elling Trias. In Stormwind's Trade District, Elling Trias runs a cheese shop with his family. He welcomes customers with easy talk, while his quiet work as an information broker reaches across continents. Elling Trias sells fine cheese in the Trade District, working beside his wife Elaine and son Ben. He cheerfully offers wheels of cheese and chats with the townsfolk. To those who know better, Trias' Cheese is one of Stormwind's most reliable fronts. The city's steady trade gives operatives, courtiers and adventurers a place to exchange quiet words beyond the city watch's notice. Elling Trias has informants and allies far beyond what most shopkeepers can claim. He keeps ties with Master Mathias Shaw of SI:7, works with Church contacts such as Bishop DeLavey, and corresponds with agents in Darkshire, Theramore Isle and the distant Plaguelands near Hearthglen. When rumors surface about highway bandits or quiet movements in the countryside, Trias often pieces them together before the royal court takes notice.

npc:fandral-staghelm.text: Fandral Staghelm. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the druids of the Cenarion Circle from the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. Stepping into power after Malfurion Stormrage vanished into the Emerald Dream, he championed the planting of the new World Tree, Teldrassil. Proud, abrasive, and relentlessly ambitious, Fandral advocates for an aggressive Kaldorei resurgence that frequently pits him against High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Following the Third War and the sacrifice of Nordrassil atop Mount Hyjal, the night elves lost their immortality and their sacred sanctuary. When Malfurion Stormrage vanished, Fandral took up leadership of the druids and convinced the Circle of Ancients that it was time for their people to rebuild and regain their immortality. With the Circle's approval, he led the druids in raising Teldrassil off the coast of Kalimdor. He envisioned the colossal bough as a monument to Kaldorei endurance and a vessel to restore their lost supremacy, even though the Dragon Aspects pointedly withheld their blessings from the unapproved endeavor. A millennium before the First War, Fandral served as the Kaldorei field commander in Silithus during the War of the Shifting Sands. Renowned among the insectoid qiraji as 'Kar'sis'—the Hand of Earth—he held the front lines alongside his beloved only son, Valstann. Exploiting Fandral's devotion, the qiraji General Rajaxx engineered a feint against Southwind Village and captured Valstann, ruthlessly executing him directly in front of the horrified Archdruid. The loss shattered Fandral's spirit, precipitating a devastating retreat and cementing an abiding, bitter hatred for the swarm that remains etched into his haughty demeanor. Within the marble boughs of Darnassus, Fandral governs Kaldorei affairs with a haughty, unyielding hand. Unlike High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, who favors spiritual preservation and cautious diplomacy, Fandral views military expansion and decisive strength as paramount to the survival of their people.

npc:farthing.text: Farthing. Farthing serves the faithful from Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. The kind and wise human clergyman guides parishioners and directs aid to settlements across the kingdom. Bishop Farthing tends to the spiritual needs of Stormwind City from the Cathedral of Light. Alongside Archbishop Benedictus and the gathered clergy, he counsels travelers, assists those pursuing the holy arts, and attends to the Church of the Holy Light's civic and pastoral duties. From the capital, Farthing directs earnest travelers toward parts of the kingdom in need of holy aid. Reports tell of the necromancer Morbent Fel and an undead blight spreading through Duskwood. Farthing advises on ways to overcome dark sorceries and cleanse the blighted frontier.

npc:first-mate-fitzsimmons.text: First Mate Fitzsimmons. First Mate Fitzsimmons is a ragged, reeking sailor who spends his days drinking outside the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Once the first mate aboard the Wave Mistress of the Kul Tiras Third Fleet, he is the sole known living survivor of the fleet's destruction during the Second War. Haunted by the tragedy, he seeks willing adventurers to face the restless spirits of his drowned comrades. Lounging outside the Deepwater Tavern amid the damp salt air of Menethil Harbor, First Mate Fitzsimmons is an easy man to overlook—or avoid entirely, given his unwashed stench. To most patrons, he is just another broken old salt drinking his memories away. Yet those willing to sit and listen will hear harrowing tales of a proud fleet brought low by fire and claw. During the Second War, Fitzsimmons served as first mate aboard the Wave Mistress, part of the Kul Tiras Third Fleet dispatched to fight the Horde. Off the coast of the Wetlands, the fleet was ambushed and incinerated by enslaved red dragons flown by Dragonmaw orcs. The ships were shattered and sunk, leaving Fitzsimmons as the only man to drag himself ashore alive.

npc:foreman-oslow.text: Foreman Oslow. Foreman Oslow is Lakeshire's beleaguered master builder, tasked with repairing the ruined Everstill Bridge in the heart of Redridge Mountains. Beset by Blackrock orc artillery and gnoll raiders, his reconstruction efforts have stalled due to lost shipments and sunken equipment. He relies heavily on traveling adventurers to retrieve his gear and secure materials so Lakeshire can reconnect its vital trade route. Standing by the fractured masonry of the Everstill Bridge, Foreman Oslow faces an uphill battle. The bridge is the lifeline of Lakeshire, spanning the expanse of Lake Everstill and linking the western roads toward Elwynn to the eastern shores. Blackrock orcs, sweeping down from the crags of Stonewatch, targeted the crossing to cripple the town's logistics and military movement, leaving the settlement splintered and vulnerable. Every attempt Oslow makes to rebuild seems plagued by misfortune. When the bridge fell, his replacement tools were shipped overland from Goldshire and loaded onto a lake ferry. Orc catapult crews caught the vessel in their sights, sending his heavy iron toolbox straight to the muddy bed of Lake Everstill. To compound matters, local Redridge gnolls hijacked the caravan of new materials sent from Stormwind, making off with the iron pikes and rivets necessary to raise the arches.

npc:furen-longbeard.text: Furen Longbeard. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, warriors seek Furen Longbeard's skill to forge specialized, battle-ready armor. Apprenticed to Grimand Elmore, the master armorer is known for his metallurgical expertise and heavy protective gear. Furen Longbeard works far from Ironforge's great forges, among the cobblestones and soot of Stormwind's Dwarven District. Like many dwarves, he brought traditional metallurgy south to help rebuild and defend the kingdom. His work keeps him connected with artisans throughout the city and beyond. Grimand Elmore taught Furen Longbeard his craft. Furen has perfected ways to treat heavy mail and plate so they can withstand the punishment of battle. Young warriors seeking durable protection turn to him, and he requires rare ores, specialized components, and exotic reagents from distant corners of the world to fashion his signature fire-hardened armor.

npc:gakin-the-darkbinder.text: Gakin the Darkbinder. Beneath The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder teaches the warlock arts in secret. He tests aspiring Alliance warlocks before they attempt to summon and bind demons. Below The Slaughtered Lamb's taproom, a cellar shelters those who study shadow and fel. The crypt-like room holds summoning circles and grim tomes, hidden from the eyes that watch Stormwind's open mage sanctuaries. Gakin guides young warlocks there, teaching discipline and restraint before they summon forces they cannot control. Gakin teaches demonology and the rites used to bind demons. Those who earn his notice travel across the kingdom to gather rare things, including stolen bloodstone talismans and corrupt wood from dark forests. When the materials are ready, Gakin oversees their work in the crypt's summoning circle. Novices must master voidwalkers and succubi in trials that test their will and put their lives at risk.

npc:gaxim-rustfizzle.text: Gaxim Rustfizzle. Gaxim Rustfizzle is an ambitious gnome scholar and tinker stationed at a small Alliance camp along the Webwinder Path in Stonetalon Mountains. A representative of the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, he seeks to prove to skeptical night elves that advanced artifice and alchemy can preserve their woodland realm. His scientific curiosity is matched by a fierce vendetta against the destructive operations of the Venture Company. While night elves traditionally rely on ancient druidism and nature magic, Gaxim Rustfizzle arrived in the craggy passes of Stonetalon to demonstrate a radically different perspective. Representing the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, he genuinely believes that calculated mechanisms and chemical solutions can defend and restore Kalimdor's wilderness just as effectively as prayers to Elune. Camped alongside the sentinel Kaela Shadowspear on the Webwinder Path, he works tirelessly to convince his tall, reclusive allies of engineering's ecological merits. Much of Gaxim's energy is channeled against the Venture Company, whose clear-cutting and industrial greed desecrate nearby Windshear Crag. Believing that crude goblin machinery deserves neither respect nor mercy, Gaxim coordinates covert operations and volatile chemical sabotage against their logging operations. To him, crippling their shredders and stealing their schematics is not merely tactical warfare—it is a practical demonstration that superior gnomish intellect always triumphs over careless corporate plunder.

npc:gelbin-mekkatorque.text: Gelbin Mekkatorque. Gelbin Mekkatorque is the High Tinker of the gnomes, currently residing in exile in Tinker Town within Ironforge. Renowned as a visionary engineer whose inventions include the mechanostrider and the Deeprun Tram, he now carries the heavy burden of Gnomeregan's fall and oversees efforts to reclaim his people's ancestral home. Gnomish leadership is earned through intellect and merit rather than bloodlines, and Gelbin Mekkatorque's rise to High Tinker was propelled by pure inventive genius. Mekkatorque revolutionized personal transportation with the creation of the first functioning mechanostrider. He also assisted the Bronzebeard dwarves in developing their formidable siege engines, and he was instrumental in the creation of the subterranean Deeprun Tram linking Ironforge to Stormwind.

npc:glorin-steelbrow.text: Glorin Steelbrow. Glorin Steelbrow is a dwarven operative found drinking at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Acting as an associate of Bishop Farthing of Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, he helps adventurers investigate the lost Third Fleet and recover sacred relics and materials scattered across the Wetlands coast. His efforts tie the haunted wilderness of Duskwood directly to the sunken shipwrecks of the north. While Bishop Farthing aids the people of Duskwood against its creeping terrors from Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, he maintains ties far to the north in Menethil Harbor. Stationed inside the bustling Deepwater Tavern, Glorin Steelbrow acts as Farthing's eyes and hands on the coast. He offers aid and direction to travelers sent north in search of sacred metals and forgotten relics, providing a crucial bridge between the troubles of the southern forest and the sunken wreckage of the Wetlands.

npc:grelin-whitebeard.text: Grelin Whitebeard. Grelin Whitebeard is a dwarven scout stationed in Coldridge Valley by royal decree to assess the Frostmane troll threat. Operating out of an isolated camp, he relies on rising adventurers to keep the trolls contained while Ironforge's attention remains consumed by the trogg crisis. Grelin Whitebeard and his brother Senir were dispatched to Coldridge Valley under direct orders from the Senate of Ironforge and King Magni Bronzebeard himself. Their mission was clear: assess and neutralize the threat posed by the native Frostmane trolls. With Ironforge's official military fully bogged down combating trogg outbreaks across Dun Morogh, the brothers were given very few resources to accomplish their task. Grelin had to establish an outpost in the snowy hills and look toward local recruits and passing initiates to carry out the necessary work. From his camp, Grelin monitors the encroaching Frostmane tribe south of Coldridge Valley. The trolls have grown increasingly aggressive, staging bolder incursions outside their mountain caverns. During one such raid, a heavily painted brute named Grik'nir the Cold slipped into the unattended camp and made off with Grelin's field journal, containing his critical observations. Unwilling to fail the King, Grelin uses intrepid travelers to strike deep into the Frostmane caves, recover his stolen writings, and ensure his final intelligence reaches Senir in Kharanos.

npc:grif-wildheart.text: Grif Wildheart. Grif Wildheart is a seasoned dwarven hunter trainer stationed outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Renowned among the local mountaineers for his deep affinity with wildlife, he instructs budding marksmen in tracking, marksmanship, and the rites of beast taming. For young hunters emerging from Coldridge Valley, Grif provides the vital bridge between firing a rifle and walking alongside a loyal animal companion. While many Ironforge dwarves prefer the fiery warmth of a forge or the steady clink of pickaxes, Grif Wildheart has dedicated his life entirely to the frozen wilderness of Dun Morogh. Local mountaineers half-jokingly say he spends a bit too much time with four-legged beasts, but none dispute his mastery of the wild. Having spent years tracking across snowbound ridges alongside seasoned hunting companions, Grif possesses an intimate understanding of the natural predators that roam the crags. When young dwarf hunters finish their preliminary trials in Coldridge Valley, they are directed straight to Kharanos to seek Grif's guidance. While he sharpens their aim and teaches essential wilderness survival tricks, his true specialty lies in forging bonds between hunter and beast. Through a sequence of rigorous trials, Grif sends his pupils out into the freezing wastes with a taming rod to test their mettle against Dun Morogh's iconic predators: Large Crag Boars, Snow Leopards, and Ice Claw Bears. Once a hunter demonstrates the will and composure needed to calm three distinct wild beasts, Grif's tutelage in Kharanos reaches its conclusion. Recognizing that a hunter must also learn to feed, discipline, and train their new ally, he sends his graduates up the mountainside to Ironforge. There, under the great vaulted roofs of the dwarven capital, novice hunters report to master beast trainers to learn the deeper art of caring for their permanent lifelong companion.

npc:gryan-stoutmantle.text: Gryan Stoutmantle. At Sentinel Hill in Westfall, Gryan Stoutmantle leads the People's Militia. A paladin of the Silver Hand, he returned from Lordaeron to defend his birthplace after Stormwind's crown left it to banditry. Gryan Stoutmantle first served far from Westfall's fields. As a young man, he traveled north to Lordaeron and took vows as a Knight of the Silver Hand. He endured the horrors of the Third War there. News reached him that his native province was collapsing into lawlessness, overrun by organized brigands and abandoned by the crown. Gryan left the northern fronts to defend honest farmers, determined that his home would not fall as the north had. When Gryan returned, Westfall had virtually no defenders. Royal neglect and political paralysis in the House of Nobles kept Stormwind from sending garrison troops. Gryan formed the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill, gathering local farmers, sentries, and traveling mercenaries into a volunteer defense corps. The militia holds a precarious line against the Defias Brotherhood, riverpaw gnolls, and hostile mechanoids. Even when nearby Lakeshire pleads for aid, Gryan cannot spare reinforcements.

npc:guard-thomas.text: Guard Thomas. At the bridge west of Eastvale Logging Camp, Guard Thomas watches Elwynn’s eastern frontier. The Stormwind soldier guards local workers from wild predators and murlocs. At the stone bridge over the river toward Eastvale Logging Camp, Guard Thomas holds a quiet but exposed post. The woods around him shelter aggressive creatures, and the logging workers depend on the Stormwind guard for protection. With the army stretched thin, Thomas must rely on travelers to help keep order and carry messages to central command.

npc:gwennyth-bly-leggonde.text: Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde is a night elf residing in the coastal port of Auberdine. Stationed along the misty Darkshore coast, she watches the tides and directs travelers to investigate the strange remains washing ashore. Her concerns center on the mysterious sea creatures and massive turtles whose carcasses have begun littering the northern beaches. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde makes her home in Auberdine, the bustling seaside haven of Darkshore. While many in town concern themselves with the forest or shipping across the Veiled Sea, Gwennyth keeps her gaze firmly on the coastline. The tides have recently turned grim, depositing the remains of colossal marine life onto the surf. To understand what is happening in the waters offshore, she relies on willing adventurers to scour the sands, retrieve skeletal samples, and bring back answers. The beaches north and south of Auberdine have seen an alarming influx of beached sea creatures and ancient sea turtles. Rather than letting their deaths go unnoticed, Gwennyth tasks travelers with inspecting these fallen titans. By studying the bones and discovering what drove these beasts ashore or took their lives, she hopes to piece together the hidden perils lurking off the shores of northern Kalimdor.

npc:high-executor-darthalia.text: High Executor Darthalia. High Executor Darthalia is a high-ranking Forsaken military commander stationed at Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Acting under the direct authority of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and Varimathras, she directs Forsaken operations against the human stronghold of Southshore and local Syndicate brigands. Her leadership is central to securing the Horde's southern flank in Lordaeron. Operating out of Tarren Mill, High Executor Darthalia serves as the operational commander for Forsaken forces throughout the Hillsbrad Foothills. Her primary strategic concern is halting the expansion of human resistance, keeping the Alliance forces in Southshore contained, and hunting down the lawless Syndicate rogues infesting the surrounding countryside. Every offensive push into southern Hillsbrad flows directly through her command. Under direct orders originating from the Undercity's high leadership—the Banshee Queen and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras—Darthalia oversees the relentless attrition war across Hillsbrad. She coordinates scouting missions, targeted strikes against human leadership, and bounties on dangerous outlaws who threaten the Forsaken hold on northern Lordaeron.

npc:high-priestess-laurena.text: High Priestess Laurena. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena trains human priests in devotion and arcane wards. High Priestess Laurena holds a senior post in the Church of the Holy Light. She serves in Stormwind City's Cathedral of Light, the heart of the faith, where Archbishop Benedictus leads the Church. Behind the central altar in the cathedral sanctuary, High Priestess Laurena mentors aspiring priests. Acolytes who show dedication and piety are sent to her for deeper study. She teaches sacred boons such as Desperate Prayer and defensive spells that turn enemy arcane magic against its wielders. When her students have learned all she can teach, she sends them to other master priests across the Alliance.

npc:illiyana.text: Illiyana. Illiyana is an ancient dryad stationed in southwestern Ashenvale, dedicated to protecting the woodland from ancient corruption. Wandering near the Shrine of Aessina, she rallies champions of the Alliance to push back against the vicious satyrs that plague the ancient groves. Her vigilance represents the enduring bond between the daughters of Cenarius and the night elven wilderness. Like all dryads, Illiyana is one of the daughters of the demigod Cenarius. Peaceful yet fiercely protective of wild lands, she patrols the woods of southwestern Ashenvale. As dark forces stir and the woodlands suffer under creeping corruption, Illiyana keeps watch over sacred relics and groves, acting as a steward for nature's primal sanctity. Illiyana's primary concern in the region is the lingering blight of the satyrs. These twisted, demonic creatures continuously seek to corrupt the glades and endanger her dryad sisters. Illiyana frequently enlists passing travelers to strike down these vile abominations and recover lost artifacts, including the Branch of Cenarius, to ensure the woods remain sheltered from demonic taint.

npc:iverron.text: Iverron. Iverron is a young night elf found in Shadowglen, the sheltered starting bough of Teldrassil. Stricken by the venom of the woodland's increasingly agitated arachnids, his plight serves as an early warning of the growing corruption within the World Tree. While wandering through the quiet canopies of Shadowglen, Iverron ran afoul of the webwood spiders nesting in the vale. Succumbing quickly to their toxic bite, the young elf was left incapacitated, unable to return to safety on his own. His helpless condition highlights the sudden aggression sweeping through creatures that once shared the glade in peace.

npc:jaina-proudmoore.text: Jaina Proudmoore. Lady Jaina Proudmoore is the ruler of Theramore Isle and the most powerful human sorceress alive. Formerly a star pupil of Dalaran's Kirin Tor, she led the survivors of Lordaeron across the Great Sea and now strives to maintain a fragile peace between the Alliance and the New Horde. The daughter of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras, Jaina showed remarkable aptitude for the arcane at an early age and studied under Archmage Antonidas in Dalaran. During the Third War, she investigated the mysterious Plague of Undeath alongside Prince Arthas Menethil, witnessing firsthand the tragic downfall of Lordaeron. Guided by the warnings of the Prophet Medivh, she rallied an expedition of human survivors and set sail westward to the forgotten continent of Kalimdor. There, her forces forged an unprecedented alliance with Thrall's Horde and the night elves, standing together atop Mount Hyjal to defeat Archimonde and shatter the Burning Legion's invasion. Following the Legion's defeat, Jaina founded the island citadel of Theramore off the coast of Dustwallow Marsh, establishing the primary bastion of the Alliance in southern Kalimdor. Her commitment to diplomacy was tested to its limits when her father arrived seeking vengeance against the orcs; Jaina refused to support his war, stepping aside as Thrall's forces slew the Grand Admiral to prevent Kalimdor from plunging into another devastating conflict. Today, she rules Theramore as a steadfast advocate for coexistence, working closely with Warchief Thrall while anchoring the Alliance's presence against rising local tensions.

npc:je-neu-sancrea.text: Je'neu Sancrea. Je'neu Sancrea is a Darkspear troll and a member of the Earthen Ring stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the Ashenvale coast. Sensing dark disturbances deep beneath the shoreline, he directs Horde adventurers to investigate the corruption infesting the ancient submerged temple of Blackfathom Deeps. While most of the Earthen Ring focuses on elemental harmony across Kalimdor, Je'neu Sancrea keeps watch over the secluded and dangerous Zoram Strand. Perched at Zoram'gar Outpost, he observes the dark tremors and unnatural tides stirring near the ruined temple of Blackfathom Deeps. Though bound by the shamanic duties of his circle, his strong loyalties to the Darkspear tribe and Thrall's Horde keep him working exclusively alongside Horde champions.

npc:jern-hornhelm.text: Jern Hornhelm. Jern Hornhelm is a dwarven miner affiliated with the Explorers' League, stationed in the town of Thelsamar. He coordinates vital logistics and communication between the settlement, Ironforge, and the archaeological dig site deeper in Loch Modan. Adventurers frequently assist him with shuttling mining supplies and progress reports across the region. Stationed within the rustic town of Thelsamar, Jern Hornhelm plays a key logistical role for dwarven operations throughout Loch Modan. While dwarven scholars and field teams venture out into the wilderness to unearth their ancestral past, maintaining consistent supply chains remains essential. Jern ensures that vital resources, tools, and communications reach the active dig sites safely. As a member of the Explorers' League, Jern bridges the gap between field archaeologists and the League's leadership in the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. Sites such as Ironband's Excavation rely heavily on blasting powder, equipment, and regular dispatches to keep work moving forward. Jern enlists reliable travelers to navigate the trogg-infested roads and keep the dig fully operational.

npc:jitters.text: Jitters. Jitters is a terrified, half-starved human hiding among the ruins of Raven Hill in Duskwood. He clings to scraps of food and struggles to speak about the horrors he has witnessed. Found shivering amid the dilapidated houses of Raven Hill, Jitters lives in constant terror of the predators stalking Duskwood's western trails. He relies on passing adventurers for simple sustenance, desperate for food while keeping a frantic eye on the encroaching shadows. His skittish mannerisms and uncanny reflex for leaping clear of sudden danger earned him his moniker long ago, but his frantic paranoia is born from firsthand encounters with horrific horrors.

npc:jonathan-carevin.text: Jonathan Carevin. Jonathan Carevin is a resolute human hunter residing in Darkshire, dedicated to eradicating the darkness plaguing Duskwood. Unlike the defensive Night Watch, he and his family actively hunt down the undead, worgen, and any heretical threats lurking under the darkened canopies. While Darkshire depends upon the Night Watch to patrol the roads and safeguard the township, Jonathan Carevin believes a mere defensive perimeter is insufficient. Alongside his family and allies like Calor, Jonathan takes the offensive. He actively targets the unholy fiends wandering Duskwood, pursuing a personal crusade to purge all demons, undead, and heretics from the region under the grace of the Light.

npc:jordan-stilwell.text: Jordan Stilwell. Jordan Stilwell is a skilled human weaponsmith stationed outside the snowy Gates of Ironforge in Dun Morogh. Though originally meant to become a paladin of the Holy Light, he followed his father's craft to become an artisan whose work serves paladins across the Alliance. He is best known for forging Verigan's Fist in honor of his old friend, Bosch Verigan. Though Jordan Stilwell was expected to take holy vows and become a paladin within the Church of the Holy Light, he ultimately chose the way of the forge. He followed in his father's footsteps, taking up his father's enchanted smithing hammer. Jordan refined his craft under the tutelage of the dwarven blacksmith Bailor Stonehand. Despite setting aside the mantle of an anointed holy warrior, Jordan remains deeply faithful to the Light, dedicating his extraordinary craftsmanship to outfitting champions who fight in its name. Long before setting up shop in the biting cold of Dun Morogh, Jordan served as a smith at the keep of Baron Silverlaine in Silverpine Forest. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the feral worgen upon the fortress, turning it into the cursed bastion known as Shadowfang Keep, Jordan managed to escape the bloodshed. Forced to abandon his forge and his former home, he eventually found refuge among the dwarves of Dun Morogh.

npc:kaela-shadowspear.text: Kaela Shadowspear. Kaela Shadowspear is a night elf sentinel stationed southwest of Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. From her small outpost, she coordinates with fellow sentinels to monitor escalating tensions and regional disruptions in the wilderness. She relies on brave travelers to scout dangerous territory and learn what has corrupted the land's ancient defenders. Positioned just southwest of the industrial devastation of Windshear Crag, Kaela Shadowspear keeps a watchful vigil over the surrounding passes. The Stonetalon Mountains are fraught with danger as the Horde encroaches and goblin operations exploit the land's natural bounty. Operating alongside the gnome Gaxim Rustfizzle, Kaela acts as an essential forward liaison for the night elves, tracking threats that push deeper into ancestral territory. The unrest in Stonetalon goes far beyond territorial skirmishes. The violent disruption of nature has agitated the elementals and brought harm to ancient guardians of the forest. Kaela works tirelessly to dispatch adventurers against raging elemental spirits and to learn what has corrupted the wounded ancients, the treants who once guarded the Vale, striving to restore peace before the land is irrevocably scarred.

npc:laurna-morninglight.text: Laurna Morninglight. Laurna Morninglight is a night elf priest trainer residing in the tranquil settlement of Dolanaar within Teldrassil. Devoted to the Sisterhood of Elune, she guides budding acolytes emerging from Shadowglen in the spiritual rites and healing graces of the Moon Goddess. Her teachings prepare young night elf priests for the growing threats encroaching on the boughs of the World Tree. Situated amidst the boughs of Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight serves as one of the primary mentors for young priests who have completed their initial rites in Shadowglen. As new initiates step out into the broader reaches of Teldrassil, she instructs them on expanding their communion with Elune, balancing the light of healing with defensive rites necessary to survive an increasingly hostile wild. Priestcraft among the kaldorei is deeply intertwined with the worship of Elune rather than the abstract Holy Light revered by humans and dwarves. Laurna tasks her students with spiritual labors such as receiving sacred robes and healing a wounded Sentinel. Through these traditions, acolytes learn that their powers are direct gifts of the Mother Moon, meant to preserve and mend the kaldorei people.

npc:lieutenant-farren-orinelle.text: Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle is an officer of the Stormwind army currently stationed at the Southshore inn in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Deeply unhappy with his frontier posting, he spends most of his time drinking while outsourcing his duties to passing travelers. His primary military assignment is dealing with the encroaching murlocs along the coast, a chore he eagerly delegates in hopes of securing a transfer back south. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle did not choose Southshore. Dispatched far from Stormwind City, the lieutenant finds the damp, contested shores of Hillsbrad a miserable step down from the civilized comforts of the capital. Instead of patrolling the fields or coordinating defenses with his commanding officer, Marshal Redpath, Orinelle has practically taken up permanent residence inside Southshore's inn. His days are spent sulking, drinking, and dreaming of an official transfer order that will return him to the south. Despite his comfortable seat at the tavern, Orinelle still answers to Marshal Redpath, who tasked the lieutenant with clearing out the murlocs swarming the nearby shoreline. Unwilling to soil his boots in coastal mud, Orinelle relies on wandering adventurers to cull the creatures and gather proof of their demise. He hopes that presenting tangible results back to his superiors will show his duty is accomplished, hastening his eventual recall to Stormwind.

npc:lord-ello-ebonlocke.text: Lord Ello Ebonlocke. Lord Ello Ebonlocke is the mayor of Darkshire and the leader of its governing council, stationed inside the Darkshire Town Hall. Surrounded by darkness and creeping horrors, he struggles daily to maintain order and protect his besieged citizens despite receiving little aid from Stormwind. Seated in the gloom of the Darkshire Town Hall, Lord Ello Ebonlocke bears the heavy burden of governing a settlement on the brink of ruin. Once part of the prosperous rural haven known as Grand Hamlet, Darkshire is now smothered by perpetual shadow and besieged by ravenous ghouls, skeletal abominations, and feral beasts. Ello presides over the Council of Darkshire, striving against impossible odds to keep the remnants of civilization functioning while Stormwind turns a blind eye to their plight. Because Stormwind's garrison refuses to spare soldiers for the borderlands, Darkshire relies almost entirely on local volunteer militias like the Night Watch, commanded by his relative, Althea Ebonlocke. When neighboring leaders like Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire plead for reinforcements to combat Blackrock orcs, Lord Ebonlocke must make agonizing choices. As he solemnly explains to messengers from Redridge, Darkshire cannot spare a single blade: sending their guards beyond the forest's edge would leave their own homes to be instantly overrun by the surrounding evils.

npc:madame-eva.text: Madame Eva. Madame Eva is a revered fortune-teller and matriarch living in Darkshire in the shadowed forest of Duskwood. Practicing older, mystic arts of divination and cartomancy, she often serves as the first townsperson to sense unnatural disturbances across the woods. Travelers frequently seek her out to unravel grim mysteries or procure occult charms against the creeping dark. Dwelling quietly amidst the gloom of Darkshire, Madame Eva practices cartomancy and ancient folk rituals that many in Stormwind's cathedral would view with suspicion. In a forsaken region plagued by feral beasts, the undead, and darker horrors, her eerie insights are tolerated and sought after by desperate townspeople and visiting adventurers alike. Beyond her role as an occult reader, Madame Eva is deeply devoted to her family, serving as grandmother to Alyssa Eva and young Lohgan. When her cartomancy reveals dark omens threatening her granddaughter, Eva does not hesitate to enlist the aid of passing wanderers to scour the woods, uncovering long-buried tragedies before history can repeat itself. Eva's knowledge extends beyond card reading to ritual crafting and warding. From spinning Ghost Hair Thread out of a spirit's hair to crafting bizarre folk relics like the Totem of Infliction, she understands the strange, twilight logic that governs Duskwood's restless spirits better than almost anyone else in town.

npc:maggran-earthbinder.text: Maggran Earthbinder. Maggran Earthbinder is a grizzled tauren veteran appointed by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof to lead the Horde encampment at Sun Rock Retreat. Hardened by a lifetime of brutal conflict, he oversees the defense of the craggy valleys of Stonetalon against ravenous beasts and aggressive harpy covens. Though wearied by countless battles, he remains a steadfast guardian of the settlement. Maggran Earthbinder was sent into the Stonetalon Mountains by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof himself. A veteran of countless skirmishes and bloody campaigns, Maggran admits that age and violence have hardened his heart, stripping away the natural gentleness typical of his people. Sun Rock Retreat was meant to be both an outpost under his steady command and a place of respite, where warm winds and mountain sunshine might soothe his battle-worn spirit. Even in Stonetalon, Maggran finds little peace. As overseer of Sun Rock Retreat, he coordinates defense efforts against the Bloodfury harpies nesting in the peaks and marshals fighters to counter predatory perils across the crags. Having once survived an ambush by the giant spider Besseleth herself, Maggran holds no illusions about the deadly wilderness around them and frequently enlists travelers to eliminate deadly regional predators before they overrun the outpost.

npc:magistrate-solomon.text: Magistrate Solomon. Magistrate Solomon is the chief magistrate of Lakeshire, presiding over local affairs from the town hall. Besieged by Blackrock orcs and relentless gnoll clans, he spends his days frantically pleading for military aid from an indifferent and distracted Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon governs Lakeshire during the darkest hour in its recent history. The tranquil lakeside settlement is surrounded by hostility: Redridge and Shadowhide gnolls prowl the surrounding hills, while Blackrock orcs descend from the north in organized warbands. Solomon works alongside Marshal Marris to maintain civil order and muster a defense, but Lakeshire's local guards and militia are stretched to their absolute breaking point. Desperate to secure reinforcements, Solomon has dispatched messengers across the kingdom—pleading for aid from Westfall, Darkshire, and the capital of Stormwind itself. His petitions have yielded bitter disappointment. Westfall struggles under the grip of the Defias Brotherhood, Duskwood is consumed by its own creeping terrors, and Stormwind City refuses to deploy troops to the eastern frontier, leaving Lakeshire entirely to its own devices.

npc:magni-bronzebeard.text: Magni Bronzebeard. Magni Bronzebeard is the Lord of Ironforge, Thane of the Bronzebeard clan, and ruler of Khaz Modan. A veteran commander of the Second War, he leads his mountainous kingdom through grief and political tension while championing dwarven archaeology across Azeroth. The eldest of three brothers, Magni grew up keenly aware of the weight awaiting him under the mountain. When the Horde invaded during the Second War, he held Ironforge behind its impenetrable gates, emerging to pledge Khaz Modan to the Alliance of Lordaeron once the siege was broken. In the years of peace that followed, Magni welcomed his gnomish allies into the city after the fall of Gnomeregan, granting High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his refugees sanctuary within the mountain. To unite the fractured southern and northern kingdoms, Magni petitioned Mekkatorque to engineer an unprecedented subterranean marvel: the Deeprun Tram, connecting Ironforge directly to Stormwind. Beneath Magni's regal bearing lies deep personal tragedy. During the Third War, word arrived from Northrend that his beloved younger brother, Muradin, had perished on Prince Arthas Menethil's expedition. Magni was overcome with grief, yet he and his youngest brother, Brann, remained steadfast in their duty to the dwarven people, and the king still rules wisely with that sorrow weighing upon him. Under Magni's decree, dwarven society has turned much of its focus away from traditional commercial mining toward the unearthing of ancient history. Spurred by discoveries of strange titan relics deep beneath the earth, Magni co-founded the Explorers' League alongside his surviving brother, Brann Bronzebeard. Dwarven dig sites now dot the continents, from Dun Morogh to Kalimdor, striving to unlock the mystery of the dwarves' fabled origins. However, domestic peace remains fragile: Magni's daughter, Princess Moira, has gone missing, believed kidnapped by the hated Dark Iron clan.

npc:makaba-flathoof.text: Makaba Flathoof. Makaba Flathoof is a tauren survivor hailing from Camp Aparaje in the Stonetalon Mountains. Having witnessed the devastation of his home and people at the hands of the Grimtotem clan, he seeks brave champions of the Horde to bring vengeance upon the attackers and ensure his family's safety. Makaba Flathoof represents the tragic toll of internal strife among the tauren. His home, Camp Aparaje in the Stonetalon Mountains, fell victim to a ruthless surprise attack by the Grimtotem clan. While many tauren strive for peace and unity under the leadership of Cairne Bloodhoof, the treacherous Grimtotem continually sow discord and violence, leaving survivors like Makaba displaced and grieving.

npc:malfurion-stormrage.text: Malfurion Stormrage. Malfurion Stormrage is the first mortal druid and the revered leader of the night elves alongside High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Renowned for defeating the Burning Legion in both the War of the Ancients and the Third War, he is venerated as the Shan'do, or honored teacher. Currently, he lies trapped in a comatose slumber within the Emerald Dream, leaving the kaldorei without his waking guidance. Ten thousand years ago, before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, Malfurion studied under the demigod Cenarius. While Queen Azshara and her Highborne caste delved dangerously into the arcane energies of the Well of Eternity, Malfurion turned toward the primal forces of nature, becoming Azeroth's first mortal druid. His suspicions regarding the Highborne proved tragically correct when Azshara's reckless sorcery pierced the veil and summoned Sargeras and the Burning Legion into Azeroth, igniting the catastrophic War of the Ancients. Alongside Cenarius, Tyrande Whisperwind, and his twin brother Illidan, Malfurion spearheaded the resistance that halted the demon onslaught and closed the portal over the Well of Eternity. Following the world's shattering, Malfurion committed the druids to the Emerald Dream to rebuild and protect Azeroth's living tapestry. Ten millennia later, Tyrande awakened him from his long barrow sleep to confront Archimonde during the Third War, where he rallied the forest spirits at Mount Hyjal to shatter the Burning Legion once more. Following the Third War, Malfurion returned to his slumber within the Moonglade to commune with the Emerald Dream and replenish his spent power. However, his spirit has failed to return to his physical body, plunging him into an unnatural, comatose state. In Darnassus, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm has assumed the temporal duties of leadership among the Cenarion Circle, while Tyrande and the sisterhood watch anxiously for signs of their great Shan'do's waking.

npc:marshal-dughan.text: Marshal Dughan. Goldshire's marshal faces threats on every road and mine. Marshal Dughan commands the Stormwind Army detachment there, but kobolds, gnolls, and bandits stretch his small garrison. He depends on independent adventurers to help protect the town and nearby farms. Marshal Dughan directs Elwynn Forest's defense from Goldshire, outside the Lion's Pride Inn. Stormwind's soldiers are tied up elsewhere, while trouble grows in the woods. Kobolds crowd the mines, gnolls gather along the riverbanks, and highwaymen harass travelers on the King's Road. With too few footmen under his command, Dughan sends new recruits to reinforce outposts and scout dangerous ground. Kobolds overrun Fargodeep and Jasperlode Mines, threatening Goldshire's mineral supply. West of town, Hogger's Riverpaw gnolls press against Westbrook Garrison. Eastward, Guard Thomas reports vicious murlocs killing patrols along the river. Dughan has too few soldiers to meet each threat, so he needs capable mercenaries to help contain them.

npc:marshal-marris.text: Marshal Marris. Marshal Marris is the beleaguered military officer commanding the town watch at Lakeshire. Stationed near the town's bridge, he coordinates defense operations against the massive Blackrock orc invasion pressing down from the heights of the Redridge Mountains. With Stormwind's army absent, he relies on visiting adventurers to blunt the horde's advances. Lakeshire stands on the brink of collapse, caught between the gnolls to the west and the terrifying military might of the Blackrock clan to the east. Marshal Marris oversees the guard line at the town's primary bridge, but his resources are depleted and his soldiers are spread impossibly thin. With the kingdom of Stormwind withholding royal reinforcements, Marris carries the heavy burden of keeping the township from being overwhelmed by brute force. Recognizing that defense alone will not save Redridge, Marris orchestrates decisive offensive strikes against the orc encampments. He directs mercenaries to cull the Blackrock warriors, dismantle their shadowcasters, and ultimately hunt down Tharil'zun, the menacing commander entrenched inside the ruins of Stonewatch Keep. His orders aim to break the command structure of the orcs before an all-out assault crushes Lakeshire completely.

npc:marshal-mcbride.text: Marshal McBride. At Northshire Abbey, Marshal McBride commands Stormwind's garrison and defends the valley. Kobolds threaten its farms and mines, so he directs new recruits against them. Marshal McBride commands Stormwind's garrison outside Northshire Abbey. The abbey is a place of faith and learning, while unrest across the kingdom has left military garrisons short of soldiers. With only a handful of sworn guards, McBride must keep the valley peaceful and protect its food and resources. Green recruits arrive seeking training from the abbey's masters, and he must put them to work. Kobolds have grown more aggressive around Northshire. Once a nuisance, they have spread through the woods and seized Echo Ridge Mine, an important local resource. Short of regular soldiers, McBride calls on paladins, warriors, and other novices to drive back the tunneling kobolds and learn how far the infestation reaches before the valley is cut off.

npc:mathias-shaw.text: Mathias Shaw. In Old Town, Mathias Shaw directs SI:7, Stormwind's covert intelligence agency. From the shadows, he sends spies and scouts to guard the realm against conspiracies within and horrors beyond. Mathias Shaw leads Stormwind's spies and assassins from SI:7's hidden headquarters behind the barracks in Old Town. His covert network reaches across the Eastern Kingdoms and beyond. Loyal to the House of Wrynn, Shaw weighs every threat with care. He trusts unseen daggers and stolen messages to defend Stormwind as much as armor and palace guards. Mathias Shaw watches threats beyond the unrest in Westfall and Elwynn. Reports of strange Forsaken operations in the Eastern Plaguelands led him to send five of his finest agents to investigate. Only one came back alive, babbling about "Nathanos" and a "Blightcaller" before dying in his sleep. Shaw now depends on trusted champions to go where his scouts vanish and uncover the dangers gathering at the kingdom's borders.

npc:mathrengyl-bearwalker.text: Mathrengyl Bearwalker. Mathrengyl Bearwalker is a master druid trainer and respected elder of the Cenarion Circle residing in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. Having once served as Archdruid Fandral Staghelm's direct assistant, he guides young Alliance druids through their spiritual trials, shapeshifting rites, and duties across Kalimdor. Perched within the verdant reaches of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker stands as one of the most venerable and balanced druids on Teldrassil. He serves as a primary guide for fledgling Alliance druids, overseeing their communion with Moonglade and testing their readiness to master primal animal forms. Having undergone the intense, bewildering communion with the Great Bear Spirit in his own youth, Mathrengyl understands the weight of these rites, personally charging initiates to prove their spirit against the sacred moonkin Lunaclaw before inducting them into the path of the Druid of the Claw. Mathrengyl has long operated as Fandral Staghelm's second, managing day-to-day circle affairs and handling recruitment for the Archdruid's ambitious endeavors. When Fandral demanded vast quantities of morrowgrain, Mathrengyl organized its collection from returning adventurers, despite privately confiding a quiet unease regarding the strange plant's unnatural essence. He also coordinates Alliance responses to summons from Moonglade, navigating the delicate politics of the Cenarion Circle while Fandral turns his gaze toward southern Kalimdor. While Staghelm is infamous for his fierce pride and disdain for other races, Mathrengyl often displays a more contemplative, open mind. When relics arrived in Darnassus from the fallen druid Mulgris Deepriver—who perished fighting the Scourge in the Western Plaguelands—Mathrengyl was deeply moved to discover the investigator was a tauren. Reflecting on the Cenarion Circle's shared mission, he quietly mused that the tauren may not have drifted nearly as far from the teachings of Cenarius as the Archdruid insists.

npc:motega-firemane.text: Motega Firemane. Motega Firemane is a tauren scholar stationed at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to cataloging the dangerous wildlife of the canyon, he finds his studies disrupted by a vengeful wind serpent spirit and the reckless misadventures of his young assistant. Four years following the Third War, Motega Firemane journeyed south into Thousand Needles to observe and record the distinct beasts surviving among the towering mesas. Accompanied by his youthful assistant, Pao'ka Swiftmountain—whose protective father was reluctant to let him leave Mulgore—Motega set up camp alongside Kanati Greycloud at Whitereach Post. While his original calling was quiet natural observation, the harsh perils of the canyon floor continually demand a more martial approach to survival.

npc:onyxia.text: Onyxia. Onyxia is the broodmother of the black dragonflight and the devious daughter of Deathwing. From her lair in Dustwallow Marsh, she schemes to restore the black dragonflight's dominion over the mortal kingdoms.

npc:orgrim-doomhammer.text: Orgrim Doomhammer. Orgrim Doomhammer was the supreme Warchief of the Old Horde throughout the Second War, remembered as one of the greatest orc warriors in history. Though he died liberating the internment camps in the Arathi Highlands, his legacy endures in the capital of Orgrimmar and through Thrall, who inherited his mighty warhammer and black plate armor. Originally second-in-command to Blackhand of the Blackrock clan, Orgrim refused the demonic blood offered by Gul'dan, though he concealed his doubts beneath fierce loyalty. Near the close of the First War, disgusted by the Shadow Council's treachery and the murder of his childhood friend Durotan, Orgrim slew Blackhand in honorable combat. Assuming the mantle of Warchief, he ruthlessly purged Gul'dan's warlocks and led the Horde across the Eastern Kingdoms during the Second War. Though a devastating strategist who pushed human kingdoms to the brink of ruin, he was ultimately defeated and captured outside Blackrock Spire after the betrayal of Gul'dan split his forces. Escaping human captivity, Doomhammer lived in hiding until he met Thrall, Durotan's orphaned son. Reinvigorated by the young shaman's vision, Orgrim rallied what was left of the orcish clans to storm the internment camps and break their people free. During a fierce battle at an encampment in the Arathi Highlands, the Warchief was struck down from behind by a lance. As he lay dying, he bestowed his black plate armor, his ancestral weapon—the Doomhammer—and the title of Warchief upon Thrall. In his honor, the liberated outpost was renamed Hammerfall, and the newly founded capital in Durotar was christened Orgrimmar.

npc:ozzie-togglevolt.text: Ozzie Togglevolt. Ozzie Togglevolt is a gnome engineer and survivor of Gnomeregan's fall, currently operating out of the snowy village of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Haunted by the tragedy that struck his people, he works alongside his partner Razzle Sprysprocket to research a remedy for the irradiated leper gnomes. Ozzie Togglevolt was inside the subterranean wonders of Gnomeregan when catastrophe struck. When the toxic fallout was vented throughout the corridors to stem the trogg invasion, Ozzie stood right beside his fellow gnome, Gnoarn. A sudden radioactive discharge struck Gnoarn directly, altering him forever before Ozzie's eyes. Though Ozzie made it to the surface alive and reached the haven of Dun Morogh, the horrifying memory of that disaster never left him. Now established in Kharanos, Ozzie spends his days tinkering alongside Razzle Sprysprocket. Their primary technological and scientific endeavor remains intensely personal: finding a way to reverse the horrific mutagenic fallout of their lost home and cure the suffering leper gnomes.

npc:pelturas-whitemoon.text: Pelturas Whitemoon. Pelturas Whitemoon is a night elf father dwelling in Astranaar whose young daughter, Relara, has been struck by a terrible, corrupting illness. Desperate to save her, he works closely with local herbalist Orendil Broadleaf and traveling Alliance champions to gather sacred remedies from the surrounding wilds.
