subzone:lake-everstill.text: Lake Everstill. Lake Everstill is the expansive azure body of water dominating the heart of the Redridge Mountains, flanking the town of Lakeshire. Once celebrated for tranquil fishing and clean mountain runoff, its shores and waters have lately turned treacherous due to aggressive murloc tribes and predatory lake beasts. Spanning the central basin of Redridge, Lake Everstill provides the scenic backdrop and vital waterway for the township of Lakeshire. Its crystal-clear waters drain eastward toward the looming heights of Stonewatch. Spanned by the town's central bridge, the lake has long sustained local trade and quiet anglers, though anyone walking the shoreline today will find its peaceful reputation thoroughly shattered by encroaching wilderness threats. In recent times, hostile murlocs have established camps along the northern and eastern shallows, disrupting trade and harrying fishermen. Below the surface, aquatic hazards lurk as well, including dangerous threshers that patrol the deeper waters.

subzone:lake-falathim.text: Lake Falathim. Lake Falathim is a tranquil body of water nestled in the forested hills of western Ashenvale, southwest of Maestra's Post. Revered for the constant touch of Elune's moonlight upon its surface day and night, it was once a beloved retreat for night elves. In recent days, however, aggressive murlocs have overrun its shores, turning a sacred haven into a perilous hazard. Tucked away southeast of the Zoram Strand, Lake Falathim was long cherished by the Kaldorei as a peaceful sanctuary for swimming and fishing. According to local lore, the gentle radiance of Elune rests upon these waters at all hours, day or night. Despite this sacred blessing, ferocious murlocs have surged inland to seize the shores, nesting in thick numbers and driving away local travelers and scholars alike. The sudden occupation by murlocs has made the lake deadly to solitary wanderers. The night elf scholar Teronis was recently lost somewhere near the water's edge on a mission of inquiry. Given the savage hostility of the amphibians lurking on the banks and in the shallows, the Sentinels fear the worst for any who venture toward the moonlit pool alone.

subzone:lakeridge-highway.text: Lakeridge Highway. Lakeridge Highway is an old thoroughfare running along the southern shore of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Once a vital and heavily traveled artery prior to the First War, it has fallen into ruin and disuse. Today, roving packs of gnolls and Blackrock orcs make passage along the road perilous for travelers. Before the devastation of the First War, the Lakeridge Highway served as a bustling trade corridor through Redridge, carrying goods and folk along the southern banks of Lake Everstill. In those peaceful days, travelers could journey between the valley settlements and the eastern heights under the protection of the Kingdom of Stormwind. That safety shattered when the Horde marched through the region, leaving eastern Redridge contested and desolate. Following the seizure of Stonewatch Keep by Blackrock orcs, regular maintenance and patrols along the highway ceased entirely. The road quickly deteriorated into an overgrown track contested by savage gnoll packs. With Stormwind's military spread thin and unable to reinforce Lakeshire, the highway remains officially unsafe. Any traveler seeking to reach the eastern ridges must now carve a path through gnoll ambushes.

subzone:lakeshire.text: Lakeshire. Lakeshire is the primary human settlement in the Redridge Mountains, nestled along the northern shores of Lake Everstill. Led by Magistrate Solomon and guarded by Marshal Marris, the picturesque town is currently on the brink of collapse due to relentless assaults by Blackrock orcs, aggressive gnoll packs, and shoreline murlocs. Once a peaceful haven in the foothills east of Stormwind, Lakeshire has become the kingdom's most embattled frontier. The town's garrison at Stonewatch Keep was brutally overrun by Blackrock clan orcs sweeping down from the north, and dark wizardry has riled local Shadowhide gnoll packs into organized raiding parties. Blackrock saboteurs have even shattered parts of the Everstill Bridge, leaving Foreman Oslow and his crew struggling to repair the span while under constant threat of attack. With murlocs choking the lake's shores and gnolls stalking the high passes, Lakeshire's defenders are stretched to their breaking point.

subzone:lakeshire-inn.text: Lakeshire Inn. The Lakeshire Inn is the social hub and primary refuge in the beleaguered town of Lakeshire. Situated in the heart of the Redridge Mountains, it provides warmth, ale, and safe lodging for local townsfolk and weary travelers contending with the surrounding perils. Perched on the shore of Lake Everstill, the Lakeshire Inn offers a brief respite from the gnoll bands and Blackrock orcs pressing in on the town. Despite Lakeshire's increasingly desperate military situation, the tavern maintains a cozy, bustling atmosphere. Barkeep Daniels and Innkeeper Brianna attend to the locals and travelers, serving up flagons of ale, wine, and warm meals. It is a vital meeting point where townspeople trade news, drown their sorrows, and seek hired blades to help defend the eastern border of the kingdom. Beyond ordinary patrons nursing drinks at the counter, the inn draws a variety of colorful figures. Wiley the Black watches the room from a table, keeping his own counsel and keeping tabs on regional dangers. Traveling brewers like Yorus Barleybrew make stops here, while Darcy Parker and other townsfolk frequent the common room. For adventurers venturing further into the jagged peaks or heading south toward Duskwood, the inn is the final bastion of civilization and safety before entering contested wilderness.

subzone:lakeshire-town-hall.text: Lakeshire Town Hall. Lakeshire Town Hall serves as the administrative seat of the Redridge Mountains, standing at the heart of the lakeside settlement. Inside, Magistrate Solomon oversees local governance while wrestling with relentless threats from Blackrock orcs and gnolls. Lakeshire Town Hall is an aging stone structure that has been diligently refurbished multiple times over the years. Positioned prominently within Lakeshire, it houses Magistrate Solomon, a kind and dedicated civil leader tasked with maintaining order in the eastern reaches of the Kingdom of Stormwind. With Stormwind's military resources stretched thin and royal aid scarce, the hall has transformed from a quiet administrative office into an active command center where desperate appeals for volunteer defenders and mercenaries are processed daily. Gnoll incursions and the encroaching Blackrock orcs have pushed Solomon to desperation. With aid scarce, the magistrate readily accepts help from independent adventurers who come through the town hall doors.

subzone:library-ironforge.text: Library (Ironforge). Tucked inside the eastern wing of the Hall of Explorers, the Library serves as Ironforge's foremost repository of historical knowledge, archeological relics, and ancient lore. Maintained diligently by the Explorers' League, it houses extensive historical tomes alongside rare artifacts recovered from digs across Azeroth. Occupying a massive chamber within the Hall of Explorers, the Library is where dwarven scholars sift through the relics and field reports recovered by adventurers across the world. Administered by the Explorers' League, the shelves are packed with foundational chronicles detailing the War of the Three Hammers, the ancient Troll Wars, and the origins of the dwarven race. Inquiries regarding rare books or archival locations are directed to Librarian Mae Paledust. Beyond rows of dense bookshelves, the Library doubles as a working museum overseen by Curator Thorius. Here, physical specimens collected from deep excavations, abandoned ruins, and distant shorelines are analyzed, preserved, and displayed. The League's curators preserve everything from crude murloc idols and carved knives to mysterious relics recovered frozen in northern ice, cataloging each find to piece together the hidden history of the Titans and early Azeroth.

subzone:library-wing-northshire.text: Library Wing (Northshire). In Northshire Abbey, the Library Wing gathers scholars and new priests and mages. Its quiet southern rooms offer instruction for those joining Stormwind’s defense. The Library Wing branches south from Northshire Abbey’s Main Hall. Dusty shelves, study lecterns, and quiet alcoves fill its rooms, where aspiring mages and priests learn the Arcane and the Holy Light. Across the abbey, martial recruits drill in the Hall of Arms. Priestess Anetta guides novice priests in faith and healing, while Khelden Bremen teaches budding mages to shape primal elemental energy.

subzone:lion-s-pride-inn.text: Lion's Pride Inn. Travelers gather at the Lion's Pride Inn, Goldshire's tavern and community center in Elwynn Forest. Innkeeper Farley keeps the inn, a place to rest, meet others, and find work just south of Stormwind City. The Lion's Pride Inn anchors Goldshire at the crossroads of Elwynn Forest. Innkeeper Farley keeps it by the old motto, “Rest and relaxation for the tired and cold.” Inside, warm hearths, strong drinks, and rooms welcome weary travelers from Northshire. Goldshire sits on trade routes between Stormwind, Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood, making the inn an indispensable gathering place. Town marshals, local crafters, and seasoned trainers meet there to share news and hire passing mercenaries.

subzone:long-wash.text: Long Wash. The Long Wash is a bleak, windswept stretch of beach in Darkshore running just south of Auberdine toward the ruins of Ameth'Aran. Gloomy and scattered with marine carcasses and flotsam, the shoreline has recently grown dangerous due to an increasing presence of hostile murlocs. Despite its name, the Long Wash is actually the shortest distinct stretch of coastline in Darkshore. It sits under the region's perpetual overcast skies, an expanse of damp sand littered with flotsam, beached driftwood, and the carcasses of sea creatures washed up by the Veiled Sea. While local crabs comb through the surf, travelers southward from Auberdine must tread cautiously: murloc tribes have established camps along the water's edge, aggressively attacking anyone encroaching on their scavenged territory.

subzone:longshore.text: Longshore. Along Westfall’s western edge, Longshore’s broad sands are claimed by hostile murlocs and broken ships. Longshore runs along Westfall’s western coast, a wide stretch of unbroken sand. Travelers find little peace there. Murlocs dominate the surf, with Old Murk-Eye among the feared leaders, and sunken ships, including ruined elven destroyers, lie in the shallows. Near the south, Daphne Stilwell’s isolated farm faces Defias bandits. Across the water, the Westfall Lighthouse stands within sight.

subzone:lordamere-lake.text: Lordamere Lake. Lordamere Lake is one of the largest bodies of freshwater in the Eastern Kingdoms, bordered by Tirisfal Glades, Silverpine Forest, and the Alterac Mountains. Once the bustling aquatic heart of human civilization in the north, its cold waters and islands are now haunted by Scourge necromancers, feral murlocs, and the spreading shadow of the undead. In the golden age of the Alliance of Lordaeron, Lordamere Lake sat at the crossroads of human power. The Capital City of Lordaeron guarded its northern shores, the sorcerous city-state of Dalaran rose near its southern reach, and the kingdom of Alterac lined its mountainous eastern edge. Merchant vessels and fishing boats once crossed its broad, mist-covered expanse without fear. Following the devastation of the Third War, the lake was transformed from a hub of commerce into a natural barrier dividing the Forsaken-held lands of Tirisfal and Silverpine from the treacherous heights of Alterac. Today, navigating the dark waters of Lordamere is fraught with peril. At the center of the lake sits Fenris Isle, where the Scourge necromancer Thule Ravenclaw and his Rot Hide gnolls hold out against the Forsaken. Further east lie the Dawning Isles, completely overrun by aggressive Vile Fin murlocs. From the ruins around Dalaran to the shoreline of the Undercity, the lake is no longer a peaceful highway, but a drowned frontier contested by remnant monsters and the armies of the dead.

subzone:maclure-vineyards.text: Maclure Vineyards. In southern Elwynn, Maclure Vineyards sends grapes and wine to Stormwind. The Maclure family's estate is known as much for its bitter feud with the neighboring Stonefields as for its harvest. The Maclure Vineyards should be a peaceful haven of farming and winecraft in southern Elwynn Forest. Instead, the feud with the Stonefields down the road overshadows the family's daily labor. Accusations of theft and old resentment keep tempers high between the households. Hungry boars prowl the land, while kobolds press toward both homesteads.

subzone:maestra-s-post.text: Maestra's Post. Maestra's Post is a small Alliance settlement in western Ashenvale, perched along the road northwest of Astranaar and south of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran. Guarded by night elven Sentinels and hosting a rare human presence in Kalimdor's ancient forest, it serves as a forward watch against encroaching threats. Positioned under the canopy of western Ashenvale, Maestra's Post consists of a slender night elven tower and an open lodge. It sits as an essential waypoint for travelers marching between the coast of Darkshore and the larger hub of Astranaar. Despite its tranquil elven architecture, the outpost stands perpetually on edge. The local Sentinels keep a wary eye on the surrounding wilderness, where corrupted furbolg stir and nearby Horde movements constantly threaten the Alliance's supply lines. Unlike many insular night elf enclaves deep within the woods, Maestra's Post is notable for housing a handful of human allies. Figures such as Feero Ironhand and Delgren the Purifier dwell alongside the Sentinels here, lending their martial strength and devotion to the holy Light in service to the broader Alliance. Their presence makes this remote campsite one of the earliest meeting grounds between the eastern kingdoms and the ancient defenders of Kalimdor.

subzone:mage-quarter.text: Mage Quarter. The Mage Quarter forms the arcane heart of Stormwind City, resting across the canals in the capital's southwestern corner. Towering over its cobblestone streets and esoteric specialty shops stands the Wizard's Sanctum, where the kingdom's conjurers hone their craft. Beneath the district's scholarly surface also lie shadowy recesses, harboring practitioners of far darker arts. Reachable by bridges crossing the canals from Cathedral Square or the Trade District, the Mage Quarter caters entirely to the mystical needs of the Alliance. Centered around the spire of the Wizard's Sanctum, human and allied spellcasters gather to study the weave of arcane magic and train apprentices. The surrounding streets are crowded with purveyors of tailoring cloth, reagents, alchemical supplies, and enchanted staves, creating an insular district dedicated to research and the defense of the kingdom.

subzone:main-hall-northshire.text: Main Hall (Northshire). Newcomers report in the Main Hall at Northshire Abbey in western Elwynn. From there, they reach the Hall of Arms, the Library Wing, and the abbey tower, then receive their first assignments defending Stormwind. Trainees and clerics pass through the Main Hall after entering Northshire Abbey. The chamber links the Hall of Arms, where recruits prepare for battle, with the Library Wing and the stairs to the abbey tower. Strife in the valley reaches even this quiet place, and officers rally able newcomers to defend the kingdom's borders.

subzone:malaka-jin.text: Malaka'jin. Malaka'jin is a small Horde encampment nestled in the lower hills of the Stonetalon Mountains, just south of the Grimtotem Post. Inhabited primarily by Darkspear troll hunters, the settlement serves as a rustic waystation and hunting outpost for travelers ascending into the rugged peaks from the Barrens. Tucked away near the main path into the Stonetalon Mountains, Malaka'jin provides a welcome sanctuary for Horde wanderers venturing into contested heights. The village is home to a band of rugged troll hunters who eke out a living off the crags and scrublands. While living modestly, these hunters offer supplies, trade their fresh game to weary adventurers, and keep a wary eye on the hostile mountain wildlife and the belligerent Grimtotem tauren lurking further up the trails. Perched precariously near the boundary of the Barrens, Malaka'jin marks one of the earliest Horde presences established in Stonetalon. Though small and quiet compared to the major fortress at Sun Rock Retreat further north, it functions as a vital logistical anchor, allowing Horde trackers to monitor tribal unrest and secure the winding roads against encroaching threats.

subzone:manor-mistmantle.text: Manor Mistmantle. Manor Mistmantle is a decaying estate nestled in the shadowed hills of northeastern Duskwood, north of Darkshire. Once a proper family homestead, it has fallen into ruin and horror, crawling with undead ghouls bound to its infamous master. Located west of Beggar's Haunt, Manor Mistmantle stands as a grim monument to murder and madness. The grounds are choked with decay and prowled by vicious ghouls who defend the ruined structure. Amidst the rot and withered vegetation, the only sign of living beauty on the entire property is a solitary, sorrowful blossom growing in the untended garden: the flower known as the Tear of Tilloa.

subzone:mast-room.text: Mast Room. The Mast Room is a cavernous subterranean lumber mill nestled deep within the Deadmines. Overseen by the goblin taskmaster Sneed and his woodcarvers, this chamber processes timber stripped from Westfall to construct Edwin VanCleef's secret juggernaut.

subzone:master-s-glaive.text: Master's Glaive. The Master's Glaive is an ancient, unsettling landmark tucked into southwestern Darkshore where a colossal adamantine weapon stands impaled in a massive petrified skull. Long revered by local night elves as a sacred mystery, the site now swarms with Twilight's Hammer cultists drawn to the lingering malevolence of an ancient entity. Rising out of the Darkshore earth, the Master's Glaive is a massive adamantine blade buried deep in a colossal petrified skull. No record names the creature that died here or the hand that drove the blade home. Onu, the Ancient of Lore, says only that an old, old lord of the earth fell on this spot, and the night elves long believed that only the titans could have wielded so gigantic a weapon. Today, the impaled monolith stands as a stark, petrified monument to that forgotten struggle. Though the site was held in solemn reverence by night elves for generations, sinister forces have recently seized the grounds. Fanatics of the Twilight's Hammer cult have established a camp around the sunken carcass, carving out trenches and uncovering petrified ribs. Drawn by whispers beneath the stone, the cultists obsessively study the remains and commune with the malevolent power that still clings to the ancient remains, seeking to revive or harness whatever fell essence slumbers within the earth.

subzone:menethil-harbor.text: Menethil Harbor. Menethil Harbor is a heavily fortified dwarven port town perched on an island off the western shore of the Wetlands. Named after King Terenas Menethil II, it acts as the primary maritime lifeline connecting the Eastern Kingdoms to the distant shores of Kalimdor. Sheltered behind massive stone battlements and the sturdy towers of Menethil Keep, it is a bustling hub for merchants, off-duty soldiers, and salty adventurers. Named in tribute to King Terenas Menethil II of Lordaeron, Menethil Harbor stands as a premier Alliance haven on the Wetlands coast. Despite its remote marshland setting, it remains a heavily defended bastion, reinforced by massive walls, a single bridged causeway, and the four stone watchtowers of Menethil Keep. Today, the harbor is the grand crossroads of the Alliance. Ships steam continually across the ocean toward Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh and, by way of Southshore, Auberdine in Darkshore, carrying trade, diplomats, and off-duty Kul Tiran marines blowing their wages at the Deepwater Tavern. Yet peace is fragile here: inland supply paths through Dun Algaz are regularly contested by the Dragonmaw clan, while hostile Dark Iron raiders pressure the northern marshes, leaving Captain Stoutfist and the harbor garrison on constant alert.

subzone:military-ward.text: Military Ward. The Military Ward serves as the martial heart of Ironforge, housing the city's command infrastructure, weapons masters, and barracks. Marked by bold red banners, it is where dwarven soldiers, hunters, and siege engineers train alongside mechanized siege engines and flying machines. Situated within the northern perimeter of the mountain fortress, the Military Ward concentrates Ironforge's defensive forces into a bustling staging ground. The central complex, the Hall of Arms, accommodates warrior and hunter trainers, battlemasters, and hangars housing dwarven flying machines and steam tanks. Surrounding the drill squares and training dummies are supply outlets such as Craghelm's Plate and Chain, Goldfury's Hunting Supplies, and Timberline Arms, making the ward the primary staging point for mountaineers and city defenders. Distinguished from the pale blue of the Commons and the fiery orange of the Great Forge, the Military Ward is draped in martial red banners. Between drills and weapons inspections, soldiers and off-duty guards gather at Bruuk's Corner for an ale, while Weapon Master Buliwyf Stonehand instructs recruits in ancient dwarven martial traditions.

subzone:mirage-raceway.text: Mirage Raceway. The Mirage Raceway is an impromptu engineering proving ground situated in the shimmering salt flats of Thousand Needles. Founded on the heated rivalry between goblin tinkerer Pozzik and gnome engineer Fizzle Brassbolts, it pits high-speed rocket cars against one another across the baked earth. The track serves as a neutral gathering place where members of both the Alliance and Horde come to wager, tinker, and cheer on their favored machines. Sprawled across the vast white desert floor of the Shimmering Flats, the Mirage Raceway was born out of an unrelenting grudge match between two master tinkerers: the goblin Pozzik and the gnome Fizzle Brassbolts. Determined to settle once and for all whose race possesses superior technical ingenuity, the two constructed custom rocket-powered drag cars and recruited rival crews to pit them against each other in daily high-velocity showdowns. The relentless competition has turned the barren flats into a bustling hub of invention, sabotage, and testing as each crew desperately looks for any mechanical advantage. The raceway draws supporters from both the Horde and Alliance. Spectators gather from across Kalimdor to cheer on either gnome precision or goblin firepower, while gamblers and shady opportunists thrive on the constant wagers placed on the results. Beyond the roar of rocket thrusters, the camps serve as a busy trading depot for travelers journeying between Thousand Needles and the blazing sands of Tanaris.

subzone:mirkfallon-lake.text: Mirkfallon Lake. Mirkfallon Lake sits in a central highland basin in the Stonetalon Mountains, nestled beneath the sheer cliffs of Windshear Crag. Its waters and surrounding banks teem with native wildlife, including aggressive slimes, roaming thunder lizards, and descending wyverns. Positioned at the geographic center of the Stonetalon range, Mirkfallon Lake rests between the mountain passes leading south toward the Webwinder Path and north toward Stonetalon Peak. Fed by highland runoff, the lake offers a fertile oasis amidst the craggy peaks, drawing thunder lizards down to drink and wyverns from their roosts high above. The waters are also inhabited by strange, bubbling slimes, turning an otherwise serene mountain tarn into a hazardous crossing for lone travelers. Paths crisscross the lake basin in all directions. To the east, rocky tracks ascend into Windshear Crag and the logging operations running deep into the forested valleys. Travelers pressing north past the lake climb toward night elven sanctums and tauren heights, while those skirting south must contend with venomous spider hollows. As a result, the shores of Mirkfallon Lake often serve as an unpredictable crossing point for explorers and scouts navigating the contested mountains.

subzone:mirror-lake.text: Mirror Lake. Water spills into Mirror Lake beneath Stormwind's cliffs in northwestern Elwynn Forest, near an orchard. Defias bandits prowl the surrounding orchards, while mages watch for trouble in the forest's arcane currents. Mirror Lake lies beneath Stormwind City's walls, where fishermen and weary travelers might seek a quiet rest. Defias Brotherhood brigands stalk the surrounding orchards, making a long stay perilous for locals. Mystical disturbances across Azeroth have also begun to warp the forest's natural channels of arcane energy. Mages from the Wizard's Sanctum watch the lake closely. They send practitioners to sample its currents and guard against chaotic arcane runoff poisoning communities downstream.

subzone:mirror-lake-orchard.text: Mirror Lake Orchard. Defias bandits now hold Mirror Lake Orchard, on Mirror Lake's southern shore in western Elwynn Forest. The quiet homestead near Thunder Falls has fallen to outlaws while Stormwind's guards are stretched thin. Mirror Lake Orchard once fed a peaceful farmstead with the clean waters of Mirror Lake. Now Defias Brotherhood bandits have seized the cottage and grounds near Thunder Falls. With Stormwind's military stretched thin and King Varian Wrynn missing, rural homes across Elwynn are easy targets for outlaws seeking shelter.

subzone:mist-s-edge.text: Mist's Edge. Mist's Edge is the long, windswept coastline stretching north from Auberdine along western Darkshore. Shrouded in damp ocean fog, these gray beaches are littered with shipwrecks, colossal sea creature remains, and roving packs of crabs and murlocs. Running along the western edge of Darkshore, Mist's Edge is defined by damp sands, rocky tidepools, and perpetual coastal fog. The beach is a graveyard of the sea, littered with decaying sea behemoths, drift timber, and the shattered ribs of wrecked vessels. While seemingly barren, the coastline teems with shoreline scavengers, notably aggressive crabs and territorial murloc tribes that nest in the surf. The treacherous waters off the coast of Darkshore have claimed countless vessels, depositing shattered hulls and discarded cargo all along the sands. Night elf sentinels and local scavengers keep a wary eye on the coastline, where opportunistic murloc encampments frequently menace travelers heading up and down the coast from Auberdine.

subzone:misty-pine-refuge.text: Misty Pine Refuge. Misty Pine Refuge is a small outpost building of the Argent Dawn tucked amidst the frigid snows of central Dun Morogh. Situated amid the windswept hills of Dun Morogh, Misty Pine Refuge is an unassuming outpost of the Argent Dawn in the dwarven realm. While the surrounding crags are patrolled by Ironforge mountaineers, the refuge is home to Father Gavin, the order's lone agent here, who offers a quiet hearth amid the bitter elements and the perils that threaten the mountain roads.

subzone:mo-grosh-stronghold.text: Mo'grosh Stronghold. Mo'grosh Stronghold is a fortified den of ogres dug into the northeastern hills of Loch Modan. Nestled among ancient, weathered ruins, these brutal giants pose a constant threat to the dwarven settlements below. Tucked away in the crags of northeastern Loch Modan, Mo'grosh Stronghold serves as the primary base for the Mo'grosh clan of ogres in the region. The brute forces lurking within the caves and outer camps raid traveling dwarven supply caravans and present an enduring danger to the peace of Thelsamar. The rugged stonework scattered around the camp suggests the site once belonged to an older settlement, before the lumbering ogres claimed the territory and raised their distinctive mounds.

subzone:molsen-farm.text: Molsen Farm. Molsen Farm is an abandoned homestead located in the breadbasket region of Westfall. Once a fertile piece of farmland feeding Stormwind, it has fallen into ruin following the rise of the Defias Brotherhood and the prowling mechanical harvest golems left in their wake. Like many homesteads across Westfall, Molsen Farm stands as a casualty of the kingdom's neglect and criminal uprising. When the Defias Brotherhood took control of the countryside, the resident farmers were driven out or worse, abandoning their crops and buildings. Now, instead of laborers gathering grain, hostile mechanical Harvest Watchers and wandering outlaws scour the untended fields, making the farm a hazard to anyone traveling through the province.

subzone:moonbrook.text: Moonbrook. In southwestern Westfall, Moonbrook lies under Defias control, its streets emptied of peaceful residents. The Brotherhood uses the town as a guarded screen for its hidden headquarters in the Deadmines. Before the First War, Moonbrook stood at the heart of Westfall’s breadbasket, supporting farming families and the gold shafts of the Deadmines. The Old Horde razed the town, but it was rebuilt after the Second War. Its peace did not last. The House of Nobles in Stormwind neglected the settlement, and its military protection was stripped away. Unable to resist the red-masked bandits, Moonbrook’s people were driven from their homes. Citizens and teachers fled toward Sentinel Hill and Elwynn Forest.

subzone:moonbrook-schoolhouse.text: Moonbrook Schoolhouse. In Moonbrook's northwestern corner, the schoolhouse stands abandoned under Defias occupation. A small graveyard lies behind the hall where Stalvan Mistmantle once taught local children. Moonbrook's schoolhouse once welcomed children before ruin and bandits overtook the town. After Stalvan Mistmantle began tutoring local children, the mayor commissioned him to run a school. Students filled the hall in Moonbrook's brighter days, when the town prospered. Now outlaws occupy the abandoned building, and weathered headstones in its rear cemetery look out over Westfall's decline.

subzone:moonshrine-ruins.text: Moonshrine Ruins. The Moonshrine Ruins are a flooded expanse of ancient night elven architecture deep within Blackfathom Deeps. Once dedicated to the worship of Elune, these crumbling halls have been desecrated and seized by the Twilight's Hammer cult. Past the cavernous Pool of Ask'ar lies the Moonshrine Ruins, a somber testament to the night elves' ancient past along the Ashenvale coast. These partially submerged halls once rang with chants honoring the Moon Goddess Elune, but the Great Sundering shattered the temple and drowned its lower levels in sea water. Today, the murky waters churn with feral aquatic beasts, from aggressive crabs to serpentine threshadons, while the Twilight's Hammer cult maintains an active presence throughout the stones, bent on dark rituals that mock the shrine's sacred origin.

subzone:moonspray.text: Moonspray. The Moonspray is an Alliance transport vessel belonging to the Kaldorei Fleet. It provides essential maritime passage across the waters separating mainland Kalimdor from the great World Tree, Teldrassil. The Moonspray serves as an indispensable lifeline between the docks of Auberdine on Darkshore's coast and Rut'theran Village at the root of Teldrassil. Traversing the Veiled Sea, the transport carries adventurers, couriers, and vital provisions between the isolated night elf sanctuary in the crown of the World Tree and the ancient mainland of Kalimdor.

subzone:moonwell-ashenvale.text: Moonwell (Ashenvale). This secluded shrine, known to the night elves as the Moonwell of Purity, rests in central Ashenvale east of Iris Lake and west of Raynewood Retreat. Its blessed waters channel the grace of Elune to nourish the ancient forest and cleanse creeping foulness from the land. Alliance travelers following Raene Wolfrunner's research often seek out Shael'dryn, who keeps watch beside its tranquil basin. Tucked away beneath the canopy of central Ashenvale, this moonwell serves as a spiritual anchor for the kaldorei. Its luminescent waters tap into nature's latent magic and the light of the Moon Goddess. As the surrounding forest suffers from satyr corruption, fel taint, and logging incursions, pure shrines like this one become vital lifelines for those trying to heal the woods.

subzone:mor-shan-rampart.text: Mor'shan Rampart. The Mor'shan Rampart is a heavily fortified Horde barricade positioned at the northern border of the Barrens, guarding the entrance to Ashenvale. Constructed primarily by the Warsong clan, it shields Horde territory from night elf counterattacks while serving as a staging ground for incursions deeper into the forest. Standing at the northern terminus of the Gold Road, the Mor'shan Rampart marks the transition between the arid plains of the Barrens and the ancient canopies of Ashenvale. Built from heavy timber, defensive palisades, and fortified watchtowers, this bulwark was raised to stem the retaliatory strikes of night elven forces outraged by the Horde's logging operations. It acts both as a shield securing the northern gate to Kalimdor's interior and as a forward staging post for raiding parties pushing north toward Astranaar. Manned primarily by battle-hardened fighters affiliated with the Warsong clan, the rampart remains under constant military readiness. From these parapets, sentries monitor the tree line for night elf scouts and archers, keeping open supply lines between the frontline outposts of Ashenvale and the greater Horde settlements to the south.

subzone:mortwake-s-tower.text: Klaven's Tower. Klaven's Tower, also called the Defias Tower, is a fortified watchtower standing near the river in southeastern Westfall. Commanded by the rogue Klaven Mortwake, it serves as a critical waypoint for smuggling stolen goods across kingdom borders. Perched on the borderlands north of the Dagger Hills, Klaven's Tower is a vital hub for Defias Brotherhood operations in southern Westfall. Together with Jerod's Landing across the river in Elwynn Forest, the site acts as a receiving post and staging ground for contraband plundered from the Redridge Mountains. Its commanding vantage over the waterways allows the Brotherhood to slip supplies past Kingdom patrols, shielding their logistical network from the crown's eyes.

subzone:mystic-ward.text: Mystic Ward. The Mystic Ward is the northwestern district of Ironforge, serving as the dwarven capital's quiet sanctuary for spiritual devotion and arcane study. Distinguishable by its cool, pale blue banners and quiet halls, it stands in stark contrast to the clanging anvils of the nearby Great Forge. Its grandest structure, the Hall of Mysteries, gathers priests, paladins, and mages beneath cavernous stone arches. While dwarves are famed across Azeroth for their prowess at the forge and on the battlefield, the Mystic Ward represents the kingdom's quieter intellectual and spiritual pursuits. Marked by pale blue heraldry, this cavernous quarter connects the bustling Commons to the Forlorn Cavern and the Great Forge. Within its reaches, merchants supply scholars and spellweavers with regalia, scrolls, and alchemical reagents from shops like The Fighting Wizard and Maeva's Mystical Apparel. Dominating the district is the majestic Hall of Mysteries, where the holy disciplines of the Holy Light intersect with the practiced arts of arcane magic, offering guidance to those who wield unseen powers in defense of the Alliance.

subzone:mystral-lake.text: Mystral Lake. Mystral Lake is the largest body of water in Ashenvale, resting in the south-central forest just below Silverwind Refuge. Its deep waters draw travelers from both the Alliance and the Horde. Spanning a vast expanse south of Silverwind Refuge and east of Talondeep Vale, Mystral Lake is the largest lake in Ashenvale. The night elves keep watch over it from their outpost at Silverwind Refuge on its northern shore, and travelers from both the Horde and the Alliance frequently find their journeys pulling them to its banks. Mystral Lake draws attention across faction lines. Horde shaman traveling the path of elemental communion seek out its deep waters during their trials to understand the element of water. The raw primal resonance of the lake makes it an essential pilgrimage site for those learning to bind and respect the tidal spirits.

subzone:night-run.text: Night Run. Night Run is a small, secluded satyr outpost perched atop a cliff-ringed bluff in east-central Ashenvale. Inhabited by the demonic Felmusk satyr, it serves as a corrupted encampment harboring dark soul magic within ancient elven ruins. Night Run is the smallest and most isolated of Ashenvale's three major satyr strongholds, alongside Xavian and Satyrnaar. Sheltered among crumbling elven stonework and broken pillars, the settlement juts outward on a high ridge bounded by steep, impassable cliffs. Reaching it requires a circuitous trek along the Falfarren River near the waters of Xavian or navigating a precarious northern ledge above Raynewood Retreat. Despite its modest size, the enclave poses a severe danger: the Felmusk satyr who dwell here work in concert with the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand, anchoring twisted soulgems to pool demonic essence within the forest.

subzone:nightsong-woods.text: Nightsong Woods. Nightsong Woods forms the embattled eastern expanse of Ashenvale, reaching from Raynewood Retreat toward the borders of Azshara. It serves as the primary battleground between the night elves defending their sacred forest and the Warsong clan harvesting lumber for the Horde. Across its shadowed glades, ancient groves clash with fortified encampments amidst persistent demonic corruption. Stretching eastward across Ashenvale to Azshara, Nightsong Woods is defined by escalating violence. The Falfarren River bisects the western reaches, creating a volatile boundary between Alliance settlements and Horde encroachments. Further east, the forest fractures into heavily disputed territories where Splintertree Post coordinates Horde campaigns against the Silverwing Sentinels. Orcish axes continuously clear southern groves to fuel the Horde's expansion, leaving clear-cut swaths that infuriate the Kaldorei. Adding to the peril, satyr strongholds like Satyrnaar and Xavian, alongside demonic remnants in Demon Fall Canyon and Felfire Hill, taint the eastern canopies.

subzone:north-gate-outpost.text: North Gate Outpost. North Gate Outpost is a fortified dwarven camp situated high in the North Gate Pass of Dun Morogh. Manning the rugged route between Ironforge's snowy heartland and Loch Modan, its mountaineers guard travelers against the hostile wildlife that infests the crags. Positioned in the middle of North Gate Pass, this small settlement serves as the northeastern threshold of Dun Morogh. Dwarven mountaineers stationed here keep the main roadway cleared of prowling beasts and monitor traffic heading through the mountain tunnels into Loch Modan. The harsh climate and steep ravines make patrol duty treacherous, and the garrison frequently calls upon travelers to scout the surrounding ridges for missing patrols and dangerous predators.

subzone:north-gate-pass.text: North Gate Pass. North Gate Pass is a vital mountain thoroughfare connecting the snowy crags of Dun Morogh with the rolling basin of Loch Modan. It forms the northern corridor through the Khaz Modan peaks, watched over by a fortified dwarven outpost. Travelers heading toward the northern lowlands of the Wetlands frequently traverse this high road. Carved into the sheer stone of Khaz Modan, North Gate Pass serves as the northern arterial link between the high, frozen valleys of Dun Morogh and the temperate waters of Loch Modan. Descending through steep mountain tunnels, travelers emerging from the west are greeted by the broad expanse of the loch valley. Because it sits within easy striking distance of the paths heading down into the Wetlands, the pass carries heavy traffic of dwarven messengers, merchants, and roaming adventurers. Its strategic value is anchored by the North Gate Outpost, where mountaineers keep vigilant watch against troggs and mountain predators.

subzone:northshire-valley.text: Northshire Valley. Northshire Valley shelters Stormwind's newest defenders in northern Elwynn Forest. Natural barriers guard the peaceful valley, where ancient Northshire Abbey, fertile vineyards, and the rich Echo Ridge Mine sustain a pocket of the kingdom. Bandits, kobolds, and displaced predators now trouble its quiet pastures. Northshire Valley lies behind mountain ridges, with one road south through a fortified gatehouse toward Goldshire and the rest of Elwynn Forest. A clear river crosses the pastures and flows into Crystal Lake. At the valley's heart, ancient Northshire Abbey teaches the Holy Light and trains recruits under the Knights of the Silver Hand and seasoned veterans. Beyond its walls, the fertile Northshire Vineyards and Echo Ridge Mine make this a self-sustaining pocket of Stormwind territory, far from the wars beyond its ridges. Stormwind's overextended defenses have strained even this sheltered valley. Marshal McBride and his detachment of the Stormwind Guard struggle to maintain order across it. Wolves driven north from blighted Duskwood prowl the woods, while kobolds have overrun Echo Ridge Mine's tunnels. Masked thugs aligned with the Defias Brotherhood harass the vineyards and threaten the abbey grounds, so local commanders recruit every able-bodied civilian who arrives at the gates.

subzone:northshire-vineyards.text: Northshire Vineyards. At Northshire Vineyards, Defias brigands have seized the fields east of Northshire Abbey. The grapes once supplied wine to the clerics, but now the thieves plunder the harvest and threaten local farmers. Northshire Vineyards lie east across the stream from Northshire Abbey, where workers such as Milly Osworth once tended the fields. Defias Brotherhood brigands now hold the acreage, led by Garrick Padfoot. The thieves plunder the harvest and strip local farmers of their livelihood. Their occupation gives new Brotherhood recruits a foothold close to the abbey.

subzone:old-ironforge.text: Old Ironforge. Old Ironforge, also called the Assembly of Thanes, is an ancient subterranean chamber lying directly beneath the High Seat of Ironforge. Carved deep into the mountain's roots above glowing magma veins, it represents the ancestral heart of the dwarven capital. In the present day, its heavy access gates in the royal throne room remain sealed and vigilantly guarded. Beneath King Magni Bronzebeard's throne in the High Seat rests the cavernous hall known as Old Ironforge or the Assembly of Thanes. Deep inside these fiery subterranean foundations, winding stone bridges cross pools of subterranean lava. Long before the bustling halls of the Great Forge and the Commons echoed with modern dwarven commerce, early thanes gathered in these cavernous depths to deliberate and govern the mountain kingdom. Currently, entrance to Old Ironforge from the throne room is securely barred. The Ironforge royal guard keeps strict watch over the thresholds leading down into the old vaults.

subzone:old-town.text: Old Town. In Old Town, soldiers train beside weathered tenements and crowded alleys. The quarter largely survived the First War and remains home to Stormwind’s military Command Center and the covert headquarters of SI:7. Old Town keeps much of the shape of Stormwind before the First War. While the Stonemasons rebuilt the rest of the city from the ground up, this quarter escaped total ruin. It never gained the pristine marble facades and grand canals found in the Trade District and Cathedral Square. Working folk, laborers, and the city’s poorest residents live among its crowded tenements. Its cobbled streets are narrower, dirtier, and more chaotic than those elsewhere in the capital, preserving the feel of the old kingdom. Old Town holds Stormwind’s military officers, barracks, and combat trainers in the Command Center. Nearby, the Champions’ Hall gathers the Alliance’s finest warriors. At the district’s edge, SI:7 keeps its covert compound under the leadership of Master Mathias Shaw. Off-duty footmen and shadowy operatives meet at the Pig and Whistle Tavern, one of the city’s liveliest watering holes.

subzone:oracle-glade.text: Oracle Glade. Nestled in northwestern Teldrassil, the Oracle Glade is a sacred woodland sanctuary home to the wondrous Oracle Tree and the World Tree's premier moonwell. Despite its serene purpose as a center of communion and vigilance, the glade faces constant harassment from encroaching Bloodfeather harpies. The Oracle Glade rests quietly between Darnassus and Wellspring Lake, serving as a vital nexus of night elven communion with nature. At its center stands the Oracle Tree, an ancient specimen whose massive boughs evoke the silhouette of an eagle perched atop a bear. Nearby shimmers the first and most potent of Teldrassil's sacred moonwells, an oasis of lunar magic bathed in Elune's grace. Alongside the Circle of the Ancients, the Oracle Tree watches over the island boughs, shedding inscribed bark that acts as vital communiques to Archdruid Fandral Staghelm regarding the World Tree's health. The glade's tranquility is fragile. Aggressive Bloodfeather harpies have descended upon the grove, establishing roosts among the high branches and threatening the sacred tree. Sentinels dispatched from Darnassus struggle to root out the avian scavengers, who actively harass traveling druids and taint the natural serenity of the moonwell. Travelers passing through the northern boughs must tread lightly, as the harpies strike swiftly at any who venture near their roosts.

subzone:park.text: Park. In Stormwind's western edge, Park offers visiting night elves a haven amid the stone city. It lies between Cathedral Square and the Mage Quarter, with greenery and quiet for rest. Druid trainers here are the only ones in the Eastern Kingdoms. Stormwind's Park brings a quiet stretch of wilderness into the stone capital. Once a place for the city's people to seek recreation, it became an enclave for night elf emissaries and travelers from across the Great Sea. Shaded canopies shelter the district, and a central Moonwell stands amid its grounds. The grove offers a glimpse of Kalimdor's sacred glades in the heart of the human kingdom. Night elves have a foothold in foreign lands within the Park. Kaldorei priests such as Nara Meideros tend visiting pilgrims, while druidic mentors guide those devoted to the wild. Weary travelers can also rest from the clatter of the Trade District and the solemn duties of the Cathedral.

subzone:petitioner-s-chamber.text: Petitioner's Chamber. Petitioners wait for the crown in a chamber just inside Stormwind Keep. Nobles, church dignitaries, and visiting subjects spend the time mingling, drinking, or awaiting an audience. The Petitioner's Chamber lies just to the right as you enter Stormwind Keep. Count Remington Ridgewell and Bishop DeLavey wait there for audiences with boy-king Anduin Wrynn and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Between formal visits, the chamber gives nobles and clergy room to mingle, trade gossip, and quietly press their concerns. Who holds influence in the realm can often be seen in who speaks with whom.

subzone:pig-and-whistle-tavern.text: Pig and Whistle Tavern. In Stormwind City's Old Town, the Pig and Whistle Tavern welcomes travelers and local laborers. Veterans gather there to remember the kingdom's past conflicts. In Old Town's winding alleys, the Pig and Whistle Tavern offers warmth, ale, and lodging. Common citizens, working folk, and travelers fresh from the road gather there. Merchants such as recipe vendor Kendor Kabonka share the room with grizzled veterans, who trade memories of the First and Second Wars over their tankards.

subzone:pool-of-ask-ar.text: Pool of Ask'ar. The Pool of Ask'ar is a sprawling, submerged cavern lake located deep within Blackfathom Deeps. Teeming with aquatic beasts and foul naga invaders, its waters conceal ancient night elven architecture alongside hidden passageways that wind deeper into the corrupted sanctuary. Situated just beyond the Drowned Sacellum, the Pool of Ask'ar fills a massive subterranean vault with murky, cold water. The natural caverns and ancient stonework have become a nesting ground for oversized snapping turtles and deep-sea crabs, overseen by the enormous ancient chelonian known as Ghamoo-ra. The naga who have taken over the temple utilize this submerged threshold as a defensive staging ground, guarding the waterlogged approaches that lead deeper into the complex toward Lady Sarevess and the Moonshrine Ruins. Beyond its monstrous fauna and hostile patrols, the waters of the pool hide valuable relics from the shrine's pre-Sundering past. Submerged ledges and hidden alcoves along the cavern's edges conceal lost artifacts, including the valuable Lorgalis Manuscript sought by the dwarven scholar Gerrig Bonegrip of Ironforge. Swimming through the flooded southern passageways brings travelers out into dry tunnels guarded by vile murlocs and Old God cultists, marking the pool as the critical aquatic crossroads of Blackfathom Deeps.

subzone:pools-of-arlithrien.text: Pools of Arlithrien. The Pools of Arlithrien are a cluster of secluded springs resting in western Teldrassil, just south of the gates to Darnassus. Once a tranquil retreat centered around a sacred moonwell, the area has fallen into neglect and danger as local wildlife and nearby hostile Gnarlpine furbolgs encroached upon it. Tucked along the shaded boughs south of Darnassus, the Pools of Arlithrien were originally meant to be a quiet place of natural harmony. At their heart lies a stone moonwell, a vessel for the waters imbued with the grace of Elune. Yet despite its proximity to the night elven capital, the sanctuary has become perilous. Agitated beasts roam the shallows, and the persistent hostility of the displaced Gnarlpine furbolgs forced the night elves to abandon routine upkeep of the site, leaving a peaceful wonder shadowed by the island's growing malaise.

subzone:raven-hill.text: Raven Hill. Raven Hill is a desolate, ruined village in western Duskwood sitting in the long shadow of the vast Raven Hill Cemetery. Once a lively human settlement, it lies abandoned by all but a handful of frightened squatters and invisible spirits. Situated along the western thoroughfare of Duskwood just north of Addle's Stead, Raven Hill is a tragic shell of its former self. When dark magic and undead horrors swept through the Grand Hamlet region, the living evacuated eastward toward Darkshire or fled the territory entirely. Today, ruined timber homes rot beneath perpetual gloom, avoided by travelers who fear both the restless dead wandering down from the neighboring cemetery and the invisible Unseen lurking between the crumbling walls. Despite its bleak reputation, Raven Hill is not entirely uninhabited. A nervous wreck of an adventurer named Jitters hides among the abandoned structures, terrified of the horrors that stalk the woods. Higher up in one of the dilapidated attics, an entrepreneurial goblin named Bliztik ekes out a solitary living selling supplies to wary passersby. They share the ruins with invisible spirits known as the Unseen, living on borrowed time at the edge of the sprawling burial grounds.

subzone:raven-hill-cemetery.text: Raven Hill Cemetery. Raven Hill Cemetery is a vast, cursed graveyard stretching across the western reaches of Duskwood. Once a peaceful burial ground for local hamlets, the cemetery has been overrun by hordes of walking dead, scavenger spiders, and ruthless grave robbers. Before the darkness engulfed the Dawning Wood, Raven Hill Cemetery served as the primary resting place for the surrounding settlements. As dark sorceries fell upon the region, the dead failed to remain in their plots. Skeletons, ghouls, and shambling horrors clawed their way out of the soil, swelling the graveyard's grim boundaries. Today, it stands as one of the most perilous blights in Duskwood. The cemetery is prowled not only by rotting abominations and giant spiders, but also by desperate grave robbers eager to plunder ancestral crypts unhindered by local authorities.

subzone:ravenholdt-manor.text: Ravenholdt Manor. Tucked away high in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills, Ravenholdt Manor serves as the secluded headquarters for the guild of thieves and assassins known as Ravenholdt. Overseen by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the estate provides a discreet haven where practitioners of stealth hone their craft far from the eyes of authorities. Hidden behind a narrow mountain pass and a winding cave northwest of Durnholde Keep, Ravenholdt Manor sits isolated on the borderlands of the Alterac Mountains. The property belongs to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, a nobleman who maintains a disciplined enclave of rogues, assassins, and intelligence operatives. The grounds feature a tranquil garden and an outdoor training arena overseen by martial experts like Master Kang, providing a disciplined space to practice lockpicking, poison-crafting, and close-quarters combat. While the manor welcomes those with a talent for skullduggery, clumsy outsiders and unwanted visitors are treated with cold suspicion by the manor's watchful sentries. Prior to the First War, the land surrounding the manor was part of the kingdom of Alterac, reflected in the weathered orange tiles of the manor's roof. In the turbulent wake of Alterac's ruin, the fallen nobles of the Syndicate sought to control the region, placing them in direct conflict with Ravenholdt. For Jorach's followers, every skirmish fought across Hillsbrad and Alterac is part of a silent war to maintain their sovereign haven.

subzone:raynewood-retreat.text: Raynewood Retreat. Raynewood Retreat is an ancient night elf outpost perched around a massive great tree in north-central Ashenvale. Guarded by dryads and Cenarion protectors, it serves as a watchful sanctuary monitoring the northern passes toward corrupted Felwood. It is also the sanctuary of Keeper Ordanus, an elder son of Cenarius targeted by sinister outside forces. Nestled between Shael'dryn's moonwell and the satyr-infested ruins of Night Run, the outpost is fiercely guarded by Cenarion Protectors, faerie dragons, and Laughing Sisters. Their collective vigilance keeps a wary eye on the encroaching taint descending from Felwood just to the north.

subzone:razorfen-downs.text: Razorfen Downs. Razorfen Downs is the ancestral capital and sacred burial labyrinth of the quilboar, carved deep into the colossal brambles bordering the southern Barrens and Thousand Needles. Once their holiest sanctuary, it has fallen under the sway of the undead Scourge, transforming into a festering bastion of necromancy. Long revered as the ancestral capital city and burial grounds of the quilboar race, Razorfen Downs rests within the colossal petrified briars sprung from the fallen demigod Agamaggan. Legend holds that its arched entryway was carved directly from the Great Boar's very maw. For centuries, the high priests of the Death's Head tribe tended these deep, winding burrows and honored their revered dead. Yet despite its sacred standing among the boar-folk, the maze of bone and bramble has recently suffered a catastrophe far darker than any squabble over Barrens water.

subzone:remtravel-s-excavation.text: Remtravel's Excavation. Remtravel's Excavation is an archaeological dig site located in the southern reaches of Darkshore. Established by the dwarven Prospector Remtravel, the expedition recently struck ancient subterranean ruins, inadvertently unearthing hostile troggs and stone golems that quickly overran the quarry. Prospector Remtravel came to Darkshore in search of relics of the distant past, establishing an ambitious dig far from the safety of Auberdine. While excavating ancient strata, his team unearthed a swarm of subterranean Gravelflint troggs alongside hulking stone golems buried beneath the earth. The site was instantly transformed from a scholarly quarry into a hazard zone, scattering the miners and leaving Remtravel scrambling to retrieve his most promising findings.

subzone:render-s-rock.text: Render's Rock. Render's Rock is a cavern stronghold tucked into the northwestern crags of the Redridge Mountains, sitting near the high pass leading toward the Burning Steppes. Controlled by the fierce Blackrock orcs, it serves as a forward redoubt and an active staging ground for their raids on the valleys below. Carved into the rugged heights north of Lakeshire, Render's Rock serves as a fortified cave system for the invading Blackrock clan. From this defensible redoubt near the mountain pass to the Burning Steppes, veteran Blackrock orcs orchestrate attacks against the local defenders of Redridge. Its shadowed depths are strictly guarded, making any foray inside a perilous undertaking for those seeking to disrupt the orcish supply lines or recover captives lost in the ongoing conflict.

subzone:render-s-valley.text: Render's Valley. Render's Valley is a tucked-away encampment held by Blackrock orcs in the southeastern Redridge Mountains. Far less entrenched than the massive fortresses of Stonewatch, it nonetheless poses a persistent threat to nearby travelers and hosts captives taken from surrounding lands. Tucked among the rocky ridges southeast of Lake Everstill, Render's Valley serves as an auxiliary camp for the Blackrock orcs operating in Redridge. Unlike the heavily fortified keeps and stone towers of the northern cliffs, the valley consists of a modest cluster of war tents, banners, and sentry outposts. Despite being smaller and less armed than the clan's core forces, the warriors here raid local roads, harass travelers, and keep captured prisoners in crude cages under guard. Beyond the war parties roaming its dirt paths, the valley holds unexpected points of interest for intrepid scouts. Human prisoners have occasionally been sighted within the camp, including a captive servant connected to the Tower of Azora who managed to trade specialist goods right under his captors' noses. Additionally, rugged and unmarked pathways through the high southern bluffs behind the valley allow daring pathfinders to slip across the border into the murky bogs of the Swamp of Sorrows.

subzone:rethban-caverns.text: Rethban Caverns. Rethban Caverns is an extensive cave system tucked into the northwestern cliffs of the Redridge Mountains. Infested with aggressive Redridge gnolls, it is best known as the sole source of uncommon Rethban ore. Carved deep into the northwestern mountains overlooking Lake Everstill, Rethban Caverns serves as a fortified redoubt for the local gnolls. Under the cunning leadership of Ardo Dirtpaw, the pack fiercely guards the twisting passages and subterranean chambers, attacking any wanderers who stray too close to their hillside entrance. The caverns are best known for Rethban ore, a distinct mineral found within the rock walls and carried by the Dirtpaw pack. Blacksmiths and researchers in Lakeshire often send travelers into the dangerous, winding tunnels to recover samples of this rare mountain ore.

subzone:ridgepoint-tower.text: Ridgepoint Tower. Stormwind guards watch the eastern frontier from Ridgepoint Tower. They keep vigil over the perilous corridors, valleys, and roads leading into neighboring wilderness. At Ridgepoint Tower, the garrison watches the valleys and roads of eastern Elwynn. The tower stands on high ground, where Stormwind's authority reaches its eastern border and the wilds begin. Its guards keep watch over the routes before threats can reach the farms and settlements nearer Northshire and Goldshire. Ridgepoint Tower faces threats from several directions. East lie the Redridge Mountains, where aggressive gnoll packs and blackrock orc raiders test human defenses. Across the southern river, undead horrors prowl the timberline of Duskwood. Rogue Defias Brotherhood bandits also haunt nearby wilderness camps, looking for gaps in the guard's defenses.

subzone:roland-s-doom.text: Roland's Doom. Roland's Doom is an abandoned, shadow-drenched mine tucked into the southeastern hills of Duskwood, just east of the Rotting Orchard. Once an ordinary delve, it has become infamous as a dangerous den overrun by savage worgen. Cut into the ridges east of the Rotting Orchard, Roland's Doom long ago ceased to be a functioning mine. Instead, it serves as a violent staging ground for the Nightbane worgen pack, led by beasts such as Gutspill and Nefaru. The dark tunnels echo with guttural snarls and the reek of damp earth and blood, making it one of the most perilous corners in all of Duskwood for unwary travelers.

subzone:rotting-orchard.text: Rotting Orchard. The Rotting Orchard is a blighted, abandoned fruit grove situated in southern Duskwood. Once a source of harvest for the nearby settlement of Darkshire, it has fallen into ruin and is now overrun by ravenous lupine predators known as the Nightbane pack. Located east of the ruined Yorgen Farmstead and west of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, the Rotting Orchard stands as a grim testament to Duskwood's decline. The trees hang heavy with withered, spoiled fruit, while dilapidated barns and outbuildings have been converted into rough encampments by the Nightbane worgen. Nightbane Stalkers prowl the twisted brush, while dark casters known as Shadow Weavers weave their sinister magic amid the decaying timber. The pack answers to the fierce worgen Gutspill and Nefaru, who lair in the nearby mine of Roland's Doom.

subzone:royal-gallery.text: Royal Gallery. Stormwind Keep's Royal Gallery honors figures from the kingdom's history and the Grand Alliance. Past the courtyard garden, its statues and works of art fill a quiet hall of remembrance. The Royal Gallery lies beyond Stormwind Keep's interior garden, beside the Royal Library. Its statues honor King Llane Wrynn, the fallen ruler of Stormwind; Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras; and Lady Mara Fordragon, patron of the refugees who fled to Lordaeron after the First War. Courtly visitors such as Lady Dena Kennedy come to this quiet hall, where the kingdom's noble heritage is remembered.

subzone:royal-library.text: Royal Library. Scholars come to the Royal Library in Stormwind Keep for the kingdom’s records and histories. Head Librarian Milton Sheaf watches over its scrolls and treatises, from ancient wars to accounts of realms beyond the sea. The Royal Library offers quiet among Stormwind Keep’s guarded halls and courtly intrigues. Milton Sheaf oversees its shelves of southern human history, from surviving texts written before the First War to recent military chronicles and recovered tomes. Alliance scholars, priests, and travelers may browse its treatises. They cover the founding of the Alliance of Lordaeron and the recent arrival of Thrall’s Horde in Kalimdor.

subzone:ruins-of-mathystra.text: Ruins of Mathystra. The Ruins of Mathystra are the crumbled remnants of an ancient night elven city sitting along the northern coast of Darkshore. Shattered during the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago, the coastal ruins are now overrun by hostile Stormscale naga and prowled by elusive Ghost Sabers. Ten millennia ago, Mathystra stood as a bustling night elven settlement, home to high-ranking Highborne nobility. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, cataclysmic waves shattered the coastal city, toppling its grand marble arches and washing much of its stonework into the sea. The surviving night elves abandoned the ruined city in favor of smaller woodland villages further south, leaving Mathystra's sunken courtyards and cracked foundations to the relentless coastal elements. In the modern era, Mathystra has become a dangerous domain ruled by the Stormscale naga. Creeping up from the dark depths, these serpentine abominations guard the broken halls fiercely, driving away any travelers who venture north past the Tower of Althalaxx. Among the shattered flagstones, ancient Highborne relics still lie half-buried in sand and seafoam. Daring young night elves sometimes brave the naga vipers hoping to recover remnants of their lost heritage, often contending not only with serpent blades but also with the spectral Ghost Sabers that stalk the broken streets.

subzone:ruins-of-ordil-aran.text: Ruins of Ordil'Aran. The Ruins of Ordil'Aran are the crumbling remnants of an ancient night elf settlement in northwestern Ashenvale, situated between Maestra's Post and Bathran's Haunt. Once a hidden redoubt for shadow cultists, the fallen stones have recently been overrun by the corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs. Little remains of the original Kaldorei architecture at Ordil'Aran save for weathered pillars, cracked arches, and moss-draped stonework. For a time, the isolated ruins served as a lair for the Cult of the Dark Strand, who lurked among the debris to ambush travelers along the northwestern paths of Ashenvale. Recently, however, violent furbolgs of the Thistlefur tribe drove out the cultists in a bloody takeover. The bodies of fallen Dark Strand practitioners still litter the ground while aggressive furbolgs patrol the perimeter, fiercely guarding the site and the ancient Heartswood tree growing within.

subzone:ruins-of-stardust.text: Ruins of Stardust. The Ruins of Stardust are an ancient, fallen night elven holy sanctuary nestled on a lake island in southwestern Ashenvale. Once a serene place of worship, the island's waters and native bog beasts have suffered corruption from demonic rot washing down from Felwood. Despite this pervasive blight, luminous stardust shrubs still thrive amidst the crumbling stones, retaining potent restorative power. Resting on a solitary island south of Astranaar, the Ruins of Stardust were once a venerated night elf holy site. Today, an eerie, sickly yellowish-green hue hangs over the water—a consequence of foul demonic rot draining south from Felwood, much like at nearby Iris Lake. The local plant life has twisted into hostile bog beasts that prowl the fallen masonry, their temperaments warped by the tainted lake. Despite the corruption saturating the soil and shoreline, the island possesses an unyielding spark of resilience. Scattered among the ruins are stardust shrubs, blooming unmarred by the demonic taint. Their leaves and blossoms hold remarkable cleansing and healing virtues, attracting shamans, herbalists, and local night elf defenders seeking remedies against Ashenvale's encroaching decay.

subzone:rut-theran-village.text: Rut'theran Village. Rut'theran Village is a coastal haven nestled at the southern base of Teldrassil. Serving as the primary maritime harbor for Darnassus, it connects the secluded World Tree to the mainland of Kalimdor via ferry and hippogryph routes. Perched at the water's edge below the towering heights of Teldrassil, Rut'theran Village acts as the threshold between the night elven capital and the wider world. While Darnassus rests within the boughs high above, Rut'theran provides the logistical foundation required to sustain it. A mystical portal arches beneath the trees, whisking travelers between the shore and Darnassus in an instant. For journeys across the sea, ferry service runs from the village docks directly to Auberdine on the mainland of Darkshore, accompanied by flight masters tending dedicated roosts of trained hippogryphs.

subzone:saldean-s-farm.text: Saldean's Farm. At Saldean's Farm, the Saldeans hold Westfall's only homestead not completely overrun and abandoned to the Defias Brotherhood. Farmer Saldean and his wife Salma keep the farmhouse as a rare safe haven amid the region's turmoil. The Saldean family stayed on their soil as neighboring lands fell to banditry and mechanical sabotage. Farmer Saldean and his wife Salma still offer hot food and a kind word to travelers. Rogue harvest golems deployed across the plains plague their fields, so the family keeps close to the farmhouse walls. Stormwind's crown has largely neglected Westfall, leaving law enforcement thin. A handful of Sentinel Hill and Stormwind guards patrol the periphery, but the Saldeans rely chiefly on their own grit and help from passing travelers. Salma's famous Westfall stew and goretusk liver pie, and the shelter of the farmhouse, offer small comforts against the Defias threat.

subzone:satyrnaar.text: Satyrnaar. Satyrnaar is an ancient, ruined night elf settlement in northeastern Ashenvale that has fallen entirely into the hands of the Bleakheart satyrs. Perched just off the main road between Splintertree Post and Azshara, it is the most intact and easily accessible of the satyr strongholds in the forest. Located northeast of Splintertree Post and southwest of Forest Song, Satyrnaar stands as one of Ashenvale's three primary satyr settlements alongside Xavian and Night Run. Unlike the deeper wilderness ruins, Satyrnaar is relatively well-preserved, featuring pitched tents nestled among crumbled elven architecture. It serves as a bustling camp for the Bleakheart satyrs, making the nearby trade route fraught with peril for travelers moving east toward Azshara. Furthermore, dark ties fester here: the satyrs have forged an alliance with the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand, harboring one of their insidious soulgems amidst the corrupted stones.

subzone:scarlet-raven-tavern.text: Scarlet Raven Tavern. The Scarlet Raven Tavern is the social center and primary inn of Darkshire, offering hearthside shelter in the gloom of Duskwood. Presided over by Tavernkeep Smitts, it serves as a gathering spot for beleaguered locals, passing adventurers, and terrified travelers trying to escape the horrors lurking beyond the town's perimeter. Standing near the heart of Darkshire, the Scarlet Raven Tavern keeps its hearth ablaze while eternal dusk chokes the surrounding forest. Years ago, it was a bustling stop where Marshal Haggard and the Stormwind Guard would share pints after patrols. Today, business has withered alongside the town's security. Tavernkeep Smitts tends bar for a somber, anxious clientele huddled against the cold and fear. Even so, the tavern remains an indispensable crossroads for rumors, serving as the starting point for travelers seeking answers to the dark phenomena consuming the region.

subzone:sentinel-hill.text: Sentinel Hill. In Westfall, Sentinel Hill remains the Alliance's main stronghold and the People's Militia's command post. Overgrown fields, scavenging gnolls, and hostile outlaws surround the rise, the only secure foothold for lawful citizens in the region. Sentinel Hill rises above central Westfall, with a barracks-style inn, a gryphon roost linking travelers to Stormwind and beyond, a forge, and a lumber mill around Sentinel Tower. Overgrown fields, scavenging gnolls, and outlaws crowd the surrounding land. The encampment keeps a fragile perimeter where travelers, beleaguered farmers, and recruits can regroup under the watchful eyes of veteran defenders. With the royal army detained in Stormwind and unable to spare soldiers for outlying territories, Gryan Stoutmantle established the People's Militia on Sentinel Hill. Volunteer fighters organize scouts, coordinate strikes against the Riverpaw gnolls, and investigate the organized banditry tearing through Westfall's abandoned farmsteads. The camp is neither an opulent fort nor a comfortable refuge; it is a working frontline camp determined to reclaim the kingdom's former breadbasket.

subzone:sentinel-tower.text: Sentinel Tower. Defenders watch Westfall from Sentinel Tower atop Sentinel Hill. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia organize resistance against bandits, gnolls, and the Defias Brotherhood. Sentinel Tower rises above the unsettled plains of Westfall. With Stormwind's official army largely absent and aid withheld, local volunteers and veterans joined together around this central stronghold. From its stone heights, lookouts can see across the dusty plains, from abandoned pumpkin patches to the misty shores. They watch for highwaymen and gnoll raiding parties moving through the region. Gryan Stoutmantle and the local leadership direct the militia from Sentinel Tower. Makeshift defenses surround the stronghold, where wounded refugees and weary soldiers gather, and homesteaders driven from their lands find emergency shelter. Militia members piece together reports about the Defias Brotherhood and organize volunteers into strikes against the syndicate that has brought Westfall to ruin.

subzone:shadowthread-cave.text: Shadowthread Cave. Shadowthread Cave is a damp cavern carved into the northwest cliffs of Shadowglen on Teldrassil. Traditionally inhabited by indigenous Webwood spiders, the cave has recently turned dangerously aggressive under the dominion of their broodmother, Githyiss the Vile. Tucked away in the shaded perimeter of Shadowglen, Shadowthread Cave has long served as a natural lair for Teldrassil's giant spiders. In earlier years, these arachnids coexisted quietly alongside the nascent boughs of the World Tree. Recently, however, their temperament has turned fiercely territorial. Thick layers of webwood silk now choke the stone corridors, and the aggressive nature of the brood poses an immediate hazard to young kaldorei taking their first steps beyond Aldrassil. The primary menace lurking deep within the cave's darkest recesses is Githyiss the Vile, a monstrous broodmother whose ferocity far outstrips the common webwood crawlers. Novice night elf sentinels and druids are dispatched to the cave to curb the spider infestation and slay Githyiss, ensuring that the corruption touching Teldrassil's wildlife does not overrun the sanctuary of Shadowglen entirely.

subzone:shimmer-ridge.text: Shimmer Ridge. Shimmer Ridge is a rugged highland nestled in northern Dun Morogh, directly west of the Gates of Ironforge. Occupied by hostile Frostmane trolls, the rocky heights consist of two camps joined by a rickety bridge and are renowned as the sole harvesting ground for potent shimmerweed. Perched along the craggy slopes just west of Ironforge's mighty entryway, Shimmer Ridge serves as an active redoubt for the Frostmane troll tribe. Divided into twin camps straddling a chasm and linked by a wooden span, the enclave is heavily guarded by troll scavengers and their tamed mountain boars. Their proximity to the main roadway and the dwarven capital poses a continuous nuisance to travelers and mountain patrols, who must constantly remain on guard against opportunistic raids from the high ground. Aside from strategic positioning, the ridge is famous for cultivating shimmerweed, a plant grown by the Frostmane trolls. Prized by local dwarven brewmasters for crafting potent, flavorful highland ales, the herb cannot easily be gathered elsewhere. Daring mountaineers and young recruits frequently risk Frostmane ambushes and savage tusked beasts simply to harvest fresh baskets of the precious botanical directly from the trolls' plots.

subzone:shimmering-flats.text: Shimmering Flats. The Shimmering Flats is an expansive salt flat lying at the southeastern tip of Thousand Needles, bordering the desert of Tanaris. Once the bed of an ancient lake, this sun-baked expanse is now famous for the high-speed mechanical rivalries of the Mirage Raceway and a harsh population of desert beasts. Stretching out under the blinding southern sun, the Shimmering Flats is a vast dried lakebed devoid of vegetation, dotted with the sun-bleached bones of turtles and even the wooden wreck of an ancient sailing vessel. Its sheer, unbroken level surface makes it the premier testing ground on Kalimdor for experimental vehicles. At the center of the flats lies the Mirage Raceway, where gnome and goblin tinkerers constantly clash to see whose rocket cars, gyrocopters, and engines can achieve the highest speeds—often resulting in fiery crashes and smoking craters across the white crust. Beyond the roaring engines of the raceway, the basin is far from peaceful. Hardened basilisks, aggressive scorpids, and circling vultures prey upon anything that slows down on the open expanse. Further south, the ground grows treacherous around the Rustmaul Dig Site. Originally excavated by dwarven prospectors before being contested by the Horde, the quarry was entirely abandoned when picks cracked into subterranean tunnels, unleashing a swarm of vicious silithid into the southern edge of the flats.

subzone:shrine-of-aessina.text: Shrine of Aessina. The Shrine of Aessina is a sacred elven landmark nestled in the forests of southwestern Ashenvale, dedicated to the ancient forest spirit of nature and wild creatures. Located between Maestra's Post and Astranaar, it stands as a serene sanctuary amidst the growing border friction in the region. Tucked away west of Astranaar, the Shrine of Aessina honors the mysterious Wild God who embodies the heart and spirit of the deep forests. For generations, night elves and their woodland kin have revered this quiet place, communing with nature away from the bustling main roads. However, with the Horde pushing into Ashenvale to gather timber and establish footholds, sacred grounds throughout the territory face an uncertain peace.

subzone:si-7-stormwind-city.text: SI:7 (Stormwind City). Tucked away in the eastern corner of Old Town, this unassuming stone manor houses the headquarters of SI:7, the kingdom of Stormwind's elite intelligence and espionage service. Behind its heavy doors, spymaster Master Mathias Shaw and his senior operatives quietly monitor threats to the realm, coordinating undercover agents across the kingdom. To the casual passerby in Old Town, this fortified stone structure looks little different from a standard manor or military barracks. In truth, it serves as the nerve center for Stormwind Intelligence, Section 7. Directed by Master Mathias Shaw, SI:7 gathers intelligence, conducts surveillance, and executes covert operations to protect the kingdom from subversion. While the city guard patrols the open cobblestones and the Royal Guard defends Stormwind Keep, SI:7 works in the margins, training handlers and dispatching stealthy operatives against foreign enemies, saboteurs, and domestic unrest alike.

subzone:silver-stream-mine.text: Silver Stream Mine. Silver Stream Mine is a depleted dwarf mine located in northern Loch Modan, nestled between Algaz Station and the Stonewrought Dam. Once a rich silver vein for the kingdom of Ironforge, the excavated hollow was repurposed as a Miners' League supply depot before being overrun by vermin. Today, Tunnel Rat kobolds squat inside the tunnels, hoarding stolen equipment and rare mineral curiosities. Silver Stream Mine once flowed with precious ore, contributing heavily to the silver reserves of Ironforge. In time, the dwarf pickaxes dug deep enough to exhaust the primary veins, turning the sprawling chambers into an empty subterranean complex. Rather than abandon the hard-won earthworks, the Miners' League transformed the shafts into a secure storage depot for tools, mining crates, and regional equipment. It also serves as the only known source of rare Charged Rift Gems, which draw inquisitive arcanists searching for delicate tailoring reagents. The quiet depot did not remain secure for long.
