Aggressive Tunnel Rat kobolds, drawn by the smell of unattended tools, candle wax, and forgotten subterranean crevices, swarmed the shafts in large numbers. The Miners' League caretakers were promptly driven out into the Loch Modan cold. Now, the kobolds guard the stolen dwarf crates with manic fervor, while old, shattered orcish catapults and wagons rest forgotten outside the rear entrances, silent reminders of older frontier skirmishes.

subzone:silverwind-refuge.text: Silverwind Refuge. Silverwind Refuge is a serene night elven settlement nestled in south-central Ashenvale, situated just north of Mystral Lake. Protected by Sentinels, it offers a welcoming haven for travelers along the forest's wooded trails. Resting between the placid waters of Mystral Lake and Iris Lake to the north, Silverwind Refuge stands as one of the major night elven waystations in central Ashenvale alongside Astranaar. It boasts craftsmen and wilderness trainers who instruct travelers in herbalism, alchemy, skinning, and hunting. Guarded by stalwart Sentinels, the retreat serves as a peaceful rest stop for allies moving through the shaded ancient woods.

subzone:silverwing-grove.text: Silverwing Grove. Tucked away in south-central Ashenvale near Fallen Sky Lake, Silverwing Grove serves as the staging grounds for the Silverwing Sentinels. From this fortified hollow, night elf warriors muster Alliance forces to push back the Warsong Clan loggers tearing through the forest. Hidden beneath the emerald canopy southwest of Silverwing Outpost, Silverwing Grove is a crucial military staging post for the Silverwing Sentinels. Rather than a tranquil woodland retreat, it functions as the operational heartbeat for the night elves' bitter territorial contest against the Horde's lumber operations in Warsong Gulch. High-ranking Alliance officers, provisions, and scouts gather here, organizing skirmishes and marshaling champions to defend ancient Ashenvale against orcish expansion.

subzone:silverwing-outpost.text: Silverwing Outpost. Silverwing Outpost is a fortified night elf garrison positioned in south-central Ashenvale, east of the Falfarren River. Commanded by Duriel Moonfire, it stands as the easternmost bastion of the Alliance against the Horde in the contested woodland. Situated southwest of Splintertree Post and just north of the border with the Barrens, Silverwing Outpost holds an inherently perilous strategic position. By sitting on the eastern side of the Falfarren River—territory heavily contested and patrolled by the Horde—the outpost serves as a direct shield for night elf holdings deeper in the forest. Duriel Moonfire and her Silverwing Sentinels remain under constant siege from nearby orcs determined to purge night elf forces from the area entirely.

subzone:sishir-canyon.text: Sishir Canyon. Sishir Canyon is a rugged gorge in the Stonetalon Mountains, carving an eastward path through the craggy heights. Thickly swarmed by monstrous Deepmoss spiders and choked in webbing, it serves as the dangerous approach to the Ruins of Eldre'thar. Travelers who brave its tangled depths must contend with venomous arachnids and their brooding matriarch. Branching off the mountain roads of the Stonetalon range, Sishir Canyon is a treacherous natural corridor cutting toward the ancient Ruins of Eldre'thar. Rather than a quiet mountain trail, the gorge has been thoroughly overrun by Deepmoss spiders. Their sticky silken sheets and clusters of egg sacs smother the stony ground and rock walls, transforming the ravine into a living nest. Travelers and sentinels seeking the night elven ruins beyond must cut their way through swarms of aggressive webspinners. Lurking in the deepest recess of the canyon is Besseleth, the massive and deadly matriarch of the Deepmoss brood. Her venom and monstrous size make her a terror to anyone attempting to secure the pass. Local forces in Stonetalon keep a wary watch on the canyon, warning adventurers that venturing into the webbed recesses means facing not just scattered spiders, but an apex predator fiercely guarding her brood.

subzone:slaughtered-lamb.text: Slaughtered Lamb. Tucked away in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, the Slaughtered Lamb appears to be nothing more than a quiet, seedy tavern. Beneath its floorboards, however, sprawling catacombs hide the sanctum and training grounds of the Alliance's illicit warlocks. On the surface, the Slaughtered Lamb offers little more than dark corners and sparse patronage, attended by barkeep Jarel Moor, who warns casual visitors to stay away from the shadows. That warning is literal. Descending through the back passages reveals a subterranean complex of crypts and summoning circles, where human warlocks and transfer practitioners from Khaz Modan openly study fel arcana sheltered from the disapproving eyes of the Church of the Holy Light and the Kirin Tor.

subzone:south-gate-outpost.text: South Gate Outpost. South Gate Outpost is a fortified dwarven mountain post situated along the South Gate Pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Manning the snowy southern road, its mountaineers guard the steady flow of travelers walking between Ironforge's frigid heights and the temperate valley of the Loch. Perched midway through the high mountain cut of South Gate Pass, South Gate Outpost marks the frontier between the snowy slopes of Dun Morogh and the verdant basin of Loch Modan. Stationed here are Ironforge mountaineers tasked with patrolling the rocky switchbacks and keeping dangerous wildlife off the main highway. Compared to their hard-pressed kin up at North Gate Outpost, the defenders here have largely secured their stretch of road, allowing travelers, pilgrims, and trade wagons headed toward Thelsamar to journey in relative safety.

subzone:south-gate-pass.text: South Gate Pass. South Gate Pass is the primary mountain thoroughfare linking the snowy heights of Dun Morogh with the valley basin of Loch Modan. Flanked by dwarven tunnels and watch posts, it serves as the most direct route between Ironforge and the settlement of Thelsamar. Carved straight through the Khaz Modan range, South Gate Pass connects Dun Morogh's high mountains to the rolling valley of Loch Modan to the east. Travelers leaving the cold slopes behind emerge through stone archways into the warmer dwarven heartlands. Because the path leads straight toward Thelsamar, it carries a steady flow of mountaineers, couriers, and newly trained adventurers setting out from the capital. The pass is fortified against wild beasts and prowling troggs by the South Gate Outpost, where dwarven mountaineers maintain a constant watch. Though generally safer than the untamed wilds deeper in the valley, travelers are advised to keep to the road, as hostile wildlife and roving threats frequently probe the approaches.

subzone:southshore.text: Southshore. Southshore is a coastal human port in the Hillsbrad Foothills and one of the Alliance's few surviving strongholds in fallen Lordaeron. Once a sleepy fishing village, it now stands as an embattled bastion facing constant hostility from the Forsaken garrison at Tarren Mill, rogue Syndicate bandits, and shoreline monsters. Southshore first rose to prominence during the First War when refugee boats carrying survivors from the fallen kingdom of Stormwind landed upon its beaches. Though contested and overrun during the Second War, it was rebuilt and later endured the horrors of the Third War. Today, while the rest of Lordaeron lies in ruins or under the rule of the Forsaken, Southshore remains fiercely loyal to the Grand Alliance. It offers shelter to displaced human survivors, veteran paladins of the Silver Hand, and scholars of the Kirin Tor. Despite its scenic docks, where the ship between Menethil Harbor and Auberdine calls, and its famous turtle bisque, life in Southshore is perilous. Led by Magistrate Henry Maleb and Marshal Redpath, the town struggles against relentless pressure. To the north, the Forsaken of Tarren Mill wage a bitter border conflict for dominance over Hillsbrad. Inland, the aristocratic outlaws of the Syndicate raid supply lines and assassinate local leaders, while ogres, murlocs, and naga constantly harass the town's borders.

subzone:splintertree-post.text: Splintertree Post. Splintertree Post is the primary Horde fortress in eastern Ashenvale, situated northwest of Felfire Hill. Established by Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan during the Third War, it serves as a heavily fortified bulwark against the night elves and a staging ground for territorial expansion. Carved straight out of the ancient woodlands, Splintertree Post serves as the Horde's main military and logistical hub across eastern Ashenvale. Originally established by Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan when orcs first pressed into the forest during the Third War, it remains a heavily armed enclave defended primarily by orcish and tauren scouts and warriors. Armed with a flight master, an inn, and steady supply lines to Orgrimmar, it anchors the Horde's contested presence beneath the canopy. Splintertree Post exists in a state of perpetual readiness. The night elves have neither forgotten nor forgiven Grommash's actions during the war, nor do they tolerate ongoing orcish logging and raids against Astranaar. As a result, the settlement faces constant retaliatory strikes and guerilla attacks from the Sentinels hiding in the surrounding timber, testing the garrison's watchmen at all hours.

subzone:splithoof-crag.text: Splithoof Crag. Splithoof Crag is a fortified settlement of the Galak centaur, tucked along the northern cliffs of Thousand Needles. It serves as one of the tribe's major enclaves alongside the high mesas, guarding the entrance to Splithoof Hold. Travelers traversing the canyon floor must contend with aggressive Galak patrols roaming near the bluffs. Nestled against the sheer northern rock face of Thousand Needles, Splithoof Crag sits just east of the towering Darkcloud Pinnacle. It is an established enclave of the Galak centaur, complete with crude tent encampments and dirt pathways cutting through the crags. At the heart of the village against the cliffside lies Splithoof Hold, a subterranean cavern holding the Cloven Hoof, an ancient relic of the centaur safeguarded by a sacred brazier. The Galak fiercely contest this corner of the canyon, clashing with any travelers, Horde expeditions, or tauren scouting parties wandering beneath their bluffs. While the Grimtotem occupy the soaring pinnacles nearby, the centaur hold firm control of this canyon ravine and the caverns burrowed deep beneath the stone.

subzone:splithoof-hold.text: Splithoof Hold. Splithoof Hold is a deep cavern stronghold carved into the stone of Splithoof Crag in Thousand Needles. Held by the Galak centaur tribe, the cavern serves as a fortified den and houses the Ancient Brazier, a site holding an eternally burning sacred flame. Tucked away inside Splithoof Crag, Splithoof Hold serves as a fortified redoubt for the Galak centaur. Unlike the windswept canyon floor, this enclosed cave offers them shelter, defensible chokepoints, and a secure sanctuary from rival tribes and travelers passing through the Needles. Deep within the shadowed recesses of the hold lies an ancient brazier cradling the Sacred Flame. This mystic fire burns incessantly, serving as a focal point of power and ritual reverence for the centaur and an object of deep curiosity for spiritual wanderers across the canyon.

subzone:starbreeze-village.text: Starbreeze Village. Starbreeze Village is an abandoned night elf settlement situated east of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a tranquil woodland hamlet, it has recently fallen to the maddened furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe. The ruined settlement now stands as a glaring symbol of the growing corruption seeping into the roots of the World Tree. Located southeast of Shadowglen and just down the road from Dolanaar, Starbreeze Village was once home to peaceful night elf families living beneath the boughs of Teldrassil. Today, the village lies in shambles, its wooden structures overrun by aggressive Gnarlpine furbolgs. Driven wild by a sinister corruption afflicting the boughs of the World Tree, the beast-men drove the elven residents out and now defend the ruined grounds ferociously.

subzone:steelgrill-s-depot.text: Steelgrill's Depot. Steelgrill's Depot is a bustling engineering workshop and repair station situated directly east of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Overseen by Beldin Steelgrill and a crew of craftsmen, it serves as a frontline hub for vehicle maintenance, tinker supply runs, and salvage efforts. Nestled just off the snowy road east of Kharanos, Steelgrill's Depot buzzes with the clamor of clanking metal, hissing steam vents, and the hum of experimental engines. Dwarven miners and eccentric gnome engineers gather here amid heavy machinery, mechanized walking frames, and stockpiles of raw ores hauled out from nearby quarries. With Dun Morogh facing relentless trogg disruptions and mechanical supply shortages, Beldin Steelgrill and his crew keep Alliance machinery in working order, serving as an indispensable stop for travelers seeking spare parts or technical guidance in the bitter cold.

subzone:stendel-s-pond.text: Stendel's Pond. Gnolls prowl Stendel's Pond southwest of Sentinel Hill, where anglers still seek fresh fish. Southwest of Sentinel Hill, Stendel's Pond draws anglers despite the danger along its muddy banks. Gnolls roam nearby, and scattered skeletons with two lone graves show that the shore is perilous. The water may be foul, or the beasts may be to blame, but the cause is unknown. Schools of sagefish still bring anglers to the pond.

subzone:stone-cairn-lake.text: Stone Cairn Lake. At Stone Cairn Lake in northeastern Elwynn, hostile murlocs hold the southern shore and renegade wizards camp on the island. Heroes' Vigil honors those lost in the First War. Families and pilgrims once crossed the calm waters to honor the dead at Heroes' Vigil. The stone memorial was raised on the lake's central island to mark the heavy loss of human life in the First War against the Orcish Horde. Now renegade wizards have made camp beside the monument, and the island has become a hostile place. Aggressive murlocs have claimed the southern banks of Stone Cairn Lake. Their crude huts line the water, and they harass anyone who comes near. The hills and rocky outcrops around the lake hold rich mineral veins, drawing prospectors and miners despite the dangers along the shore.

subzone:stonefield-farm.text: Stonefield Farm. The Stonefield family works the fields in southern Elwynn Forest. Their long feud with the neighboring Maclures keeps the two households at odds. Stonefield Farm lies south of Goldshire, where the family grows crops for the realm. For decades, the Stonefields have quarreled with the nearby Maclure Vineyards. The households trade accusations of theft and trespassing, and even small disputes keep tensions high. Gramma Stonefield, Ma Stonefield, and young Tommy Joe Stonefield make their home here.

subzone:stonefire-tavern.text: Stonefire Tavern. The Stonefire Tavern is the primary inn serving travelers inside the mountain city of Ironforge. Situated in the bustling Commons district just north of the city gates, it provides a warm hearth, strong dwarven ale, and a resting place for adventurers arriving from across Khaz Modan. Located immediately north of the fortress gates in the Commons, the Stonefire Tavern serves as the premier public house in Ironforge. Run by Innkeeper Firebrew alongside his daughter Gwenna, the inn offers weary wayfarers hearty meals, local brews, and lodging beneath the mountain. Whether seeking respite from the harsh mountain snows of Dun Morogh or looking to trade tales and supplies before venturing deep into the city, travelers from all corners of the Alliance routinely gather around its roaring hearth.

subzone:stonesplinter-valley.text: Stonesplinter Valley. Stonesplinter Valley is a rugged mountain vale in southwestern Loch Modan overrun by hostile troggs. Once a pristine alpine hollow, it has transformed into a fortified encampment under the brute command of the trogg chieftain Grawmug. Tucked away among the craggy slopes of southwestern Loch Modan, Stonesplinter Valley was once a quiet alpine hollow. That serenity ended when waves of subterranean troggs clawed their way to the surface across Khaz Modan. Claiming the valley for their own, the Stonesplinter tribe rapidly turned the rocky defiles into crude fortifications, digging dens, erecting barricades, and hunting anything that strays too close. Their numbers make the valley an open wound on roads through southern Loch Modan, forcing Mountaineers out of Thelsamar to hire adventurous mercenaries willing to cull their ranks and eliminate their towering warlord, Grawmug.

subzone:stonetalon-peak.text: Stonetalon Peak. Stonetalon Peak is an ancient night elven sanctuary tucked into a verdant alpine valley at the northwestern edge of the Stonetalon Mountains. Sacred to the kaldorei and cared for by local druids, it serves as the primary bastion of the Alliance in these craggy heights. Perched high above the arid dust of the lower ranges, Stonetalon Peak opens into a lush, mist-shrouded sanctuary. Long considered sacred and steeped in ancient magic, the valley holds ruins dating back millennia to when the region housed temples honoring Queen Azshara before the Great Sundering. In the modern era, kaldorei Sentinels and druids have restored a measure of peaceful stewardship here, maintaining a tranquil refuge complete with a barrow den and a vital Alliance flight roost. Beyond its idyllic forests and ancient ruins, Stonetalon Peak holds historic weight from the Third War. Guided by the visions of Medivh, both Jaina Proudmoore's human expedition and Thrall's Horde scaled these perilous heights in search of the elusive Oracle dwelling within the mountain's deep caverns. That fateful encounter forced mortal enemies to set aside their blades, laying the foundation for the uneasy pact that stood against the Burning Legion at Mount Hyjal. Today, the peak remains firmly under Sentinel watch, though Horde incursions in the lowlands keep the defenders vigilant.

subzone:stonewatch.text: Stonewatch. Stonewatch is a fortified stronghold in central Redridge Mountains, built to defend the surrounding human lands from northern invasions. Formerly manned by Stormwind soldiers, the fortress has fallen under the brutal control of the Blackrock orcs, posing an immediate threat to nearby Lakeshire. Positioned over the cliffs near Stonewatch Falls, Stonewatch comprises a heavily built tower and keep designed to guard the approaches from the Burning Steppes. Originally held by Lakeshire's defenders, the fortification fell when the rogue warlock Morganth forged an alliance with the Blackrock clan. Infused with dark magic, the invading orcs overwhelmed the local human garrison—the 12th Sabre Regiment—and claimed the fortress. Although Morganth eventually turned on his allies and withdrew to the nearby Tower of Ilgalar with an army of Shadowhide gnolls, the Blackrock orcs retained a stranglehold over the keep under the command of Warlord Gath'Ilzogg and Lieutenant Tharil'zun. With Stonewatch firmly garrisoned by hostile orcs, Lakeshire sits directly in the crosshairs of an impending conquest. Cut off from substantial military reinforcements by an indifferent or paralyzed Stormwind House of Nobles, Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris have been forced to hire mercenary aid and volunteers. Decapitating the fortress's leadership—targeting both Tharil'zun and Gath'Ilzogg—remains the town's desperate primary hope for relieving the siege on the region.

subzone:stonewatch-falls.text: Stonewatch Falls. Stonewatch Falls is a scenic waterfall and deep mountain pool situated in the eastern reaches of the Redridge Mountains, fed by the outflow of Lake Everstill. Cascading down the hillside beneath the looming heights of Stonewatch, its isolated waters are claimed by a hostile tribe of murlocs. Pouring from the eastern river of Lake Everstill, Stonewatch Falls cascades down the rugged terrain beneath the Blackrock orc stronghold of Stonewatch. The plunging water carves out a deep pool tucked against the mountainside. Despite its natural beauty, travelers rarely linger to admire the view; a vicious band of murlocs infests the pool, building crude reed hovels and preying upon any foolish enough to trespass along the water's edge.

subzone:stonewatch-keep.text: Stonewatch Keep. Stonewatch Keep is a fortified stone stronghold looming in eastern Redridge Mountains, once built and manned by the Kingdom of Stormwind. It has fallen to an invading host of Blackrock orcs, serving as the forward operational base from which their warlords terrorize Lakeshire. Stonewatch Keep originally defended the eastern ridges and guarded the settlers of Lakeshire against hostile incursions. That peace shattered when the renegade warlock Morganth struck an alliance with the Blackrock clan. Bolstered by dark magic, the orcs stormed the fortress with vicious ferocity, overwhelming the human defenders and taking the keep for themselves. Although Morganth later abandoned his allies to raise the nearby Tower of Ilgalar and subjugate local gnolls, the Blackrock invaders successfully consolidated their grip over Stonewatch, transforming a former bastion of the Alliance into a fortified staging ground for their assault on the valley. Now occupied by a heavy garrison of Blackrock warriors, the keep is overseen by the formidable orcish warlord Gath'Ilzogg and his brutal lieutenant, Tharil'zun. From the stone ramparts, these commanders coordinate raids across Redridge, taking prisoners such as Stormwind's Corporal Keeshan. With the kingdom's military spread thin and unable to dispatch a full regiment to liberate the fortress, Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris have been forced to hire mercenary champions to infiltrate the stronghold and execute the Blackrock leadership before Lakeshire is completely overrun.

subzone:stonewatch-tower.text: Stonewatch Tower. Stonewatch Tower is a stone guard tower standing within the overrun stronghold of Stonewatch in northeastern Redridge. Once maintained by the defenders of Lakeshire, the outpost was captured by the Blackrock clan to monitor the surrounding ridges and secure their mountain bastion. Built by the Kingdom of Stormwind to guard the high mountain passes above Lake Everstill, Stonewatch Tower served as the forward scouting sibling to Stonewatch Keep. From its elevated vantage point, sentries could easily watch the eastern ridges and alert Lakeshire to any threats advancing from the Burning Steppes. That early warning network collapsed when Warlord Gath'Ilzogg's Blackrock orcs swept down from the heights, overrunning the human defenders and claiming the stronghold for their own war effort. Today, the tower bristles with Blackrock sentinels, ensuring no Alliance scouts approach the fortress undetected.

subzone:stonewrought-dam.text: Stonewrought Dam. The Stonewrought Dam is a colossal dwarven engineering marvel standing along the northern rim of Loch Modan. It holds back the waters of the Loch, creating the massive highland lake while draining the Wetlands below into habitable marshes. Stretching across the canyon east of Dun Algaz, the Stonewrought Dam is widely regarded as one of the great structural triumphs of dwarven civilization. Designed by the master Dark Iron architect Franclorn Forgewright, the barrier was built using his pioneering stonewrought technique. By trapping the waters of the mountain basin, the dam doubled the surface area of the Loch while steadily lowering water levels to the north, allowing the marshy basin of the Wetlands to emerge from a once completely flooded valley. Though built under the guidance of a Dark Iron architect, the dam today serves Ironforge—and has become a prime target for Dark Iron saboteurs operating out of the southern mountains. Recent assaults and infiltration attempts have forced Ironforge to station a garrison here under Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Guards and engineers patrol the masonry day and night, knowing that any breach would catastrophically drain the Loch and unleash a devastating deluge across the Wetlands below.

subzone:stormwind-gate.text: Stormwind Gate. At Stormwind Gate, sentries watch the road between Elwynn Forest and Stormwind City. The passage opens onto the Valley of Heroes, where the city’s stone monuments rise beyond the arch. Stormwind Gate guards the southern road from Elwynn Forest into the capital. The Stormwind City Guard watches from the stone portal, while patrols move between the outer arch and the Valley of Heroes. Unrest lingers in Elwynn, yet the massive iron and stone gates stay open. Travelers, merchants, and returning defenders pass through into the heart of the Alliance.

subzone:stormwind-keep.text: Stormwind Keep. Stormwind Keep stands high above the capital as the stone fortress and seat of power for the Kingdom of Stormwind. Rebuilt after its ruin in the First War, it currently houses the royal court of the young boy-king Anduin Wrynn and his regent, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Perched upon a plateau overlooking the entire city, Stormwind Keep serves as both a palace and a military bastion. The original stronghold was burned to the ground by the Old Horde when King Llane was assassinated near the end of the First War. Raised anew upon the old foundations after the Alliance reclaimed the kingdom, the reconstructed keep houses not only the grand throne room and the War Room, but peaceful garden courtyards and the expansive Royal Library.

subzone:stormwind-stockade.text: Stormwind Stockade. Stormwind Stockade holds the city’s most dangerous prisoners beneath the canals near the Mage Quarter. A coordinated revolt has driven the guards from the lower cells, leaving the prison in chaos. Warden Thelwater oversees the Stockade, where Stormwind keeps cutthroats, Defias operatives, captured Blackrock orcs, and Dark Iron dwarves. Now a violent uprising led by the Defias conspirator Bazil Thredd has forced the guards from the lower cells. The prisoners roam freely through the corridors. Thelwater has managed to secure the entrance, but the revolt still threatens to reach the canals. He depends on adventurers to enter the prison and put down the uprising.

subzone:stormwind-stockade-classic.text: Stormwind Stockade (Classic). Prisoners now control the Stormwind Stockade beneath Stormwind City's canal district. A revolt has driven the guards from its halls. The Stockade lies off the canals between Old Town and the Mage Quarter, holding Stormwind's most dangerous prisoners. Warden Thelwater oversees the underground prison. Its inmates include Defias Brotherhood cutthroats, a Blackrock orc, an ogre, and a Dark Iron dwarf. Bazil Thredd recently led a coordinated riot that overwhelmed the garrison. The surviving guards fled, leaving the prisoners in control of the halls.

subzone:stoutlager-inn.text: Stoutlager Inn. The Stoutlager Inn is the lively heart of Thelsamar and a primary haven for travelers in Loch Modan. Tucked beneath the rolling hills of the loch, it offers warm hearths, strong dwarven ale, and a bustling gathering place for adventurers and locals alike. Situated squarely in the settlement of Thelsamar, the Stoutlager Inn serves as the center of community life for western Loch Modan. Miners, mountaineers, and wayfarers passing between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands stop here to trade rumors, secure lodging, and share hearty drafts of dwarven brew. While the wilderness beyond Thelsamar grows increasingly hostile with trogg and kobold activity, the thick stone walls and roaring fires of the Stoutlager provide a dependable sanctuary.

subzone:strahnbrad.text: Strahnbrad. Strahnbrad is a ruined human settlement nestled in the northeastern heights of the Alterac Mountains, near the border of the Western Plaguelands. Once famous as the site of Prince Arthas Menethil's early defense against Blackrock orc raiders, the town has since fallen into decay and serves as a fortified stronghold for the criminal Syndicate. Originally a holding of the Kingdom of Alterac before being absorbed into Lordaeron following the Second War, Strahnbrad's misfortune began on the eve of the Third War. Blackrock clan orcs raided the settlement to take human sacrifices for the Burning Legion, leading Prince Arthas Menethil and the Knights of the Silver Hand to ride to its defense. Though Arthas drove the raiders away and slew their slave master, the town was heavily bloodied. When Lordaeron crumbled beneath the Scourge shortly thereafter, Strahnbrad was abandoned to the elements. Today, Strahnbrad has become a crucial operations hub for the Syndicate, the organization of displaced Alteraci nobility and outlaws plotting to reclaim their fallen realm. Patrolled by human rogues and brigands, its abandoned town hall and blacksmith now serve as hideouts and staging grounds. The Syndicate uses the ruined town to house supplies and captive labor, including unfortunate prisoners like the orc Gol'dir, whom Horde scouts from Tarren Mill actively seek to liberate.

subzone:sun-rock-retreat.text: Sun Rock Retreat. Sun Rock Retreat is a hidden Horde sanctuary nestled high within the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains, just south of Mirkfallon Lake. Dominated by tauren and orcish forces, it serves as the Horde's primary staging ground and supply post in the region. Beyond its strategic utility, the settlement rests upon sacred ground long revered by the tauren for its deep spiritual resonance. Tucked away in a mountain basin south of Mirkfallon Lake, Sun Rock Retreat has long held spiritual importance for the tauren. According to ancient tradition, An'she, the Sun, kissed the very mountain peak where the village stands. For generations before the Horde's arrival, tauren shamans and pilgrims journeyed here to perform rituals bridging the mortal veil, drawing strength from the land's strong bond to the spirit world. Today, Sun Rock Retreat serves as the Horde's principal base of operations across the Stonetalon Mountains. Orcs and tauren work side by side to establish a secure foothold against hostile harpy broods, local night elf sentinels, and the industrial pillaging of the Venture Company. As a central hub connecting trade and flight routes between Thunder Bluff, the Crossroads, and the borders of Ashenvale, the retreat provides shelter, provisions, and spiritual guidance to those braving the crags.

subzone:talondeep-path.text: Talondeep Path. Talondeep Path is a winding underground tunnel boring through the mountain ridge between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains. Devoid of hostile creatures or travelers, it serves as a tranquil, natural subterranean passage connecting Mystral Lake to Windshear Crag. Hidden beneath the rugged ridgeline separating Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains lies Talondeep Path, a quiet subterranean route. The passage links the forests just west of Mystral Lake directly to the northwestern reaches of Windshear Crag. Unlike the dangerous surface trails haunted by predators and warring factions, the tunnel interior remains eerily calm, free of hostile beasts or encampments, though riddled with twisting side pockets, crevices, and natural alcoves in the rock. Above ground, faint remnants of an ancient surface road still linger, hinting that travelers once scaled the high peaks before this sheltered cave became the preferred route through the stone.

subzone:talondeep-vale.text: Talondeep Vale. Talondeep Vale is a quiet, forested hollow nestled in south-central Ashenvale. Bordering Silverwind Refuge, the Ruins of Stardust, and the gateway to the Stonetalon Mountains, it acts as a peaceful canopy through which travelers navigate southern Kalimdor. Tucked away beneath the dense canopy of south-central Ashenvale, Talondeep Vale serves as a crossroads between several landmark sites. It is framed by Silverwind Refuge to the east, the haunting Ruins of Stardust nearby, and the rugged rise leading up into the Stonetalon Mountains. Shaded by ancient trees, the valley remains an untamed tract of woodland through which night elf wardens, sentinels, and passing wanderers traverse as they move between the heart of the forest and the high crags beyond.

subzone:tarren-mill.text: Tarren Mill. Tarren Mill is a beleaguered Forsaken outpost nestled in the northern reaches of the Hillsbrad Foothills beneath the Alterac Mountains. Once a peaceful human farming village, it now serves as the primary bastion of the Horde in Hillsbrad, locked in constant conflict with the Alliance town of Southshore to the south. Before the Third War, Tarren Mill was a thriving agricultural township loyal to the Kingdom of Lordaeron. During the Second War, it earned renown when Alliance forces rescued captured high elven archers from nearby orc encampments, securing Quel'Thalas's full commitment to the Alliance of Lordaeron. Today, however, the town's original living inhabitants are gone, replaced by the Forsaken. The town's architecture stands weathered and decayed, its fields barren, and its old mill silent as the new undead occupants fortify the settlement against constant threats from mountain beasts, Syndicate outlaws, and Alliance skirmishers. Tarren Mill functions as the Horde's vital forward operations base in the region. Directly opposed to the Alliance port of Southshore, the road between the two settlements has devolved into an open warzone. Horde travelers use Tarren Mill to push back against the human farmers and soldiers occupying Hillsbrad, coordinate strikes against dwarven excavators at Dun Garok, and secure the treacherous roads leading up into the snowy crags of the Alterac Mountains.

subzone:temple-gardens.text: Temple Gardens. The Temple Gardens form the tranquil, water-filled heart of Darnassus, surrounding small islets just north of the Temple of the Moon. Decorated with bridges and pristine flora, the district hosts the city bank and the mystical tree portal leading to the base of Teldrassil. Spanning the waters at the center of Darnassus, the Temple Gardens serve as the crossroads of the night elven capital. Wooden bridges connect its landscaped islets to the Cenarion Enclave in the north, the bustling terraces to the east, and the grand sanctuary of the Temple of the Moon to the south. The night elves carefully shape the district's flowing waters and lush foliage, creating a serene atmosphere that offers rest to travelers and priestesses alike. Beyond housing the city's central vault and bank on its main island, the Temple Gardens hold critical importance for travelers entering or leaving the World Tree. On the western bank of the gardens stands a massive, glowing pink tree portal. This magical archway provides instantaneous passage down through the boughs to Rut'theran Village at Teldrassil's base, connecting the isolated boughs to the coastal docks and flight paths.

subzone:temple-of-the-moon.text: Temple of the Moon. The Temple of the Moon stands in Darnassus as the spiritual heart of the night elven people and the seat of government on Teldrassil. Presided over by High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, the sanctuary serves as the headquarters for the Sisterhood of Elune. Its towering marble tiers house a sacred moonwell whose blessed waters bring healing and communion with the Moon Goddess. Erected shortly after the Third War when the night elves settled Teldrassil, the Temple of the Moon is among the largest stone structures constructed by modern kaldorei hands. Much of its marble was quarried from the Kalimdor mainland and transported across the sea through magical means. At the center of its interior lies an expansive moonwell overseen by the statue of Haidene, where consecrated waters radiate quiet power. Beyond serving as a place of worship and quiet reflection for pilgrims, the temple functions as the political apex of Darnassus, housing High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind as she guides her people through the dawn of a uncertain new age. Within the temple's quiet terraces, the priestesses of the Sisterhood of Elune carry out the goddess's will both spiritually and tactically. From here, emissaries and dispatched sisters are sent outward across northern Kalimdor to investigate threats or offer aid to local sentinels, such as Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde's inquiries along the Darkshore coastline. Novices and veteran priestesses alike gather beneath the starry vaulted ceiling to train in divine spellwork, tend to the wounded, and guard the sanctum from outside corruption.

subzone:the-loch.text: The Loch. The Loch is the vast freshwater lake that dominates the valley of Loch Modan. Held back by the monumental Stonewrought Dam, it is the largest body of water on Khaz Modan and the lifeblood of the surrounding dwarven settlements. Spanning the center of Loch Modan, The Loch is among the largest inland lakes in the known world, rivaled only by Lordamere Lake and Darrowmere Lake in the north. Its waters support local fishermen and provide a peaceful backdrop for the town of Thelsamar and nearby hunting lodges. Beneath its calm surface, however, prowl aggressive threshadons and freshwater beasts that make swimming across a perilous venture. The Loch exists in its current tranquil state thanks to masterwork dwarven engineering. To the north stands the massive Stonewrought Dam, an architectural marvel built across the mountain cleft to prevent the lake from flooding out into the Wetlands below. Maintaining this colossal structure is essential to preserving the valley's ecosystem and keeping Khaz Modan secure.

subzone:thelsamar.text: Thelsamar. Thelsamar is the primary dwarven settlement in Loch Modan, nestled on the western bluffs overlooking the great lake. Positioned along the main road between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands, it serves as a bustling hub of commerce, hospitality, and civic defense against surrounding trogg and ogre incursions. Thelsamar serves as the central bastion of dwarven civilian life in the valley. Built with traditional Khaz Modan stone and timber architecture, it features the lively Stoutlager Inn, a dedicated gryphon roost, crafting stations, and various supply merchants. Sitting directly on the thoroughfare connecting the South Gate Pass into Dun Morogh with the Algaz Pass toward the Wetlands, almost all travelers through the region pass beneath its warm hearths and stout roofs. Despite its cozy comforts, Thelsamar is in constant danger. To the south, troggs pouring from Stonesplinter Valley threaten the town's perimeter, while bears and predatory beasts haunt Grizzlepaw Ridge. With Ironforge's regular military forces stretched thin across the realm, the local magistrate and Mountaineers rely heavily on traveling adventurers and mercenaries to patrol the trade roads and beat back encroaching hostiles.

subzone:thistlefur-hold.text: Thistlefur Hold. Thistlefur Hold is a cavernous den carved into northern Thistlefur Village in west-central Ashenvale. Once peaceful bears of the forest, the Thistlefur furbolgs residing here have succumbed to corruption and turn violent toward any outsider who draws near. Tucked into the northern reaches of Thistlefur Village, Thistlefur Hold serves as the heart of the Thistlefur tribe's territory. The furbolgs here have been driven mad by corruption, falling into a state of feral hostility that makes them dangerous to travelers and neighbors alike. Deep within the winding caverns, the tribe hordes scavenged relics—including troll charms of interest to the Darkspear—and keeps captives bound in wooden cages, such as the imprisoned tauren brave Ruul Snowhoof.

subzone:thistlefur-village.text: Thistlefur Village. Thistlefur Village is a sprawling settlement tucked into the forest north of Astranaar in west-central Ashenvale. It serves as the primary home of the Thistlefur furbolg tribe, who have fallen prey to dark corruption and violently assault any outsiders venturing near their dens. Situated just north of the night elf haven of Astranaar, Thistlefur Village was once part of the peaceful woodland communities native to Ashenvale. However, the malignant corruption that has seeped into the ancient forests has entirely claimed the Thistlefur tribe. Now thoroughly maddened and intensely hostile, the furbolgs fiercely guard the paths winding through their settlement. The clan answers to two exceptionally ferocious chieftains, Dal Bloodclaw and Rorgish Jowl, whose unyielding aggression poses a constant threat to travelers and nearby settlements.

subzone:thistlefuzz-arcanery.text: Thistlefuzz Arcanery. Thistlefuzz Arcanery is a prominent workshop and academy of the magical arts located east of the Great Forge in Ironforge. Run primarily by gnome practitioners, it serves as the capital's premier haven for enchanters and scholars seeking to weave magic into metal and parchment. Its busy chambers hum with arcane energy right alongside the roaring fires of dwarven industry. Tucked directly east of the thundering Great Forge, Thistlefuzz Arcanery offers a stark contrast to the clanging anvils of dwarven smiths. Within its two levels, scholars, practitioners, and apprentices gather to master the subtle disciplines of enchanting and magical study. While the Ironforge dwarves prefer to reshape steel through muscle and fire, the gnomes of the Arcanery demonstrate how raw arcane energy can be bound directly into weaponry, armor, and curious tools. It stands as an essential sanctuary for spellcasters navigating the mountain stronghold.

subzone:three-corners.text: Three Corners. Three Corners is a vital crossroads nestled just inside the western border of the Redridge Mountains. Branching toward the three neighboring towns of Goldshire, Lakeshire, and Darkshire, it marks the boundary between the heart of the kingdom and Redridge's perilous wilderness. A Stormwind Guard watchtower stands over the intersection, holding the line against encroaching gnoll packs. Situated at the western edge of the Redridge Mountains, Three Corners connects three key Alliance settlements: Goldshire in Elwynn Forest to the west, Lakeshire to the northeast, and Darkshire in Duskwood to the south. Because of this strategic junction, Stormwind erected Tower Watch at the center of the crossroads. Manning the post, local guards and scouts attempt to keep the thoroughfares clear of Redridge's aggressive gnolls, who constantly threaten travelers and supply wagons passing between the regions.

subzone:thunder-falls.text: Thunder Falls. Thunder Falls lies in Elwynn Forest’s northwestern heights, where bandits have taken a riverside cottage. Thunder Falls cuts through the ridges above Mirror Lake, where a mountain stream rushes between steep cliffs. It enters over an unreachable cascade in the north, then spills away in waterfalls on both sides. One fall empties into Mirror Lake; the stream’s downstream course runs west toward Westfall’s rugged border. A cottage, dock, and outdoor forge sit beside the water. Bandits now claim the clearing.

subzone:thunderbrew-distillery.text: Thunderbrew Distillery. Thunderbrew Distillery serves as the bustling tavern and central gathering place of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Renowned far and wide for its potent ales, it functions as both an active brewhouse and an essential rest stop for travelers passing through the snowy mountain passes. Inside, patrons find warm hearths, cold pints, and a wide array of class mentors and local tradesfolk. Perched in the center of Kharanos, the Thunderbrew Distillery is the heart of civic life in southern Dun Morogh. Founded by the Thunderbrew clan—established by Arkilus Thunderbrew and maintained by his kin—the brewhouse is famous across Khaz Modan for producing robust, warming ales built to ward off the biting mountain chill. It operates as the local inn, managed on the floor by Innkeeper Belm, offering weary mountaineers a roaring fire, hearty fare, and beds to escape the blizzards outside. Beyond pouring renowned stouts, the distillery doubles as a vital hub for developing adventurers. Because Kharanos is the first major settlement travelers reach after departing Coldridge Valley, the Thunderbrew tavern plays host to diverse trainers. Mentors in martial arts, holy rites, arcane studies, and roguecraft congregate under its sturdy timber rafters alongside instructors in cooking and emergency medical aid, turning a boisterous drinking hall into an indispensable preparation post.

subzone:tinker-town.text: Tinker Town. Tinker Town is the bustling gnomish quarter nestled within the subterranean dwarven city of Ironforge. Established to shelter refugees following the tragic fall of Gnomeregan, the district serves as the seat of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque's government-in-exile and the primary terminus for the Deeprun Tram. When subterranean troggs overran the high-tech city of Gnomeregan, the dwarven hosts of Ironforge opened their gates to the survivors. To accommodate the sudden influx of refugees, a cavernous district—previously home to dwarven residents and the entrance to the Deeprun Tram—was set aside for them. Under the watchful eye of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his council, Tinker Town quickly became an energetic hub of whirring gears, experimental alchemy, and gadgetry. Despite being cramped guests in a stone city, the gnomes have rebuilt a semblance of their civilization around a massive spherical contraption, determined to reclaim their subterranean homeland. Beyond housing the gnomish leadership, Tinker Town is one of the most strategically significant transit hubs on the continent. The district hosts the Ironforge entrance to the Deeprun Tram, an engineering wonder that swiftly links the dwarven capital to Stormwind.

subzone:tinkers-court.text: Tinkers' Court. Tinkers' Court is the grand council chamber at the heart of Gnomeregan. Once the bustling seat of the High Tinker and his ruling council, it is now the grim stronghold of the traitor Mekgineer Thermaplugg. Before the disaster that ruined Gnomeregan, the Tinkers' Court served as the civic and political heart of the nation. It was here that High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque gathered with advisors and master inventors, including Tinkmaster Overspark, to debate technological advancements, govern civic matters, and guide gnomish society. The court represented the pinnacle of gnomish ingenuity and governance, situated just beyond the industrial works of the Engineering Labs and the Launch Bay.

subzone:tower-of-althalaxx.text: Tower of Althalaxx. The Tower of Althalaxx is an ancient Highborne spire standing in northern Darkshore near the coast. Once an isolated retreat for the sorcerer Athrikus Narassin before the Great Sundering, it has become infested by demonic cultists and warlocks practicing dark arts. Ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne servants in the coastal towns of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, placing the powerful sorcerer Athrikus Narassin in authority over them. Growing distant from civic governance, Athrikus chose to isolate himself within the nearby Tower of Althalaxx. When the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, the tower endured along the desolate coastline of Darkshore, standing as a quiet ruin of forgotten elven magics.

subzone:tower-of-azora.text: Tower of Azora. At the Tower of Azora, Archmage Theocritus leads a scholarly outpost in eastern Elwynn Forest. The slender spire stands north of the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, where its human master keeps watch over a silent magical feud with a hostile tower in the Redridge Mountains. The Tower of Azora stands beside the eastern road to the Redridge Mountains, staffed almost entirely by gnome spellcasters. Archmage Theocritus guides their studies of strange curiosities and teaches wandering spellweavers. A wild magical aura surrounds the spire and sometimes warps nearby wildlife. Within the tower, gnome servants contend with enchanted household items and mutated insects that creep past the doorway.

subzone:tower-of-ilgalar.text: Tower of Ilgalar. The Tower of Ilgalar is an isolated spire perched high in the crags of the eastern Redridge Mountains. Once a wizard's retreat, it has fallen into shadow as the hideout of Morganth, a banished sorcerer from Stormwind who now commands the region's feral gnolls and practices dark magic. Looming over eastern Redridge, the Tower of Ilgalar serves as the personal sanctum of Morganth. Cast out from the Mage Quarter of Stormwind for dabbling in forbidden magic, the rogue sorcerer retreated into these rugged heights to delve deeper into the dark arts without imperial interference. Rather than living in solitude, Morganth asserted dominion over the local Shadowhide gnoll clan, employing them as savage sentries around the base of the spire. Inside, the tower crawls with conjured demonic hounds and crackles with shadowy power, posing a constant, brooding menace to the beleaguered town of Lakeshire below. Scholars often draw parallels between the Tower of Ilgalar and the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest. While the true identity of Ilgalar remains shrouded in mystery, the two towers stand in quiet, magical opposition. In Elwynn, the archmage Theocritus maintains careful watch over Ilgalar through enchanted scrying devices like the Eye of Azora, monitoring Morganth's sinister experiments and plotting to neutralize the renegade before his corruption spreads further through the kingdom.

subzone:trade-district.text: Trade District. Past the Valley of Heroes, Trade District draws Stormwind’s merchants and travelers. Its bank, Auction House, guild registry, and shops serve citizens and adventurers alike. You pass beneath the stone arches from the Valley of Heroes into Trade District. The open plaza is Stormwind’s main marketplace and a hub for goods and travel. The Auction House stands at its center, with the Stormwind Counting House, the city’s main bank, and The Gilded Rose nearby. From here, routes lead to Old Town, the Cathedral Square, and the Mage Quarter. Coin, raw goods, and supplies for adventurers pass through the district on their way across the realm. Shops line the paved avenues and canals, offering goods for daily needs and travel. Weller’s Arsenal and Lionheart Armory sell blades and mail, while The Empty Quiver offers bows. Stalls sell fresh flowers and aged vintages from the Gallina Winery. Just inside the gates, the Stormwind Visitor’s Center handles newly registered guild charters and tabard designs. On the eastern side, an elevated ramp leads to the Gryphon Roost, connecting Stormwind’s markets with Alliance territories.

subzone:tradesmen-s-terrace.text: Tradesmen's Terrace. Tradesmen's Terrace is the bustling commercial heart of Darnassus, situated along the city's southern flank. It brings together craftspeople, merchants, and the local auction house beneath the sweeping wooden architecture of the night elf capital. The terrace serves as the primary trade link connecting artisans with adventurers journeying across Teldrassil and beyond. Occupying the southern stretch of Darnassus, Tradesmen's Terrace houses the capital's mercantile life. While much of the city is devoted to quiet contemplation, wilderness sanctuaries, and spiritual duties, this terrace brings together shopkeepers, tradespeople, and merchants serving both local kaldorei and travelers from the wider Alliance. It contains Darnassus's central auction house, general provisions, and crafting supply stores, making it the essential staging ground for journeys into the wilds. Broad footpaths connect it northward directly to the Warrior's Terrace and westward toward the serene waters of the Temple Gardens and the grand Temple of the Moon. Kaldorei crafts prioritize harmony with nature, and the shops here reflect that delicate balance. Even amidst everyday commerce, the terrace operates without the roaring furnaces or smog seen in dwarven or human workshops, favoring quiet stone, curated timber, and woven goods. For visiting adventurers seeking trade contracts, repairs, or materials gathered from Teldrassil's dense boughs, the terrace stands as the principal center of business in northern Kalimdor.

subzone:train-depot.text: Train Depot. The Train Depot is a subterranean transit hub located just below the surface entrances of Gnomeregan in Dun Morogh. Once a bustling center of gnomish locomotion, it now swarms with hostile leper gnomes and invading troggs. Situated at the bottom of the grand elevator leading down from Dun Morogh, the Train Depot once served as the primary nexus for rail transport across the subterranean marvel of Gnomeregan. Today, the platforms and railbeds lie in shambles. The fallout that irradiated the city transformed its remaining workers into crazed leper gnomes, while subterranean troggs have overrun the tracks. Explorers descending into the ruined city must navigate this staging ground to reach deeper sectors such as Clockwerk Run, the Loading Room, and the inner engineering facilities.

subzone:tranquil-gardens-cemetery.text: Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Tranquil Gardens Cemetery sits just southeast of Darkshire in Duskwood. Despite its peaceful name, the grounds have become overrun with shambling skeletons and ghouls, turning the former burial site into an immediate hazard for the nearby town. Once a quiet resting place for the departed of Grand Hamlet, Tranquil Gardens Cemetery is now anything but serene. As dark curses settled over Duskwood, the dead buried here began clawing their way out of their plots. While the skeletal warriors, skeletal mages, and wandering undead haunting these gravestones are relatively weak compared to the horrors lurking deeper in the woods, their close proximity to Darkshire poses a relentless threat to the townsfolk. Because the cemetery lies so close to Darkshire's edge, it serves as the frontline for the local militia. The Night Watch frequently sends fresh recruits and arriving adventurers here to cull the rising dead before they breach the settlement. Among the tumbled headstones and the ruined chapel, more dangerous threats such as the Insane Ghoul lurk.

subzone:tundrid-hills.text: Tundrid Hills. The Tundrid Hills are a rugged, snowbound stretch of highland in south-central Dun Morogh, lying just west of the Gol'Bolar Quarry. Inhabited by dangerous mountain wildlife, the rocky passes are rarely traversed by casual travelers. Stretching between Coldridge Valley and the lowlands of eastern Dun Morogh, the Tundrid Hills offer a rugged cross-country route for those looking to bypass the main roads through Kharanos. However, convenience comes at a steep price. The jagged snowy slopes are prowled by ferocious predators, making the territory perilous for unwary travelers who venture off the beaten path without a drawn weapon.

subzone:twilight-grove.text: Twilight Grove. Tucked away in the center of Duskwood, the Twilight Grove is a stunning enclave of lush Kalimdor flora contrasting the grim, blighted forest around it. Beneath its towering great tree and ancient night elf architecture sits a moonwell and a massive emerald gateway connected directly to the Emerald Dream. Hidden behind steep crater ridges in the heart of Duskwood, the Twilight Grove looks utterly alien to the Eastern Kingdoms. Ancient night elf gazebos, vibrant green meadows, and a serene moonwell frame an unnamed great tree that towers over the gloomy canopy. The tree stands as a conduit of nature, filtering the raw vigor of the Emerald Dream into the waking world and allowing this crater to thrive even beneath the eternal gloom of Duskwood. At the base of the great tree looms a massive stone portal, one of four known gateways across Azeroth linking the physical realm directly to the Emerald Dream. While traditionally watched over by Ysera's green dragonflight, dark whispers claim that malevolent forces have begun twisting the tranquil realm beyond. The gateway stands largely silent for now, but its emerald swirl serves as a grim reminder that cosmic corruption can spill forth into Duskwood from paths far deeper than the Scourge or the local worgen.

subzone:twilight-shore-darkshore.text: Twilight Shore (Darkshore). The Twilight Shore is a rugged stretch of coast in southern Darkshore, running south from the Long Wash down to the border of Ashenvale. Its gloomy, mist-laden beaches are interrupted by jutting sea cliffs, offshore islets, and treacherous surf. The area is infested with aggressive murloc tribes and ravenous aquatic predators like threshadons. Stretching south of the Long Wash past the ruins of Ameth'Aran toward Ashenvale, the Twilight Shore is among the most rugged and inhospitable parts of Darkshore's coastline. Gray sand gives way to sharp, wave-battered cliffs and scattered rocky islands. The waters here are notoriously hostile; swimming off the coast invites attacks from territorial threshadons and sea crawlers, while the beaches themselves are dominated by thriving camps of aggressive murlocs.

subzone:twilight-vale.text: Twilight Vale. Twilight Vale encompasses the dense, shadowed southern woodlands of Darkshore stretching toward the Ashenvale border. Beneath its gloom, corrupted furbolgs, rabid bears, and vicious nightsabers prowl the undergrowth, making off-road passage perilous. It serves as a grim threshold between the tainted coast of Darkshore and the sacred canopies to the south. Running from the south of the ancient ruins of Ameth'Aran all the way to the border of Ashenvale, the Twilight Vale blankets the southern reaches of Darkshore in perpetual dusk. The encroaching corruption plaguing northern Kalimdor has bitten deep into the wildlife here. Rabid bears roam alongside feral nightsabers, and hostile furbolg tribes stalk the dark wood. Sentinels and travelers alike advise sticking strictly to the main road, as straying even a few paces into the trees invites swift and deadly ambushes.

subzone:valley-of-heroes.text: Valley of Heroes. Stone statues watch over the Valley of Heroes, where Stormwind's southern road crosses the moat into the city. They honor the leaders of the Alliance Expedition to Draenor, and guards hold this fortified entrance. You cross the moat beneath statues honoring the commanders of the Alliance Expedition. Stormwind's rebuilding after the Second War raised these monuments along the causeway. The champions marched through the Dark Portal into Draenor to seal the rift forever, giving their lives so Azeroth might survive. As you head north toward the Trade District, you pass Archmage Khadgar, Kurdran Wildhammer, Ranger-Captain Alleria Windrunner, Force Commander Danath Trollbane, and High General Turalyon. General Marcus Jonathan watches Stormwind's gates from horseback, overseeing the guards and the traffic in and out. The valley is the city's main defense against an overland invasion. Major Mattingly, Field Marshal Stonebridge, and rows of seasoned guards keep watch beside him, guarding the capital from threats beyond its walls.

subzone:valley-of-kings.text: Valley of Kings. The Valley of Kings is a lush canyon nestled in the southwestern corner of Loch Modan, directly south of the passage to Dun Morogh. It serves as a heavily watched gateway into the fiery Searing Gorge, flanked by monumental stone figures carved in memory of the War of the Three Hammers. Travelers venturing here walk beneath ancient dwarven history while facing the immediate threat of Blackrock encroachers and troggs. The valley's most commanding feature is the pair of colossal statues depicting King Madoran Bronzebeard and High Thane Khardros Wildhammer. Carved by joint commission from their sons following their deaths, these stone titans overlook the pass into the scorched southlands. They stand as a lasting monument to the allied victory in the War of the Three Hammers and an eternal warning against the Dark Iron clan, reminding all who look south of the ruin brought upon the southlands by the summoning of Ragnaros. Beyond serving as a path between South Gate Pass and Stonesplinter Valley, the Valley of Kings holds the heavy iron gate leading down into the Searing Gorge. Because of the hostile Blackrock orcs, Dark Iron dwarves, and volcanic hazards lurking on the other side, the gate is kept strictly locked and guarded by Ironforge mountaineers. Mountaineer Pebblebitty keeps watch over the threshold, turning away all but the hardiest adventurers who can prove they possess the strength to survive the inferno beyond.

subzone:vault-of-ironforge.text: Vault of Ironforge. The Vault of Ironforge is the primary banking house and treasure repository for the dwarven capital. Situated in the bustling Commons directly opposite the Auction House, it serves as a central hub where citizens and travelers across the Alliance securely store their wealth. The vault's operations are overseen by Dinita and the esteemed Stonemantle family. Carved deep into the mountain rock of the Commons, the Vault of Ironforge stands as a symbol of dwarven fiscal security and craft. With the city's trade booming, travelers, soldiers, and merchants gather here daily to deposit coin, relics, and provisions under the vigilant eyes of city guards and tellers. Overseen by Dinita and the trusted Stonemantle family, the institution offers Alliance patrons absolute peace of mind.

subzone:vul-gol-ogre-mound.text: Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. Vul'Gol Ogre Mound is a sunken basin in southern Duskwood overrun by the Splinter Fist ogres under the brute Zzarc'Vul. Once a cluster of human homesteads, its ruined farmhouses and subterranean cavern are now littered with the carcasses and scavenged plunder of the clan. Tucked away in the shadows southwest of the fork heading toward Stranglethorn Vale, the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound serves as the seat of the Splinter Fist clan in Duskwood. The basin was once peaceful farmland, but its human inhabitants have long since fled or perished, leaving behind hollowed-out cabins now claimed by lumbering ogres and used as crude shelters. Inside the cavern beneath the rise, piles of slaughtered black bears attest to the clan's voracious appetite. Their chieftain, Zzarc'Vul, rules over the encampment, hoarding odd trinkets alongside mundane scavenged goods. Because the beleaguered Night Watch must stretch its thin ranks to guard Darkshire against rabid worgen and the restless dead, Commander Althea Ebonlocke and her militia rely on outside mercenaries to cull the Splinter Fist numbers before they push north. However, the ogres have made enemies beyond the town guard. They raided the recluse Abercrombie, stealing a crate of his alchemical tools, and attracted the attention of inquisitive mages seeking the arcane lenses that chieftain Zzarc'Vul is rumored to possess.

subzone:war-room.text: War Room. Deep inside Stormwind Keep, the War Room gathers the arms, records, and charts used to plan the Alliance’s defense. Beyond Stormwind Keep’s grand chambers, commanders turn to military logistics and high-level campaign planning. Swords, blunderbusses, and heavy artillery cannons line the stone walls. Military treatises and chronicles of past wars fill nearby tables. At the center, a large map lets commanders assess Alliance deployments across Azeroth, while the royal court handles affairs of state just steps away.

subzone:warrior-s-terrace.text: Warrior's Terrace. The Warrior's Terrace is the eastern district of Darnassus, acting as both a martial training hub and the capital's fortified gateway. Overlooking the road into greater Teldrassil, it houses the city's battlemasters, warrior trainers, and Sentinel patrols. Positioned at the eastern threshold of Darnassus, the Warrior's Terrace—sometimes referred to as the Hall of Justice—stands as the primary defensive bulwark against incursions from the Teldrassil wilds. Heavily armed Sentinels mounted on nightsabers guard its high arched gates, maintaining a vigilant watch over incoming travelers. Within its open-air plazas, aspiring combatants drill alongside seasoned veterans on extensive dueling grounds and target ranges. The district also serves practical military needs, hosting weapon smiths, armorers, and the battlemasters coordinating night elf forces across the wider world.

subzone:warsong-labor-camp.text: Warsong Labor Camp. The Warsong Labor Camp is an isolated Horde timber-harvesting outpost tucked away in southeastern Ashenvale. Operated by Warsong loggers and defended by orcish sentries, the work site cuts lumber to fuel the growth of Durotar while braving the hostility of the surrounding forest. Situated east of Fallen Sky Lake and southwest of the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, the Warsong Labor Camp exists for one vital purpose: harvesting the dense timber of Ashenvale. The dry plains of Durotar offer little usable lumber to build cities like Orgrimmar, forcing the Warsong clan to push deep into the contested woods. Staffed by hardy loggers and orcish guards, the site operates in relative isolation, grinding through ancient trees despite the ever-present threat of night elf scouts and passing Alliance warbands. Because of its remote location far from the main road and fortified bases like Splintertree Post, the camp is exceptionally vulnerable. Alliance raiders often strike the working peons and watchmen, knowing reinforcements will not arrive swiftly. To the night elves, every felled tree is an act of sacrilege, turning this mundane logging camp into a perennial flashpoint in the regional war.

subzone:warsong-lumber-camp.text: Warsong Lumber Camp. The Warsong Lumber Camp is a fortified orc logging operation deep in Ashenvale, run by the Warsong clan to harvest timber for the Horde. Anchored by the fortified Kargathia Keep, it stands as both an economic lifeline for nearby Horde settlements and an unrelenting provocation to the night elves. The constant sound of goblin-built shredders chewing through ancient boughs makes this clearing a primary flashpoint of the forest war. Carved straight out of the dense canopy of eastern Ashenvale, the Warsong Lumber Camp is the industrial engine fueling the Horde's expansion across Kalimdor. Orc peons and hired goblin engineers strip the forest with whirring shredders, processing towering trunks into lumber to reinforce outpost walls like nearby Splintertree Post and build up the fledgling nation of Durotar. The camp is heavily fortified against constant night elf counterattacks, centering on the stockades of Kargathia Keep and an active kennel for the clan's fierce war wolves. For the Warsong, every felled tree is survival and strength; for the native Sentinels, every saw blade is an act of sacrilege. The Warsong clan's presence in these woods dates back to the Third War, when Grom Hellscream first led his warriors into the sacred groves to claim wood for the Horde. That initial deforestation ignited the fury of the demigod Cenarius and brought down the ancient wrath of the night elves. Though the modern camp operates under the banners of Thrall's Horde, the old animosities burn just as fiercely. Surrounded by untamed timber, hostile elves, and the lingering demonic corruption around neighboring Felfire Hill, the camp's defenders remain armed around the clock, harvesting trees with axes in hand and ready to drop their timber to repel the next ambush.

subzone:weathered-nook.text: Weathered Nook. Tucked away along the northern cliffside of Thousand Needles, the Weathered Nook is a secluded cleft and shelter perched high above the canyon floor. Overlooking the vast sea of stone spires, it serves as a modest home and retreat for solitary tauren dwellers seeking quiet contemplation away from bustling settlements. Carved into the sheer sandstone wall north of Freewind Post, the Weathered Nook is easily missed by travelers passing along the canyon basin below. A natural ramp winds up the cliff face, leading to a sheltered ledge and cave out of the prevailing winds. Rather than housing a military outpost or large settlement, the nook serves as a humble homestead for solitary wanderers like Dorn Plainstalker and Prate Cloudseer, offering safety, seclusion, and a sweeping view across the windswept needle plateaus.

subzone:webwinder-path.text: Webwinder Path. Webwinder Path is a winding mountainous road in the Stonetalon Mountains connecting the troll outpost of Malaka'jin to Mirkfallon Lake. It cuts through rugged crags and dense highland woods inhabited by aggressive arachnids and native beasts. Running from the Horde settlement of Malaka'jin toward Mirkfallon Lake, Webwinder Path serves as one of the primary roadways carving through the lower Stonetalon Mountains. True to its name, the route is notorious for the thick cobwebs strung high among the canopy and jagged cliff sides. Travelers along this winding stretch must constantly watch their step, sharing the beaten path with prowling mountain spiders, aggressive thunder lizards, and territorial rams.

subzone:wellspring-lake.text: Wellspring Lake. Wellspring Lake is a serene body of fresh water resting high within the boughs of Teldrassil, situated northeast of Darnassus. Fed by natural springs originating from deep within the World Tree, its waters feed the winding Wellspring River. Once a peaceful retreat for night elf fishermen, the lake's shores have fallen prey to the growing corruption unsettling Teldrassil's wildlife. Nestled beneath the canopy between Darnassus and the Oracle Glade, Wellspring Lake was long cherished by the Kaldorei as a quiet haven for fishing and contemplation. Its clear waters originate from subterranean springs running through the colossal boughs of the World Tree, which then drain northward through the Wellspring River. In recent times, however, an insidious blight has begun to seize the surrounding wilds. Aggressive spiders, prowling nightsabers, and agitated timberlings now roam the banks, making what was once an idyllic pond a treacherous place for unwary travelers.

subzone:wellspring-river.text: Wellspring River. The Wellspring River flows from a natural spring within Teldrassil, coursing north out of Wellspring Lake until it plummets off the boughs in a towering waterfall to the ocean far below. Once a peaceful source of fresh water for the World Tree's ecosystem, its banks have grown perilous due to agitated local wildlife. Nourished by the deep natural springs nestled in the boughs of Teldrassil, the Wellspring River carries water north from Wellspring Lake across the verdant forest floor before cascading dramatically over the edge of the great tree down into the sea below. Despite the serene surroundings, the riverbanks are increasingly unsafe. The timberlings that dwell along the water have grown crazed and hostile, violently attacking travelers and druids who attempt to draw near the river's edge.

subzone:westbrook-garrison.text: Westbrook Garrison. At Westbrook Garrison, Deputy Rainer's few guards hold Elwynn's western road against gnolls and bandits. The outpost is short on soldiers and supplies, with danger rising near the Westfall border. Westbrook Garrison watches the road where Elwynn Forest thins toward Westfall. Deputy Rainer and a handful of guards patrol the western roads with too few soldiers to cover them. Much of the Stormwind Army serves abroad, while political indecision in the capital leaves the outpost without needed support. Thieves grow bolder, and Riverpaw gnolls have overrun the southern woods. Marshal Dughan in Goldshire has not sent formal reinforcements, so the guards depend on travelers to help secure the highway. Riverpaw gnolls gather south of Forest's Edge, where their raids threaten supply lines and homesteads. The packs follow Hogger, a fearsome chieftain whose forces outnumber the garrison and overwhelm its guards with brute strength. A high bounty is posted across the outpost, seeking fighters willing to enter the hills and bring down Hogger before the gnolls press farther east.

subzone:westfall-lighthouse.text: Westfall Lighthouse. Westfall Lighthouse watches over the rocky isle off Westfall's southwestern shore, its beacon dark and its keepers gone. Old Murk-Eye led the attack that killed them, and Captain Grayson's spirit remains by the tower. Westfall Lighthouse once guided ships along Westfall's dangerous southwestern bluffs and the coast near Stormwind. As law and order failed across the region, royal patrols dwindled and coastal dangers grew unchecked. Murloc tribes drove the lighthouse keepers inland. The family returned to relight the beacon, but Old Murk-Eye rallied his kin for another attack. The murlocs killed the keepers and put out the light.

subzone:whelgar-s-excavation-site.text: Whelgar's Excavation Site. Whelgar's Excavation Site is a dwarven archaeological dig in the western foothills of the Wetlands. Intended to unearth ancient Titan relics and prehistoric secrets, the expedition ended in disaster when vicious mottled raptors overran the quarry. The surviving excavators are now trapped on a ridge overlooking the dig, cut off from their findings. Spearheaded by dwarven prospectors searching for ancient fossils and earthen mysteries, the excavation carved out a massive quarry between Menethil Harbor and Dun Modr. However, unearthing prehistoric remnants drew the wrath of native mottled raptors. Overwhelmed and under-equipped, the archaeologists retreated to a ridge overlooking the dig site, leaving their tents, tools, and unearthed relics scattered among prowling predators.

subzone:whitereach-post.text: Whitereach Post. Whitereach Post is a small Horde encampment nestled along the dusty canyon path in Thousand Needles. Serving as a minor waystation near Camp E'thok, it offers respite and watchful eyes over the harsh desert highway. For travelers moving between Feralas and the salt flats, it stands as an outpost of Horde safety beneath the looming sandstone pillars. Perched along the beaten path winding through the depths of Thousand Needles, Whitereach Post is one of several modest Horde footholds carved out of the rugged landscape. Stationed in close proximity to Camp E'thok, the post helps maintain a reliable presence along the canyon floor, monitoring travel between the windswept mesas. While not as fortified as the great lift or major tribal settlements, it serves as an indispensable stop for couriers, scouts, and adventurers traversing the contested wastes.

subzone:wildbend-river.text: Wildbend River. Wildbend River is a tainted waterway winding through the southern forests of Darkshore near the Grove of the Ancients. Flowing down directly from the corrupted heights of Felwood, its waters carry demonic poison toward the sea, endangering the surrounding wilderness. Wildbend River cuts through the southern reaches of Darkshore, flowing westward past the sacred Grove of the Ancients before emptying into the sea. Rather than offering clean nourishment to the woodland, it brings corruption down from the mountains. The river is the direct continuation of Felwood's Bloodvenom River, tumbling through the rocky ridges and dragging foul, corrupted runoff into Darkshore's ecosystem. The night elves monitor its banks closely, watching for twisted wildlife and the creeping spread of demonic blight.

subzone:windshear-crag.text: Windshear Crag. Windshear Crag is a heavily despoiled valley in the central Stonetalon Mountains, stripped of its ancient timber by the Venture Company. Once a lush forest, the region is now an industrial wasteland dominated by whirring shredders, murky runoff, and aggressive logging crews. In the shadows of the machinery, local kobolds burrow for ore while mountain passes connect the scarred landscape to Ashenvale. Not long ago, Windshear Crag was a thick, old-growth woodland flanking the slopes of Stonetalon. That tranquil wilderness vanished when the Venture Company arrived in search of profit. Today, the basin is filled with severed stumps, acrid smog, and clanking machinery. The entire logging enterprise is overseen by Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, a leper gnome whose engineering genius produced the Super Reaper 6000—a mechanical terror capable of reducing massive trunks to kindling in moments. From an elevated platform above the polluted Cragpool Lake, Gerenzo directs an unchecked operation that strips the mountain bare, earning the hostility of rival engineers and local inhabitants alike. Beyond the active timberyards, Windshear Crag holds other hazards and crossroads. To the southeast lies Windshear Mine, where territorial kobolds dig through the rock for Smoky Iron Ingots, fiercely attacking anyone who nears their haul. In the crag's northeast reaches, travelers can find the Talondeep Path, an underground cavern tunnel threading straight beneath the ridges into Ashenvale. Stationed near this shadowed portal stands the tauren elder Braug Dimspirit, who tests the historical wisdom and resolve of Horde wayfarers venturing through the contested peaks.

subzone:xavian.text: Xavian. Xavian is an ancient ruined night elf temple complex in northeastern Ashenvale, now overrun and claimed by the satyrs. Serving as the primary seat of satyr influence in the forest, the ruin is foul with demonic corruption and dark rites directed against the woodland. Tucked away in the northeastern hills of Ashenvale, west of Forest Song and north of Satyrnaar, Xavian stands as the foremost bastion of satyr power in the region. Once a sacred elven temple, its stone arches and terraces have been desecrated by followers of the Burning Legion. Leaders among the satyrs, including Prince Raze and Geltharis, oversee their kin from these ruins. They perform defiling rituals across the grounds, even utilizing stolen Warsong oil to further blight the sacred woodland. The area takes its name from Xavius, the highborne councilor who became the first satyr during the War of the Ancients after failing Sargeras.

subzone:yorgen-farmstead.text: Yorgen Farmstead. The Yorgen Farmstead is a derelict farm nestled in southern Duskwood, fallen into ruin alongside the rest of the troubled region. Formerly owned by the farmer Sven Yorgen, the property has been seized and occupied by brigands of the Defias Brotherhood. Situated amidst the gloomy woodlands of southern Duskwood, the Yorgen Farmstead was once a functioning homestead belonging to Sven Yorgen. Like many isolated holdings in the region, the farm could not withstand the encroaching perils of the territory. Sven was forced to abandon his lands, retreating north to a makeshift camp along the Darkened Bank. In his absence, the abandoned grounds were claimed by outlaws looking for a foothold far from the gaze of Stormwind's authorities. Rather than lying vacant, the farmstead has been repurposed as a staging ground by the Defias Brotherhood. Masked highwaymen and stealthy cutthroats lurk among the decaying fences and weathered outbuildings, using the dense tree cover to conceal their presence. Travelers approaching the farmstead must tread carefully, as Defias assassins patrol the perimeter and ambush anyone trespassing on their newly seized sanctuary.

subzone:zoram-gar-outpost.text: Zoram'gar Outpost. Zoram'gar Outpost is a fortified Horde beachhead nestled on the western edge of Ashenvale along the Zoram Strand. Serving as a crucial coastal encampment, it provides the Horde with access to the Veiled Sea and keeps watch over regional threats like the encroaching naga and the sinister depths nearby. Situated at the northwestern lip of Ashenvale where the primeval forest collapses into the sea, Zoram'gar Outpost serves as the Horde's isolated coastal footing on the Zoram Strand. Hemmed in by night elf territory inland and maritime hazards offshore, the encampment acts as a staging ground for scouts, hunters, and shaman tasked with tracking local dangers. Life at the outpost is an endless vigil: naga regularly prowl the shallows, while lurking cultists and primal horrors pulse from the subterranean cavern system known as Blackfathom Deeps just down the shore. Because of its peripheral location, Zoram'gar maintains flight connections with other critical Horde holdings like Splintertree Post, the Crossroads, and Thunder Bluff. While small in footprint, the outpost anchors Horde supply lines on the western coast.

subzone:zoram-strand.text: Zoram Strand. The Zoram Strand is a windswept coastline lining the northwestern edge of Ashenvale along the Veiled Sea. Once the site of an ancient night elven city swallowed by the Great Sundering, the shore is now plagued by Wrathtail naga, shipwrecks, and beached leviathans. It also holds the entrance to the submerged temple complex of Blackfathom Deeps. Ten thousand years ago, the grand night elven city of Zoram graced these shores before the Great Sundering tore Kalimdor apart and cast the settlement into the ocean depths. Today, the tide continually washes up ancient relics, remnants of shattered vessels, and the carcasses of massive sea beasts. The Wrathtail naga have overrun the beaches and tidal pools, fiercely guarding the flooded ruins and ancient artifacts against anyone daring to approach. Despite the naga menace, both mainland travelers and coastal wanderers find themselves drawn to the strand. To the south lies the fortified Horde encampment of Zoram'gar Outpost, whose warriors fight a continuous battle to secure the coast. Deep within the nearby caverns sits Blackfathom Deeps, an ancient temple of Elune that has fallen into dark hands, making the strand a gathering ground for scouts, scholars, and treasure seekers braving the surf.
